summary: This paper argues that Stephen Kellert’s well-known claim in In the Wake of Chaos (1993)—that chaotic systems require impossible accuracy for useful prediction—applies only to one kind of task. Kellert focuses on predicting the precise value of a variable within a stated tolerance at a future time. Sensitive dependence on initial conditions, measured by a positive Lyapunov exponent, forces the required initial accuracy to grow exponentially, rendering many such point-value tasks impossible for any finite observer. The paper contends that a second, equally common task falls outside this impossibility: predicting whether the system will remain confined within a specified region over a given interval. This distinction is framed through the ideas of thin and thick chaos introduced in the author’s earlier work. Thin chaos involves local instability that never carries the system across the functional boundaries that matter for its purpose; thick chaos does. The thinness ratio quantifies this by comparing the typical displacement produced by chaotic motion with the displacement that would count as failure. Four elementary results establish the claim. The first constructs an example in which the Lyapunov exponent can be fixed while the confinement outcome is varied at will, showing the two questions are logically independent. The second shows that the thinness ratio is controlled by Kellert’s own measure of predictive hopelessness scaled by the ratio of the system’s accessible span to the failure threshold; Kellert’s criterion is recovered exactly when the failure scale is half that span. The third supplies a distribution-free upper bound on the probability that the system has left the safe region by the end of the interval, proves the bound cannot be improved without further assumptions, and extends it to the entire interval when successive displacements behave like a martingale. The fourth replaces the root-mean-square displacement with a quantile of the running maximum, making the ratio equal to one precisely when confinement holds at a stated confidence level. The results are limited to logical relations and inequalities. They do not establish that any particular physical system remains confined; every confinement claim remains conditional on the adequacy of the model that supplies the confining geometry. A positive Lyapunov exponent alone therefore settles neither risk nor safety. Practical reporting of chaos should state the relevant variable, failure scale, horizon, and confidence level, and reliability claims based on the root-mean-square form of the ratio are correspondingly weak unless stronger distributional assumptions are justified. The paper’s contribution is to separate the prediction of location from the prediction of continued confinement and to supply a measure for the latter.
title: Unpredictable but Confined: Thin Chaos and the Scope of Kellert's Impossibility Argument

English title: The influence of auxiliary products in organic production on sowing qualities and yield properties of millet seeds. Organic production has been widespread in Ukraine for a long time, but in recent years it has developed rapidly, even in war conditions, Ukraine occupies a leading position in the export of such products. When introducing organic production, a number of operators in Ukraine face the problem of providing high-quality organic planting material, especially millet. The area for organic production in Ukraine is 1% of the total area of farmlands. Therefore, the aim of the research was to improve the elements of millet cultivation technology as the basis for obtaining high-quality planting material under organic production. The research was carried out during 2022-2024 on the basis of T.H.Shevchenko private agricultural enterprise, village Trostinka, Vasylkiv district, Kyiv region. The millet varieties («Omriyane» and «Bila Altanka»), the auxiliary products permitted in organic production and the conditions of their application were studied. Permitted auxiliary products in organic production had a positive effect on the improvement of germination energy, in particular with the use of «Biocomplex BTU» obtained 93,0% in the «Omriyane» variety and 92,0% in the «Bila Altanka» variety. The field germination of the studied varieties was in the range of 76,3-76,6%. The number of millet plants of the «Omriyane» variety in the phase of full emergence was at the level of 243,0-245,8 pl./m², the increase of this indicator was due to the use of biological preparations. With the use of such preparations as «Biocomplex BTU» and «Organic-Balance», the millet yield was obtained at the level of 3,74-3,90 t/ha compared to the control plots of 2,49-2,73 t/ha. summary: The study evaluates the effectiveness of a methodology for developing professional digital competencies of pre-service primary school teachers through improved software and methodological support. The methodology combined a six-block methodological model, the integrating educational platform “DigiPed” with five curriculum-aligned modules, a unified cycle of innovative methods and a multi-stage assessment system. A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design with non-equivalent intact groups was carried out in 2023–2025 at three higher education institutions in Uzbekistan with 770 students (experimental group n = 386, control group n = 384). Competence was measured on motivational, cognitive, activity and reflective criteria combined into a weighted integral index K = 0.20k₁ + 0.25k₂ + 0.35k₃ + 0.20k₄; assessors were blind to group membership. At baseline the groups did not differ (χ² = 0.08–3.39; t = 0.13–1.03). After three semesters the experimental group’s mean integral score rose from 56.77 to 67.52 and the control group’s from 56.26 to 59.24 (t = 9.79, p < 0.05). The share of experimental students at the low level fell from 62.7 % to 30.8 % (control group: 51.8 %), and differences were significant on all criteria (χ² = 49.75–68.31). The efficiency coefficient was η = 1.14 overall and 1.13–1.17 across institutions, indicating that the effect is transferable beyond a single university.

summary: Augmented reality (AR) is increasingly used in education, but most classroom studies focus on engagement rather than specific emotional or cognitive processes. We re-examined data from a six-week pilot project where AR was integrated into drama lessons for 59 primary-school students in four classes. Our goal was to see what the observations reveal about emotion recognition, emotion regulation, collaboration, problem solving, and reflective reasoning. QuiverVision and CoSpaces Edu were used for role-play, collaborative storytelling, exploring moods in space, replaying conflicts, and reflection. The data included teacher observation rubrics, structured checklists, student exit tickets, and records of regulation strategies. In this paper, we use affective computing as a conceptual framework, not as a description of the technology used in the pilot. Emotions were not detected automatically; instead, the analysis relies on human observation and student self-reports. Of the 106 exit-ticket responses from Weeks 1 and 2, happiness was the most common emotion (73 out of 106; 68.9%). Forty-eight students had emotion-recognition ratings recorded at Weeks 1, 2, 3, and 5, and these ratings changed over time (Friedman χ²(3)=34.21, p<0.001; Kendall's W=0.238), with the mean score rising from 2.90 (SD=0.66) in Week 1 to 3.46 (SD=0.50) in Week 5. Regulation strategies also varied by phase: socially oriented responses were frequent in Week 2, while breathing, pausing, and reframing were more common during the explicit regulation activities in Week 5. Because the prompts and tasks differed each week, these distributions are descriptive and do not show a causal pre/post change. Exploratory correlations found that collaborative storytelling was linked to problem solving, strategy use was associated with returning to role, and understanding emotions was connected with cooperation. Overall, the results show that a pedagogy-first AR drama approach is feasible and highlight what a future study would need: validated measures, comparison groups, multilevel analysis, follow-up data, and carefully controlled multimodal affect sensing.
title: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 79 – Augmented Reality-Enhanced Drama Through an Affective Computing Lens: A Six-Week Pilot Study of Emotional Intelligence, Emotion Regulation, and Reflective Reasoning in Children

summary: Abstract Generative visual AI is increasingly used in early-stage design to produce sketches, concept renderings and alternative visual directions. However, visually convincing outputs do not necessarily constitute traceable or justified design decisions. In human–AI co-creation, generated images may remain weakly connected to design intent, evaluation criteria, evidence and design rationale, making the creative process difficult to review, reuse, and, where applicable, assess consistently. This paper proposes a process-level methodological framework for human–AI co-creation with generative visual AI systems. The framework is conceived as a lightweight traceability schema linking design problem, design intent, evaluation criteria, generative input, AI output, selected and rejected features, specifications, evidence, design decisions and iteration records. Its purpose is not to explain the internal behaviour of the generative model, but to document the human interpretation and decision-making process around generated visual artefacts. The proposal is illustrated through a postgraduate conceptual product design case in which generative visual AI was introduced after a systemic intent-structuring phase. The case provides evidence of feasibility for reconstructing the relationship between prior intent, generated outputs, and design decisions, but it is not presented as a controlled validation. The paper contributes to creative AI and human–AI interaction by reframing generated outputs as intermediate artefacts that require explicit links to intent, evidence and accountable design decisions.
title: From Generative Output to Traceable Design Decisions: A Process-Level Framework for Human–AI Co-Creation in Conceptual Design

summary: The Kung–Traub conjecture states that the convergence order of a memoryless scalar iterative method using n evaluations of a function and its derivatives per iteration cannot exceed 2^(n−1). We prove this bound for real scalar, deterministic, causal methods with adaptive queries and partially defined rules, without requiring continuity or computability of those rules. For every total method T with budget n and every p > 2^(n−1), we construct an entire function F, real on the real axis, a simple root α, and a sequence x_m → α such that |T_F(x_m) − α| / |x_m − α|^p → +∞. summary: Heterogeneous evidence systems frequently combine observations that differ in measurement process, provenance, semantic representation, reliability, temporal coverage, spatial resolution, and statistical dependence. Naive aggregation can consequently amplify duplicated sources, conceal systematic bias, misrepresent uncertainty, and force consensus across claims that are not genuinely comparable. This manuscript proposes Cross-Domain Evidence-Constrained State Reconstruction (CDECSR), a research architecture whose default mechanism is Provenance-Aware, Uncertainty-Preserving State Reconstruction (PAUSR). The architecture preserves four macro-stages: taxonomic and semantic anchoring; error, dependence, and reliability parameterization: triangulation, robust fusion, and contradiction management; and latent-state estimation, validation, and controlled revision. These stages are operationalized through fourteen layers. The formal framework distinguishes the underlying target state from observations and model-dependent estimates. It represents heterogeneous observations through source-specific measurement models, accounts for shared provenance and correlated errors, and treats source reliability as a conditional quantity rather than a direct measure of truth. The proposed output is a state estimate or posterior distribution accompanied by uncertainty, provenance, unresolved contradictions, assumptions, validation results, and a reproducibility record. The architecture is specified through the Conflicting Reports in an Environmental Crisis (CREC), a structured primary case in which field reports and other observations may disagree about event location, timing, intensity, extent, and progression. The manuscript also defines a falsifiable research program, conditional mathematical results, counterexamples, simulation requirements, validation protocols, and a fourteen-step pathway toward a research paper.

summary: Author-authorised R2 analysis-code release for the Scientific Reports norovirus revision. Outcomes remain frozen at 4,801 cases and 220 outbreaks across 1,115 district-years (223 districts, 2020–2024). The revision_R2 directory corrects official facility-level sludge-moisture aggregation, excludes totals/subtotals and inappropriate zero codes, and distinguishes 802 measured from 313 unavailable district-years. It includes principal, paediatric, outbreak-count, spatial-graph, prior, influential-observation, missing-administrative-year and moisture-availability analyses, numerical-repeat and independent maximum-likelihood checks, and validated full-precision results. The earlier positive national moisture association is not reproduced after correction. The archived R1 input object and official annual workbooks are required and are not bundled; precise input requirements and source hashes are documented. Root-level R1 scripts are retained for provenance. No individual patient information is included.

summary: The work looks at the Riemann hypothesis from the standpoint of the model “The Birth of Dimensions” (BD). The number arrow is understood as a projection of a process — the comparison of the standard-observer with its surroundings. Four reference quantities follow from the construction: 1 — the observer and the standard; 0 and ∞ — two infinities converging into one point; 1/2 — the level of lost phase, a line perpendicular to the arrow; 2 — the first distinction, the point of doubling. Together they define a sphere: the arrow is a tangent to the circle through the observer, the rotation goes about an axis, the spin-up force is applied at a point of the equator, and its trace on the arrow is 2. The main result is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD: if the original process is a sine, that is, a rotation; if everything tied to the observer is his likeness; if an instantaneous snapshot has no duplicates and balance sets the mirror, — then all zeros lie on the equator of the sphere, that is, on the line Re s = 1/2 (section 4). This is a proof within the model, not a mathematical proof. In mathematics the hypothesis remains open: of the nine links of the chain eight are known theorems, and the ninth — that the local rotations of all primes form one rotation — is equivalent to the hypothesis itself (section 5). Each step carries a status: [K] — a known mathematical fact, [H] — a hypothesis or interpretation of the author, [O] — an open question. The detailed exposition is placed in Appendices 1–10. They show that the logic of BD independently leads to what mathematicians obtained by abstract means: Riemann's mirror, the Euler product, the Gauss sum, Gram points, the Riemann–Siegel formula, the de Bruijn–Newman constant, Li's criterion, Weil positivity, the adelic approach of Tate and Connes, the Lee–Yang theorem and other results (section 6). For BD this is strong support: the model generates the same mathematics from its own principles. Version 12. The article has been restructured so that the main conclusion is not lost among the reasoning. Part I: a dictionary of BD and mathematical notions; foundations by construction (1, 0 and ∞, 1/2, 2); the picture of the sphere with a figure (the arrow as a tangent through the observer, 1/2 as the axis of rotation, 2 as the spin-up point); a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD from the postulates P1–P4; the mathematical status (eight links of the chain are known theorems, the ninth is equivalent to the hypothesis); the role of the observer; a list of known results that BD reproduces. Part II: the former detailed exposition as Appendices 1–10, with additions on the sphere, observers in every prime and the author’s position.       Работа рассматривает гипотезу Римана с позиции модели «Рождение измерений» (РИ). Числовая стрела понимается как проекция процесса — сравнения эталона-наблюдателя с окружением. Из построения следуют четыре опорные величины: 1 — наблюдатель и эталон; 0 и ∞ — две бесконечности, сходящиеся в одну точку; 1/2 — уровень потерянной фазы, прямая, перпендикулярная стреле; 2 — первое различение, точка удвоения. Вместе они задают сферу: стрела — касательная к кругу через наблюдателя, вращение идёт вокруг оси, сила раскрутки приложена в точке экватора, и её след на стреле — 2. Главный результат — доказательство гипотезы Римана в рамках РИ: если исходный процесс — синус, то есть вращение; если всё, связанное с наблюдателем, — его подобие; если в мгновенном снимке нет дублей, а баланс задаёт зеркало, — то все нули лежат на экваторе сферы, то есть на прямой Re s = 1/2 (раздел 4). Это доказательство внутри модели, а не математическое доказательство. В математике гипотеза остаётся открытой: из девяти звеньев цепочки восемь — известные теор
title: The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2: The Riemann Hypothesis in the Light of the Birth of Dimensions Model

summary: The work looks at the Riemann hypothesis from the standpoint of the model “The Birth of Dimensions” (BD). The number arrow is understood as a projection of a process — the comparison of the standard-observer with its surroundings. Four reference quantities follow from the construction: 1 — the observer and the standard; 0 and ∞ — two infinities converging into one point; 1/2 — the level of lost phase, a line perpendicular to the arrow; 2 — the first distinction, the point of doubling. Together they define a sphere: the arrow is a tangent to the circle through the observer, the rotation goes about an axis, the spin-up force is applied at a point of the equator, and its trace on the arrow is 2. The main result is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD: if the original process is a sine, that is, a rotation; if everything tied to the observer is his likeness; if an instantaneous snapshot has no duplicates and balance sets the mirror, — then all zeros lie on the equator of the sphere, that is, on the line Re s = 1/2 (section 4). This is a proof within the model, not a mathematical proof. In mathematics the hypothesis remains open: of the nine links of the chain eight are known theorems, and the ninth — that the local rotations of all primes form one rotation — is equivalent to the hypothesis itself (section 5). Each step carries a status: [K] — a known mathematical fact, [H] — a hypothesis or interpretation of the author, [O] — an open question. The detailed exposition is placed in Appendices 1–10. They show that the logic of BD independently leads to what mathematicians obtained by abstract means: Riemann's mirror, the Euler product, the Gauss sum, Gram points, the Riemann–Siegel formula, the de Bruijn–Newman constant, Li's criterion, Weil positivity, the adelic approach of Tate and Connes, the Lee–Yang theorem and other results (section 6). For BD this is strong support: the model generates the same mathematics from its own principles. Version 12. The article has been restructured so that the main conclusion is not lost among the reasoning. Part I: a dictionary of BD and mathematical notions; foundations by construction (1, 0 and ∞, 1/2, 2); the picture of the sphere with a figure (the arrow as a tangent through the observer, 1/2 as the axis of rotation, 2 as the spin-up point); a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD from the postulates P1–P4; the mathematical status (eight links of the chain are known theorems, the ninth is equivalent to the hypothesis); the role of the observer; a list of known results that BD reproduces. Part II: the former detailed exposition as Appendices 1–10, with additions on the sphere, observers in every prime and the author’s position.       Работа рассматривает гипотезу Римана с позиции модели «Рождение измерений» (РИ). Числовая стрела понимается как проекция процесса — сравнения эталона-наблюдателя с окружением. Из построения следуют четыре опорные величины: 1 — наблюдатель и эталон; 0 и ∞ — две бесконечности, сходящиеся в одну точку; 1/2 — уровень потерянной фазы, прямая, перпендикулярная стреле; 2 — первое различение, точка удвоения. Вместе они задают сферу: стрела — касательная к кругу через наблюдателя, вращение идёт вокруг оси, сила раскрутки приложена в точке экватора, и её след на стреле — 2. Главный результат — доказательство гипотезы Римана в рамках РИ: если исходный процесс — синус, то есть вращение; если всё, связанное с наблюдателем, — его подобие; если в мгновенном снимке нет дублей, а баланс задаёт зеркало, — то все нули лежат на экваторе сферы, то есть на прямой Re s = 1/2 (раздел 4). Это доказательство внутри модели, а не математическое доказательство. В математике гипотеза остаётся открытой: из девяти звеньев цепочки восемь — известные теор

summary: All notable changes to svdynamics are documented in this file. The project follows [ Semantic Versioning ](https://semver.org/) and is currently in alpha development. [0.0.1a3] - 2026-11-11 Improved Improved scikit-learn estimator API compatibility for SVDClassifier and SVDRegressor . Added explicit fitted-state validation using check_is_fitted() , providing standard NotFittedError exceptions when prediction methods are called before fitting. Updated predict_proba availability to match scikit-learn's SVC behavior, exposing the method only when probability=True . Added conditional predict_log_proba support for probability-enabled classifiers. Improved fitted-estimator state management by assigning the underlying SVC/SVR model only after successful fitting. Preserved compatibility with scikit-learn 1.0.2 by conditionally exposing version-dependent attributes. Improved n_features_in_ handling for callable composite kernels by falling back to the input feature count when the underlying estimator does not expose the attribute. Added Exposed support_ , support_vectors_ , and n_support_ attributes for greater consistency with scikit-learn estimators. Exposed n_iter_ when supported by the installed scikit-learn version. Exposed n_features_in_ for both classification and regression estimators. Added __sklearn_is_fitted__() support for fitted-state detection. Added 12 unit tests covering fitted-state validation, probability prediction, support-vector attributes, and estimator compatibility. Unchanged Existing composite and adaptive composite kernel implementations. Training-data-based kernel normalization. Adaptive kernel-weight learning for binary classification. Underlying SVC and SVR optimization behavior. Validation All 68 unit tests passed under Python 3.8 with scikit-learn 1.3.2. The original 56 tests were also reported passing under the minimum supported scikit-learn 1.0.2 configuration. The expanded 68-test suite has not yet been confirmed in that environment. Total statement coverage increased to 96%, with 100% statement coverage for svm.py . A memory-mapping failure in scikit-learn's estimator compliance checks was also reproduced with native SVC and SVR under scikit-learn 1.3.2. Full estimator-check compliance remains unverified.
title: lshpaner/svdynamics: svdynamics v0.0.1a3

summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP), a general theoretical framework for analysing how a reasonable default inference about an object, individual, event, process, model, or system may be presented with a stronger epistemic status than its available justification warrants. The framework distinguishes the basis used to construct an inference from the inference itself, the evidence supporting it, the status assigned to it, the scope within which it is. asserted, and the role it plays in an operational system. A reference standard may consist of a statistical base rate, a measure of central tendency, an operational default, a validated baseline, a normative or formal standard, or a model-based analogy. These categories are related but not interchangeable. The central proposition is conditional. A default inference may be reasonable and useful without being an established fact. A status-escalation error may arise when an inference is promoted to the status of an established fact, objective description, or necessary system condition without adequate evidential, logical, or formal warrant. Such an error does not automatically produce a contradiction, paradox, dilemma, or operational failure. Those outcomes require independent definitions and additional conditions. The paper develops a six-class reference-standard taxonomy, a formal representation of reasonable reference-standard inference, a seven-stage-or-more process architecture, a twelve-category outcome taxonomy, seven theoretical propositions, a general mathematical specification, and a research programme centred on the social-media newcomer purpose-projection case. The framework also specifies its boundaries, alternative explanations, potential falsifiers, measurement requirements, and route to empirical validation. RSIFEP is presented as a proposed theoretical contribution rather than an established uni- versal law. Its novelty, explanatory advantage, measurement validity, and domain generality remain questions for literature comparison, formal analysis, and empirical testing. Keywords: reference standards; reasonable inference; default reasoning; epistemic status; status escalation; evidential warrant; scope overextension; contradiction; paradox; system-level outcomes.

summary: This paper proposes the Representational-Operational State-Inversion Principle (ROSIP), a candidate framework for describing cases in which an internal representation assigns a state that is the formally defined inverse of a corresponding operational state, while the operational state itself need not undergo a physical reversal. The motivating case is a false awakening: a person is asleep according to an independent physiological reference while the person's dream represents the self as awake. The proposed framework generalizes this contrast by separating the operational state of a system, the internal state of its model, the represented proposition about a shared referent, the inverse relation between comparable state features, and the attribution of the represented state as current reality. The paper defines a common semantic comparison space, an involutive inverse-state mapping, a state-divergence measure, an inversion-fit score, and a gated event-classification rule. It distinguishes representational inversion from ordinary mismatch, stale information, hypothetical simulation, false reporting, and actual reversal of physical dynamics. Eight proposed mechanism stages and fourteen analytical layers organize the framework. The manuscript identifies five foundational domains, a primary sleep-science validation pro- gram, six exploratory application domains, seven testable hypotheses, alternative explanations, falsification criteria, methodological requirements, and a fourteen-stage research roadmap. The framework's central contribution is presented as a testable formalization proposal, not as an established discovery. Its explanatory value depends on construct validity, temporal alignment, reliable measurement, independent replication, and evidence of incremental value over existing explanations. summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Functional Direction-Purpose Mismatch Framework (FDPMF), a goal-relative framework for analyzing operations whose functional direction may not correspond to an agent's specified purpose. The framework distinguishes structural direction- purpose relations from measured direct utility, capability acquisition from execution, and direct utility from broader functional value. The mathematical core defines incremental direct utility as a difference between expected goal-related outcomes under an operation and a specified baseline. This definition enables conditional statements about positive, zero, or negative contribution while avoiding the unsupported inference that a mismatch automatically makes an operation universally useless. A separate Signal-Identity Inference Module (SIIM) examines how an observed event is used to infer an agent's identity or motive. Bayesian notation is used to formalize the evidential relationship between an observation and competing hypotheses. The framework does not treat any single learned or performed behavior as a deterministic indicator of sexual orientation. The primary illustrative case concerns a heterosexual self-identified male learner being taught a sexual behavior directed toward a male recipient, where the intended use is excluded from the learner's explicitly specified personal sexual goal. The case is conditional on these assumptions and is distinguished from a control case in which the target of the learned operation is consistent with the learner's stated goal. The paper defines the framework's ontology, terminology, mathematical variables, core mechanism, propositions, boundary conditions, operationalization protocol, empirical hy- potheses, research domains, falsification criteria, and manuscript-development roadmap. No empirical results are claimed. The paper concludes that the framework is conceptually specified for investigation, while its empirical validity and novelty remain open. Keywords: functional direction; purpose congruence; goal-relative utility; causal inference; capability acquisition; signaling theory; identity inference; operationalization; theoretical model

summary: This repository provides national-scale datasets of the edaphology (Serie III) and Land Use and Vegetation (Serie IV - VI) for Mexico from official cartography of the Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI) . The datasets were used as the input to developed a national-scale raster datasets of the NRCS/SCS Curve Number (CN) and Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG) for Mexico . The research manuscript: Reproducing Mexico’s national TR-55 Curve Number map (2007–2014): A benchmark using INEGI cartography is under review. The same dataset can be also download at the following link: Edaphology: https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/edafologia/#descargas Land Use and Vegetation: https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/usosuelo/#descargas

The research manuscript: Reproducing Mexico’s national TR-55 Curve Number map (2007–2014): A benchmark using INEGI cartography is under review. The same dataset can be also download at the following link: Edaphology: https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/edafologia/#descargas Land Use and Vegetation: https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/usosuelo/#descargas
title: Reproducing Mexico's national TR-55 Curve Number map (2007–2014): A benchmark using INEGI cartography. Manuscript.

summary: Observations of a common physical event may differ across sensors because the sensors operate at different elevations, coordinate frames, reference times, sampling rates, calibration states, response functions, and uncertainty regimes. Raw disagreement does not, by itself, establish a physical contradiction, a sensor failure, or the existence of a new physical phenomenon. It may arise from frame misregistration, clock offsets, distinct measurands, correlated errors, genuine event dynamics, model misspecification, or insufficient observability. This paper specifies the Unified Cross-Frame Information Convergence Architecture (UCFICA), a modular framework for diagnosing and reconciling multisource observations before reconstructing a target system state. Its operational estimation core is the Reference-Conditioned Multisource State Reconstruction Architecture (RCMSRA). The framework preserves the Multi-Elevation Spatial Observation Discrepancy (MESOD) as its primary case, the Reference-Conditioned State Reconstruction Mechanism (RCSRM) as its default mechanism, and the Cross-Dimensional State Realization Protocol (CD-SRP) as its named operational protocol. The manuscript formalizes heterogeneous measurement models, coordinate and time registration, uncertainty propagation, linear-Gaussian information-form fusion, nonlinear estimation alternatives, unknown-correlation handling, residual diagnostics, and explicit rules for unresolved or incompatible observations. It preserves the original five conceptual levels while mapping them to nine operational layers. Relativistic corrections, quantum measurement theory, and holographic or cosmological hypotheses are retained as conditional research branches rather than assumed components of every fusion problem. Conditional propositions establish the mathematical circumstances under which familiar Bayesian and linear-estimation results apply. In particular, the paper does not assume that increasing the number of sensors necessarily drives estimation covariance to zero. It defines falsifiable hypotheses, controlled simulation scenarios, empirical validation requirements, counterexamples, and a staged reproducibility protocol. No simulation or empirical result is claimed to have been obtained in this manuscript.

summary: We compare neural networks, exact Matérn kernel regression and their combinations as emulators of a six-dimensional radiative-transfer table on the 285-band EMIT grid, and we study how their forward accuracy carries over to reflectance retrieval. Over ten partitions of 23{,}313 states, a kernel with one length scale per input reaches $0.095\%$ mean relative radiance error and a network $0.387\%$; a kernel on the concatenated hidden features of five networks reaches $0.076\%$. Forward and inverse rankings disagree. A convex stack improves on a wide feature kernel by only $0.0006$ radiance percentage points, yet its 95th-percentile reflectance error is larger at every partition, three times larger on average. We prove that on the physical domain the constrained retrieval error is at most the retrieval-weighted component error divided by the transmission, with constant one, that the rate this implies is sharp, and that errors proportional to the transmission lose no rate. The reversal persists on the physical domain of the retrieval and when every family is retrained on physically admissible targets only; on a second radiative-transfer code, whose transmissions stay away from zero outside one opaque band, it is much weaker.
title: Learned representations and kernel corrections for radiative-transfer emulation

We prove that on the physical domain the constrained retrieval error is at most the retrieval-weighted component error divided by the transmission, with constant one, that the rate this implies is sharp, and that errors proportional to the transmission lose no rate. The reversal persists on the physical domain of the retrieval and when every family is retrained on physically admissible targets only; on a second radiative-transfer code, whose transmissions stay away from zero outside one opaque band, it is much weaker.
title: Learned representations and kernel corrections for radiative-transfer emulation

summary: This report documents the curation and open publication of measurements from a long-term Turkey oak ( Quercus cerris ) thinning experiment in the Gargano area, southern Italy, monitored from 1988 to 2026. Nine 0.5-ha plots compare an unthinned control with two thinning regimes: 15% basal-area reduction over two interventions and 33% basal-area reduction in one intervention. Legacy spreadsheet records were cleaned, validated, and organized into a documented SQLite database (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24142797) containing tree measurements, experimental design, controlled vocabularies, metadata, and provenance. The curation workflow addresses duplicate identifiers, irregular or gappy measurement series, unusable records, and missing values, with imputations explicitly flagged. The resource includes a richly documented database, a JSON file with PROV-O provenance, and an entity-relationship diagram of the database schema. It is intended to make the data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable in accordance with FAIR principles, and to provide a reproducible example of data curation for long-term forest research.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24146492 . Peer review report: Caetano et al., investigate the diversity of mammalian box C/D small nucleolar RNAs (SNORDs) by combining Fibrillarin- and Snu13-associated RNA sequencing with extensive analysis of publicly available datasets. They identify 21,732 candidate loci, including a large population of unusually short single-stranded RNAs (20-50 nt), termed tiSNORDs. This work is important because it challenges the current annotation of the mammalian snoRNAs and raises fundamental questions about snoRNP biogenesis and the emergence of regulatory RNAs. Particularly convincing are the enrichment of characteristic box C/D sequence signatures, the association of selected candidates with Fibrillarin, and the demonstration that a 36-nt tiSNORD can guide RNA methylation. The observations concerning terminal stem structures, RNA stability and host-gene expression provide further support for the biological relevance of at least a subset of these RNAs. Therefore, the study is interesting and potentially significant. Addressing several methodological and interpretative concerns , particularly regarding library-preparation biases, statistical validation of candidate identification, and the distinction between mature RNAs and RNA fragments would strengthen claims and introduce reproducibility. Major points: 1. RNA library preparation and size-selection bias. Approximately ~70 % of tiSNORDs are 20-50 nt long, yet the size-selection used with the TruSeq small RNA library preparation kit is not specified. Size-dependent recovery and sequence-dependent ligation biases could substantially influence this distribution. The authors acknowledge such biases for SNORD50 and substantial technical variability between datasets. Clarification of the selected insert range and, ideally, independent analysis of RNAs across a broader size range would strengthen this central conclusion. One would be to use splint-ligation library preparation to get 'unbiased' small RNA library for sequencing (e.g. Maguire et al., 2020; PMID: 32496547). 2. Statistical validation of sequence signatures. The identification of tiSNORDs relies heavily on canonical C/D-box motifs, their terminal positions and uridine enrichment (Figures 1C to 1G). However, no explicit null model accounts for the search criteria, meaning that some positional enrichment is expected by construction. Small RNA-seq ligation biases may also influence nucleotide frequencies (Kim et al., 2019; PMID: 30605524). Permutation analyses using length- and composition-matched intronic sequences processed through the same pipeline would help ensure statistical significance and estimate false-positive rates. Potential spike ins would be of use as well. 3. Distinguishing mature tiSNORDs from RNA fragments. Although the authors demonstrate stable endogenous expression of tiSNORD candidate and successful processing of selected ectopically expressed candidates, these findings cannot necessarily be extrapolated to thousands of low-abundance sequences. Examining coverage across candidate loci, overlapping fragments, flanking regions and potential longer precursors would help distinguish independently matured tiSNORDs from RNA processing or degradation/fragmentation products. 4. Confidence in the proposed repertoire. 12% of candidates exceed one count per million, and substantial discrepancies are observed between independent datasets (Supplementary Figure 3). The authors appropriately acknowledge these limitations further in the text, but the claim that more than 20,000 loci substantially expand the snoRNA repertoire is a potential since it does not have biochemical validation and mentioning that they are "putative" in the abstract would help the reader to understand the scope of this article. Stratification by abundance, reproducibility and independent experimental evidence wou

summary: The Kung–Traub conjecture states that the convergence order of a memoryless scalar iterative method using n evaluations of a function and its derivatives per iteration cannot exceed 2^(n−1). We prove this bound for real scalar, deterministic, causal methods with adaptive queries and partially defined rules, without requiring continuity or computability of those rules. For every total method T with budget n and every p > 2^(n−1), we construct an entire function F, real on the real axis, a simple root α, and a sequence x_m → α such that |T_F(x_m) − α| / |x_m − α|^p → +∞. The construction uses properties of Wronskians of polynomial spaces, concentration of zeros, and quantitative perturbations that preserve exactly the responses to previous queries. We also develop two formalizations of computation: a fixed-budget query model and a model of procedures with internal states and performed evaluations. We prove exact representations that preserve, within the budget under consideration, the domains of valid computations, outputs, records, and evaluation counts by derivative order. From this correspondence, we obtain the order barrier for local realizations and the real formulation of the Kung–Traub bound with the specified operational cost. The results are established for real functions and real nodes. Historical documentation: Earlier versions of this research, completed on September 17–18, 2026, together with their available provenance records, are preserved at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24147519 .
title: The Kung–Traub Conjecture for Memoryless Real Scalar Methods: Proof and Formalization of Computational Procedures

summary: Heterogeneous evidence systems frequently combine observations that differ in measurement process, provenance, semantic representation, reliability, temporal coverage, spatial resolution, and statistical dependence. Naive aggregation can consequently amplify duplicated sources, conceal systematic bias, misrepresent uncertainty, and force consensus across claims that are not genuinely comparable. This manuscript proposes Cross-Domain Evidence-Constrained State Reconstruction (CDECSR), a research architecture whose default mechanism is Provenance-Aware, Uncertainty-Preserving State Reconstruction (PAUSR). The architecture preserves four macro-stages: taxonomic and semantic anchoring; error, dependence, and reliability parameterization: triangulation, robust fusion, and contradiction management; and latent-state estimation, validation, and controlled revision. These stages are operationalized through fourteen layers. The formal framework distinguishes the underlying target state from observations and model-dependent estimates. It represents heterogeneous observations through source-specific measurement models, accounts for shared provenance and correlated errors, and treats source reliability as a conditional quantity rather than a direct measure of truth. The proposed output is a state estimate or posterior distribution accompanied by uncertainty, provenance, unresolved contradictions, assumptions, validation results, and a reproducibility record. The architecture is specified through the Conflicting Reports in an Environmental Crisis (CREC), a structured primary case in which field reports and other observations may disagree about event location, timing, intensity, extent, and progression. The manuscript also defines a falsifiable research program, conditional mathematical results, counterexamples, simulation requirements, validation protocols, and a fourteen-step pathway toward a research paper.

summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP), a general theoretical framework for analysing how a reasonable default inference about an object, individual, event, process, model, or system may be presented with a stronger epistemic status than its available justification warrants. The framework distinguishes the basis used to construct an inference from the inference itself, the evidence supporting it, the status assigned to it, the scope within which it is. asserted, and the role it plays in an operational system. A reference standard may consist of a statistical base rate, a measure of central tendency, an operational default, a validated baseline, a normative or formal standard, or a model-based analogy. These categories are related but not interchangeable. The central proposition is conditional. A default inference may be reasonable and useful without being an established fact. A status-escalation error may arise when an inference is promoted to the status of an established fact, objective description, or necessary system condition without adequate evidential, logical, or formal warrant. Such an error does not automatically produce a contradiction, paradox, dilemma, or operational failure. Those outcomes require independent definitions and additional conditions. The paper develops a six-class reference-standard taxonomy, a formal representation of reasonable reference-standard inference, a seven-stage-or-more process architecture, a twelve-category outcome taxonomy, seven theoretical propositions, a general mathematical specification, and a research programme centred on the social-media newcomer purpose-projection case. The framework also specifies its boundaries, alternative explanations, potential falsifiers, measurement requirements, and route to empirical validation. RSIFEP is presented as a proposed theoretical contribution rather than an established uni- versal law. Its novelty, explanatory advantage, measurement validity, and domain generality remain questions for literature comparison, formal analysis, and empirical testing. Keywords: reference standards; reasonable inference; default reasoning; epistemic status; status escalation; evidential warrant; scope overextension; contradiction; paradox; system-level outcomes.

title: The Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP): A General Framework for Reasonable Default Inference, Epistemic Status Escalation, and System-Level Outcomes

summary: Observations of a common physical event may differ across sensors because the sensors operate at different elevations, coordinate frames, reference times, sampling rates, calibration states, response functions, and uncertainty regimes. Raw disagreement does not, by itself, establish a physical contradiction, a sensor failure, or the existence of a new physical phenomenon. It may arise from frame misregistration, clock offsets, distinct measurands, correlated errors, genuine event dynamics, model misspecification, or insufficient observability. This paper specifies the Unified Cross-Frame Information Convergence Architecture (UCFICA), a modular framework for diagnosing and reconciling multisource observations before reconstructing a target system state. Its operational estimation core is the Reference-Conditioned Multisource State Reconstruction Architecture (RCMSRA). The framework preserves the Multi-Elevation Spatial Observation Discrepancy (MESOD) as its primary case, the Reference-Conditioned State Reconstruction Mechanism (RCSRM) as its default mechanism, and the Cross-Dimensional State Realization Protocol (CD-SRP) as its named operational protocol. The manuscript formalizes heterogeneous measurement models, coordinate and time registration, uncertainty propagation, linear-Gaussian information-form fusion, nonlinear estimation alternatives, unknown-correlation handling, residual diagnostics, and explicit rules for unresolved or incompatible observations. It preserves the original five conceptual levels while mapping them to nine operational layers. Relativistic corrections, quantum measurement theory, and holographic or cosmological hypotheses are retained as conditional research branches rather than assumed components of every fusion problem. Conditional propositions establish the mathematical circumstances under which familiar Bayesian and linear-estimation results apply. In particular, the paper does not assume that increasing the number of sensors necessarily drives estimation covariance to zero. It defines falsifiable hypotheses, controlled simulation scenarios, empirical validation requirements, counterexamples, and a staged reproducibility protocol. No simulation or empirical result is claimed to have been obtained in this manuscript.
tags: multisensor fusion; cross-frame registration; state estimation; measurement uncertainty; Bayesian inference; observability; information-form filtering; MESOD; UCFICA; conditional multiphysics
title: Unified Cross-Frame Information Convergence Architecture

summary: The four-component (T, I, N, F) neutrosophic representation distinguishes pure indeterminacy I from neutrality N, in addition to truth T and falsehood F. Existing neutrosophic-graph research mainly assigns uncertain values to vertices or edges and studies the resulting graph structure. This paper addresses a different problem: a fixed weighted network is given, while a (T, I, N, F) assessment is the signal carried by each vertex. A benefit-coordinate embedding converts the semantic order into the standard product order and permits graph-Laplacian methods without merging neutrality and indeterminacy. For continuous-time heat diffusion, we prove preservation of the TINF cube, semantic order, component means, complement symmetry, and a maximum principle. A weighted Dirichlet energy is shown to decay monotonically, with exponential convergence governed by the algebraic connectivity. A stable discrete-time scheme and a soft-anchor graph filter are also established. For partially observed signals, the TINF harmonic extension is characterized simultaneously as the unique Dirichlet-energy minimizer and as a convex combination of boundary assessments. This yields complement equivariance, a semantic maximum principle, nonexpansive dependence on boundary data, and an explicit topology-perturbation bound. Complement-paired TINF prototypes are then introduced for four-state semi-supervised inference. They form a regular simplex in benefit coordinates, and nearest-prototype TINF classification is proved exactly equivalent to classical multiclass harmonic label propagation when anchors use the prototypes. In contrast, a symmetric three-component collapse makes neutrality and pure indeterminacy non-identifiable. An exact cycle example and Monte Carlo stochastic-block experiments confirm the equivalence numerically and demonstrate the information loss caused by collapse. The framework provides a mathematically auditable route for propagating four-component information over social, sensor, and knowledge networks.
title: TINF Signals on Networks: Complement-Equivariant Graph Diffusion, Harmonic Extension, and Semi-Supervised Inference

summary: Harmonized snATAC-seq / snMultiome atlas across 10 published GBM cohorts (67 patients with >=50 cells per label group, ~1.65M nuclei, 2,085,175 union peaks), scored per cell type with specificity (log2FC across 10 primary cell types or 13 cell types with Neftel subtype split) and strength (fragments per cell at the peak, patient-averaged, width-normalized). v2026-11-10d correctness patch: re-applies the 60% patient-detection hard floor on top-1000 selection, after the v7 pipeline rewrite silently dropped it at v2026-11-10. scripts/scoring_config.py gains MIN_DETECTION_RATE=0.60 and MIN_CELLS_EVALUABLE=50 constants, plus an assert_filters() guard that fails at import time if downstream scripts disagree. Both the regen_top1000_v7 and build_atlas_v4_html scripts now import and enforce the floor. v4_master_scores.parquet unchanged (byte-identical to v10c). Impact: malignant top-1000 min detection rose from 33% to 60%; several high-detection peaks (SEC61G-DT, EGFR-AS1, etc.) are back in the top-1000 as they were pre-v10. Deliverables: self-contained interactive HTML viewer with 15 cell-type tabs, per-peak UCSC links, per-patient fragment-density grids and per-cohort replication chips; 15 per-cell-type top-1000 TSV tables (now filtered to patient_detection_rate >= 0.60); full peak-level master score parquet (2.09M peaks x 153 columns); underlying 430-pseudobulk matrix.
title: A harmonized human glioblastoma chromatin accessibility atlas (snATAC-seq, 67 patients, 10 cohorts, ~1.65M nuclei)

summary: FAIR metadata (Schema.org, Bioschemas and MLCommons Croissant) for the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark of 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 protein crystal structures, together with the structure files (PDB and mmCIF), an in-repository snapshot of the PDB metadata of every entry, and the documentation of the label curation. The benchmark was published by Schweke et al. (2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). This package uses the curated annotation file of the benchmark authors (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces; 16 labels revised, 20 interfaces flagged ambiguous and 6 flagged for deletion). Every interface carries both the curated label and the published label ( PublishedPhysio ). See data/curation/README.md . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.

summary: The ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo community benchmark for discriminating physiological from non-physiological protein–protein interfaces (Schweke et al., Proteomics 2023) contains 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 PDB entries. We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The benchmark is described with Bioschemas/schema.org JSON-LD: every interface is annotated with its label, chains, structural features, sequence-cluster assignment, provenance and licence, and linked to the PDB structure files and to snapshots of the RCSB PDB metadata. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the source repository, and the errors found were corrected. A lightweight design removed the need for Git LFS and for duplicated metadata. The post-publication curation of the labels (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces, compared with 836 and 841 in the publication) is documented, and three entries superseded in the PDB are linked to their replacements. A reference machine-learning script with cluster-aware cross-validation is included. Data, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, with full attribution to the original work.
title: FAIRification of the ELIXIR 3D-Bioinfo Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark

summary: Raw data of the revised evaluation of the paper "Automatic Test Data Generation for RESTful APIs: A Case Study on a Governmental System". Two campaigns ran four techniques implemented in EvoMaster 6.2.0 (MIO, RANDOM, WTS, and SMARTS) in black-box mode against a local deployment of the CMDE API with fictitious records. official-6.2.0.tar.gz : main campaign, 30 blocks × 4 techniques (120 executions), 30-minute search budget. low-budget-6.2.0.tar.gz : low-budget campaign, 10 blocks × 4 techniques (40 executions), limited to 20 requests per minute. Each execution directory holds the generated test suite, EvoMaster's statistics, the coverage of each criterion, the HTTP traffic of two re-executions of the suite, and the API's logs. MANIFEST-*.txt give the SHA-256 of every file in each archive, and SHA256SUMS the SHA-256 of the archives. The API keys were replaced with REDACTED_API_KEY . The records of people in the deployment are fictitious. The code, the protocol of the campaigns, and the analysis scripts are in the replication package ( https://github.com/vilelaricardo/cmde-restapi-replication-package , archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22112783 ). To reproduce the analysis, extract the archives and set CMDE_DATA to the extracted directory (see analysis/jss-revision/README.md in the package).
title: Raw data of the 2026 campaigns: automatic test data generation for the CMDE RESTful API (EvoMaster 6.2.0)

summary: This article develops a mathematical reconstruction of a conceptual proposal called the fixed attractor. The proposal starts from a question in the philosophy of social order: why do human societies repeatedly produce forms of cooperation and coordination without converging either to a permanently unified condition or to uninterrupted, system-wide disintegration? The article approaches this question through a deliberately limited dialogue between Qur’anic concepts and stochastic dynamical systems. Five conceptual motifs are examined: persistent human difference (ikhtilaf ), countervailing action (daf ), a boundary or separator (barzakh), the regularity of social processes (sunnat Allah), and the presence of morally exceptional minorities. These motifs are treated as interpretive prompts for model construction, not as mathematical theorems contained verbatim in scripture. The formal model describes a vector of normalized social indicators evolving in an open, bounded state space. Its drift combines mean-reverting forces with cross-domain coupling; its diffusion is state-dependent and vanishes at the boundary; and its finite-activity jump component represents shocks whose state-dependent impact preserves the interior. The article corrects and makes explicit several conditions that are necessary for the model to work: uniform inward-pointing drift at every face of the state domain, a stable coupling matrix, and a jump map that preserves the domain. Under these assumptions, a logarithmic barrier function establishes non-attainment of the boundary in finite time. Additional Lyapunov, Feller, and irreducibility conditions yield existence and uniqueness of an invariant probability distribution. When the drift is centered and the jump marks have zero mean, the invariant mean equals the model’s interior reference point, while non-degenerate interior diffusion produces persistent stationary variation. A three-dimensional example is specified for political, economic, and cultural indicators. A reproducible Euler–Maruyama/compound-Poisson experiment, reconstructed from the supplied source manuscript with a consistent parameter matrix, gives illustrative sample means close to the reference point and non-zero dispersion. These computations verify the numerical behavior of the chosen model implementation; they do not constitute empirical evidence that actual societies obey it. summary: Freestanding thin films of quantum materials naturally develop sub-micrometer, nonuniform strain fields that strongly affect their electronic, magnetic, and structural properties in both equilibrium and nonequilibrium conditions. However, current methods to quantitatively resolve these mesoscopic features are primarily restricted to scanning probes, making it challenging for dynamical measurements such as single-shot imaging and femtosecond microscopy. Here, we present a new computational framework which we denote as bend contour electron tomography (BCET), which efficiently converts bend contours in transmission electron microscope images into quantitative two-dimensional maps of strain and topography. By iteratively minimizing a designed loss function between experimental and simulated bend contour images, BCET retrieves both surface morphology and in-plane strain tensor fields without requiring scanning or diffraction mapping. We applied BCET to freestanding SrTiO 3 thin films, demonstrating the successful reconstruction of the local strain distribution and curvature field with high fidelity. Our approach provides a quantitative framework for characterizing mesoscale structures in freestanding films using wide-field imaging, opening new avenues to investigate how spatial inhomogeneity governs phase transitions and nonequilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

summary: This record provides the derived dataset, analysis code snapshot, and complete supporting analysis archive for research on recorded wildfire fireline outcomes. The retained dataset contains 304,143 fireline units from 381 fires in 2020–2024. Each unit contains at most 250 m of total mapped fireline length. Recorded outcomes comprise 205,926 Held units and 98,217 Burned Over units. NIFC fireline records are linked with NIROPS timing evidence, weather forecasts, terrain, and vegetation. The package includes a selection audit covering 572,200 candidate fireline units, 803 designated modeling predictors, data dictionaries, evaluation folds, saved predictions, supporting results, figure-generation inputs, and the complete analysis archive. The code supports verification of saved results and reproduction of documented figures. Full reconstruction of the historical extraction and training workflow requires additional inputs described in the documentation. Fireline-unit selection was retrospective. The analyses describe relationships with recorded outcomes and do not establish the causal effect of constructing a fireline or reliability for operational suppression decisions. summary: The Kung–Traub conjecture states that the convergence order of a memoryless scalar iterative method using n evaluations of a function and its derivatives per iteration cannot exceed 2^(n−1). We prove this bound for real scalar, deterministic, causal methods with adaptive queries and partially defined rules, without requiring continuity or computability of those rules. For every total method T with budget n and every p > 2^(n−1), we construct an entire function F, real on the real axis, a simple root α, and a sequence x_m → α such that |T_F(x_m) − α| / |x_m − α|^p → +∞. The construction uses properties of Wronskians of polynomial spaces, concentration of zeros, and quantitative perturbations that preserve exactly the responses to previous queries. We also develop two formalizations of computation: a fixed-budget query model and a model of procedures with internal states and performed evaluations. We prove exact representations that preserve, within the budget under consideration, the domains of valid computations, outputs, records, and evaluation counts by derivative order. From this correspondence, we obtain the order barrier for local realizations and the real formulation of the Kung–Traub bound with the specified operational cost. The results are established for real functions and real nodes. Historical documentation: Earlier versions of this research, completed on September 17–18, 2026, together with their available provenance records, are preserved at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24147519 .
title: The Kung–Traub Conjecture for Memoryless Real Scalar Methods: Proof and Formalization of Computational Procedures

summary: Heterogeneous evidence systems frequently combine observations that differ in measurement process, provenance, semantic representation, reliability, temporal coverage, spatial resolution, and statistical dependence. Naive aggregation can consequently amplify duplicated sources, conceal systematic bias, misrepresent uncertainty, and force consensus across claims that are not genuinely comparable. This manuscript proposes Cross-Domain Evidence-Constrained State Reconstruction (CDECSR), a research architecture whose default mechanism is Provenance-Aware, Uncertainty-Preserving State Reconstruction (PAUSR). The architecture preserves four macro-stages: taxonomic and semantic anchoring; error, dependence, and reliability parameterization: triangulation, robust fusion, and contradiction management; and latent-state estimation, validation, and controlled revision. These stages are operationalized through fourteen layers. The formal framework distinguishes the underlying target state from observations and model-dependent estimates. It represents heterogeneous observations through source-specific measurement models, accounts for shared provenance and correlated errors, and treats source reliability as a conditional quantity rather than a direct measure of truth. The proposed output is a state estimate or posterior distribution accompanied by uncertainty, provenance, unresolved contradictions, assumptions, validation results, and a reproducibility record. The architecture is specified through the Conflicting Reports in an Environmental Crisis (CREC), a structured primary case in which field reports and other observations may disagree about event location, timing, intensity, extent, and progression. summary: Abstract This paper proposes the Reference-Standard Inference-to-Fact Escalation Principle (RSIFEP), a general theoretical framework for analysing how a reasonable default inference about an object, individual, event, process, model, or system may be presented with a stronger epistemic status than its available justification warrants. The framework distinguishes the basis used to construct an inference from the inference itself, the evidence supporting it, the status assigned to it, the scope within which it is. asserted, and the role it plays in an operational system. A reference standard may consist of a statistical base rate, a measure of central tendency, an operational default, a validated baseline, a normative or formal standard, or a model-based analogy. These categories are related but not interchangeable. The central proposition is conditional. A default inference may be reasonable and useful without being an established fact. A status-escalation error may arise when an inference is promoted to the status of an established fact, objective description, or necessary system condition without adequate evidential, logical, or formal warrant. Such an error does not automatically produce a contradiction, paradox, dilemma, or operational failure. Those outcomes require independent definitions and additional conditions. The paper develops a six-class reference-standard taxonomy, a formal representation of reasonable reference-standard inference, a seven-stage-or-more process architecture, a twelve-category outcome taxonomy, seven theoretical propositions, a general mathematical specification, and a research programme centred on the social-media newcomer purpose-projection case. The framework also specifies its boundaries, alternative explanations, potential falsifiers, measurement requirements, and route to empirical validation. RSIFEP is presented as a proposed theoretical contribution rather than an established uni- versal law. Its novelty, explanatory advantage, measurement validity, and domain generality remain questions for literature comparison, formal analysis, and empirical testing. Keywords: reference standards; reasonable inference; default reasoning; epistemic status; status escalation; evidential warrant; scope overextension; contradiction; paradox; system-level outcomes.

summary: This paper proposes the Representational-Operational State-Inversion Principle (ROSIP), a candidate framework for describing cases in which an internal representation assigns a state that is the formally defined inverse of a corresponding operational state, while the operational state itself need not undergo a physical reversal. The motivating case is a false awakening: a person is asleep according to an independent physiological reference while the person's dream represents the self as awake. The proposed framework generalizes this contrast by separating the operational state of a system, the internal state of its model, the represented proposition about a shared referent, the inverse relation between comparable state features, and the attribution of the represented state as current reality. The paper defines a common semantic comparison space, an involutive inverse-state mapping, a state-divergence measure, an inversion-fit score, and a gated event-classification rule. It distinguishes representational inversion from ordinary mismatch, stale information, hypothetical simulation, false reporting, and actual reversal of physical dynamics. Eight proposed mechanism stages and fourteen analytical layers organize the framework. The manuscript identifies five foundational domains, a primary sleep-science validation pro- gram, six exploratory application domains, seven testable hypotheses, alternative explanations, falsification criteria, methodological requirements, and a fourteen-stage research roadmap. The framework's central contribution is presented as a testable formalization proposal, not as an established discovery. Its explanatory value depends on construct validity, temporal alignment, reliable measurement, independent replication, and evidence of incremental value over existing explanations. summary: We compare neural networks, exact Matérn kernel regression and their combinations as emulators of a six-dimensional radiative-transfer table on the 285-band EMIT grid, and we study how their forward accuracy carries over to reflectance retrieval. Over ten partitions of 23{,}313 states, a kernel with one length scale per input reaches $0.095\%$ mean relative radiance error and a network $0.387\%$; a kernel on the concatenated hidden features of five networks reaches $0.076\%$. Forward and inverse rankings disagree. A convex stack improves on a wide feature kernel by only $0.0006$ radiance percentage points, yet its 95th-percentile reflectance error is larger at every partition, three times larger on average. We prove that on the physical domain the constrained retrieval error is at most the retrieval-weighted component error divided by the transmission, with constant one, that the rate this implies is sharp, and that errors proportional to the transmission lose no rate. The reversal persists on the physical domain of the retrieval and when every family is retrained on physically admissible targets only; on a second radiative-transfer code, whose transmissions stay away from zero outside one opaque band, it is much weaker.
title: Learned representations and kernel corrections for radiative-transfer emulation

summary: The four-component (T, I, N, F) neutrosophic representation distinguishes pure indeterminacy I from neutrality N, in addition to truth T and falsehood F. Existing neutrosophic-graph research mainly assigns uncertain values to vertices or edges and studies the resulting graph structure. This paper addresses a different problem: a fixed weighted network is given, while a (T, I, N, F) assessment is the signal carried by each vertex. A benefit-coordinate embedding converts the semantic order into the standard product order and permits graph-Laplacian methods without merging neutrality and indeterminacy. For continuous-time heat diffusion, we prove preservation of the TINF cube, semantic order, component means, complement symmetry, and a maximum principle. A weighted Dirichlet energy is shown to decay monotonically, with exponential convergence governed by the algebraic connectivity. A stable discrete-time scheme and a soft-anchor graph filter are also established. For partially observed signals, the TINF harmonic extension is characterized simultaneously as the unique Dirichlet-energy minimizer and as a convex combination of boundary assessments. This yields complement equivariance, a semantic maximum principle, nonexpansive dependence on boundary data, and an explicit topology-perturbation bound. Complement-paired TINF prototypes are then introduced for four-state semi-supervised inference. They form a regular simplex in benefit coordinates, and nearest-prototype TINF classification is proved exactly equivalent to classical multiclass harmonic label propagation when anchors use the prototypes. In contrast, a symmetric three-component collapse makes neutrality and pure indeterminacy non-identifiable. An exact cycle example and Monte Carlo stochastic-block experiments confirm the equivalence numerically and demonstrate the information loss caused by collapse. The framework provides a mathematically auditable route for propagating four-component information over social, sensor, and knowledge networks.
title: TINF Signals on Networks: Complement-Equivariant Graph Diffusion, Harmonic Extension, and Semi-Supervised Inference

summary: Purpose This record documents a two-sample summary-data Mendelian randomization study designed to test whether genetic liability to cirrhosis, and to liver fibrosis, is causally related to cardiovascular disease. People with fibrotic liver disease carry a substantial excess of cardiovascular events, but whether that excess reflects a direct vascular effect of fibrosis or the metabolic disturbance that accompanies it is difficult to separate in observational data, where both are entangled with shared risk factors and with reverse causation. The study uses common genetic variants as instruments to break that entanglement, and asks two questions in sequence: whether the exposure is causally associated with five cardiovascular outcomes, and, if the association is absent or heterogeneous, which component of the exposure carries such association as exists. Contents The deposit holds the complete analytical record rather than selected outputs. It comprises 44 analysis scripts; 6 typesetting scripts retained for transparency but not runnable in isolation; 105 analysis-ready input files derived from public summary statistics, including a rebuilt LD score panel; 56 result files, one per analysis; the thirteen numbered tables of the companion article as CSV, with a companion legends file; Figures 1–3 as submitted; and a manifest giving dataset provenance for each of the eleven source datasets, a file-level inventory with SHA-256 checksums, a crosswalk between pipeline and article table numbering, and the recorded software environment. ANALYSIS_PLAN.md is the English rendering of the study protocol, together with a record of how each provision was implemented and a twelve-item register of departures from that protocol. Two of those departures, and two analyses added after first submission, are documented there rather than left implicit in the code. Methods Instruments were constructed from eleven public datasets — ten studies from the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog and one FinnGen release — for cirrhosis liability as the primary exposure and liver fibrosis as the replication exposure, against coronary artery disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ischaemic stroke and arterial stiffness, with four metabolic traits considered as candidate mediators. Estimates were obtained from six estimators: inverse-variance weighted with multiplicative random effects, MR-Egger with SIMEX correction, weighted median, weighted mode, MR-PRESSO and the contamination mixture. These are read alongside Cochran's Q and I²_GX, leave-one-out analysis, reverse-direction Mendelian randomization, overlap correction by MRlap, multivariable Mendelian randomization with conditional F statistics, two-step mediation, stratification by each variant's effect on LDL cholesterol, and colocalisation by coloc.abf . A positive control, LDL cholesterol against coronary disease, is included to show that the pipeline recovers a known effect. Use Three entry points are supported, at increasing cost. A published estimate can be checked from the deposited harmonised per-variant effects alone, without any download, by passing four columns to the estimator functions in mrlib.py . Every numbered table can be regenerated from the deposited results with a single script; the regenerated sources for the two tables carrying the primary estimates were verified byte-identical to those that produced the submitted tables. A full re-run from raw data is possible once the third-party summary statistics are placed under data/ in accordance with the registry in datasets.py , from which the driver run_all.py executes the stages in order. Every stochastic estimator is seeded and its resampling counts are fixed, so a re-run reproduces the deposited numbers exactly rather than within Monte Carlo error. Reuse and value The deposit is constructed to be reusable beyond the study that produced it. mrlib.py implements each estimator from its published description and is self-contained, so
title: Genetic Liability to Cirrhosis and Cardiovascular Disease: A Mendelian Randomization Study of Dyslipidemia, Not Fibrosis

summary: The YiPEE cluster-randomised controlled trial was conducted in Chennai, India, in 2024-2025 evaluating a school-based intervention aiming to improve adolescent mental health and well-being. This dataset includes quantitative data from 30 schools with approximately 2,800 seventh grade students. Baseline and endline data were collected using pen and paper surveys. Variables include adolescents' self-reported anxiety and depression symptoms, suicide thoughts and behaviors, scales on well-being, school cohesion, hope, gratitude, belonging, resilience, connectedness, and school kindness. There is also data from approximately 200 teachers at baseline and endline which includes self-reported well-being. Cross-sectional data was collected from school-going adolescents in seventh grade in Stockholm, Sweden in 2025. Variables include symptoms of anxiety and depression, suicide thoughts and behaviors, scales on well-being, hope, belonging, and participation. Cross-sectional data was collected from 373 school-going adolescents in Nairobi, Kenya in 2025. Students ages 12-15 years completed pen-and-paper questionnaires on well-being, connectedness, gratitude, school kindness, hope, resilience, self-esteem and school climate.  Data access: Data are available upon request and will be made publicly available once the articles using the data are published.
title: Data for: Youth co-Production for sustainable Engagement and Empowerment in health (YiPEE)

summary: Human dermo-epidermal skin equivalents (DE) comprising  in vitro  expanded autologous keratinocytes and fibroblasts are a good option for massive burn treatment. However, the lengthy expansion time required to obtain sufficient surface to cover an extensive burn together with the challenging surgical procedure limits their clinical use. The integration of DE and biodegradable scaffolds has been proposed in an effort to enhance their mechanical properties. Here, it is shown that poly(hydroxybutyrate) electrospun scaffolds (PHB) present good biocompatibility both  in vitro  and  in vivo  and are superior to poly-ε-caprolactone electrospun scaffolds as a substrate for skin reconstruction. Implantation of PHB scaffolds in healthy rats polarized macrophages to an M2-type that promoted constructive  in vivo remodelling. Moreover, implantation of DE-PHB composites in a NOD/SCID mouse xenograft model resulted in engraftment accompanied by an increase in angiogenesis that favoured the survival of the human graft. Thus, PHB scaffolds are an attractive substrate for further exploration in skin reconstruction procedures, probably due in part to their greater angiogenic and M2 macrophage polarization properties
tags: poly(hydroxybutyrate); electrospinning; skin equivalents; human skin xenograft
title: Electrospun poly(hydroxybutyrate) scaffolds promote engraftment of human skin equivalents via macrophage M2 polarization and angiogenesis
