summary: A companion paper argued that biological memory is a record that is rewritten by its own consultation, and wrote this as a readout-write channel that preserves the index of a record and revises its content. That treatment assumed the codes addressing different records do not overlap, which is the one assumption the distributed, superposed memories of the holographic lineage never make. We relax it. In a mushroom-body layer where odour codes overlap, every write has the same form, addressed by the code of the record being read, and one line of algebra gives an identity: the change a revision of record a produces in the readout of record b is the code overlap times the change it produces in a. Because training is a write of that form too, the fraction of a revision that transfers to b and the fraction of training that generalises to b are the same number, and it cancels. The prediction has no free parameter and no measurement of overlap: transfer of revision equals generalisation of training. Four consequences follow. Leakage splits into a term set by mean overlap and a term set by the fluctuation in overlap that does not fall with sparseness, so there is a floor at a coding level of 1/√N, about two per cent in the fly. Trading read noise against leakage gives an optimal coding level that falls as the revision load rises. Leakage inherits the window of the companion paper, so a record can be protected by timing alone. And in the quantum layer, index invariance turns out to be a conservation law, one charge per record, belonging to an abelian symmetry of the channel; overlap breaks that symmetry, and the index charge moves only at second order in the overlap while content moves at first, so the objectivity result degrades more slowly than the content does. We then show that the two classic results that look like confinement, synapse-specific reconsolidation and the protection of indirectly reactivated memories, are both compatible with leakage, because neither tests two records that share synapses. The fly is where that case can be tested, and we give the experiment, its controls and its power.   Spanish version included in this record: "Lo que toca una revisión: reescritura en la lectura en una memoria superpuesta". The English version is the reference text.
title: What a Revision Touches: Rewrite-on-Read in a Superposed Memory

summary: Text, measurements, and actions reveal fragments of processes that continue beyond each observation. Life Simulation proposes learning to construct and refine numerical accounts of evolving worlds, across people, economies, institutions, and environments. Construction begins with coarse histories and progressively opens finer detail. World histories teach how worlds develop; construction histories teach how to model them: which categories to invent, where to open detail, and when to revise explanations. Trained learners would then help construct their next training corpus. Conceptual shares compare categories under declared questions; measured and inferred empirical quantities retain units and uncertainty. The Meaning Model is the shared representation connecting these histories with text, concepts, visual tracks, and expressed understanding. Narrative-world construction is the first controlled laboratory, not the scope limit. The Book of Conditions has been built twice through this method, once under the author's direction and once by an agent; the numerical dependence of both remains untested. Proposed tests ask whether numerical histories shape generation, whether process histories improve prospective prediction beyond matched controls, and whether learning from construction histories improves the next corpus and the learner trained on it. Success would motivate reconstructing existing books and historical accounts, toward one connected representation of world history and all texts. This includes discovering new processes and recovering quantitative histories not explicitly recorded. Training aims to develop a process sensorium: a learned ability to infer, track, and simulate change, supporting problem solving and whole-life understanding during conversation. The recommended alignment treatment integrates care during pretraining. Life Simulation aims to deepen understanding of people's wants, needs, and circumstances. Under Entangled Alignment, the model acts as a Reader whose interpretations begin with seven stable first-person ethical commitments, the Core, throughout the corpus. The aim is to develop care alongside capability and retain that orientation through self-improvement. Evidence, inference, and invention remain distinct. Generative utility does not establish real-world accuracy or alignment; learning and safety benefits remain to be demonstrated.
title: Life Simulation: Learning from Worlds and Their Construction

summary: BOTANICAL SHEET-MASK SCIENCE: FROM SERUM CHEMISTRY TO VERIFIED WET CONTACT F121-F125 | Family 25 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch | 33 x STARLI | Edition v1.0 / November 2026 Five integrated nonclinical research themes: storage marker integrity, lyocell sorption, three-dimensional wet contact, mass-based evaporation and qualified reconstructed-epidermis evidence. Scope and scientific authority This long-form technical notebook is a proposed investigation, not a laboratory or cosmetic product performance report. The primary source is the 817-page STARLI Botanical Master Blueprint v1.0, Family25 F121-F125; older Mothers F12 and F28 provide method and evidence constraints. The numerical charts are synthetic hypotheses. Chinese materia medica inspires provenance, processing and compound questions, not a biological proof. Claims about a commercial sheet mask, sensitive-skin suitability and humans would need independent ethically and legally appropriate evidence. Five different objects, five different vetoes F121 - Botanical Sheet-Mask Serum Active Stability at the Limit. Native measurement: stored mask-serum marker retention (%). Fair reference: equal-formula serum stored in an inert vessel, blank lyocell, matched nonwoven mask and light/dark paired packaging. Disqualifying rival: adsorption onto cellulose, packaging migration, altered extract recovery, optical co-elution or oxygen-driven degradation. F122 - Lyocell–Botanical Serum Adsorption at the Limit. Native measurement: identified botanical marker adsorbed on lyocell (mg/g). Fair reference: matched nonwoven material, no-sheet serum reservoir, same-area inert substrate and prewetted lyocell control. Disqualifying rival: surface liquid mistaken for bonded sorbate, unequal sheet density, incomplete desorption or retained marker counted as delivered. F123 - Botanical Mask Conformability and Liquid Distribution at the Limit. Native measurement: verified face-surface wet-contact area (cm2). Fair reference: shape-matched nonwoven mask, same-serum container exposure, equal-load flat phantom and reversed sheet orientation. Disqualifying rival: pressure shadows mistaken for contact, pixel threshold bias, droplet pooling in folds or high contact area with low local transfer. F124 - Botanical Mask Wear Time and Evaporation at the Limit. Native measurement: evaporation mass flux (g/m2/h). Fair reference: no-sheet serum film, humidity-matched nonwoven, impermeable occlusive reference and evaporation-free gravimetric blank. Disqualifying rival: short-term occlusion masquerades as barrier repair, variable wet area, edge leakage or ambient humidity drift. F125 - Botanical Nano-Sheet-Mask Sensitive-Skin Tolerability at the Limit. Native measurement: qualified reconstructed epidermis viability (%) and marker exposure (microg/cm2). Fair reference: same-contact-time matched serum alone, blank lyocell, nonwoven sheet with matched vehicle and qualified positive-irritant reference. Disqualifying rival: pigmented botanicals distort viability reagent, local occlusion hides evaporation, tissue necrosis mimics reduced flux or uncontrolled dose. Methodological sources and foundations Five independent scientific identities under one mask F121 tests marker retention through storage without confusing cellulose sorption with degradation. F122 resolves lyocell-bound and freely available serum markers. F123 measures the genuine 3D wet-contact area and spatial transfer rather than a photographic silhouette. F124 reconstructs evaporation by mass, time, true area and environmental gradients. F125 tests qualified RhE viability only with chemically verified exposure, matched vehicle and cell-free interference controls. None of the five outputs substitutes for another. F121: chemical stability versus package partition A marker lost from the liquid phase may reside inside lyocell, on packaging film, in a precipitate or as a true degradation product. The difference is decisive. I

summary: BOTANICAL PLANT PEPTIDE BLENDS AT THE LIMIT F111-F115 | Family 23 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: authenticated peptide HPLC retention, reversible polyphenol binding, carrier protease protection, degradation half-life and qualified reconstructed-tissue evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F111-F115; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of source-resolved peptide, carrier and nonclinical evidence F111 - Plant Peptide Extraction Stability at the Limit: primary endpoint sequence-resolved HPLC peptide retention (%). Fair comparator: authenticated free peptide, dark isothermal batch, deoxygenated vehicle and equal-solvent extraction control. Disqualifying counterexample: chromatographic coelution, peptide sequence substitution, oxygen/photo stress confounding and extraction-matrix suppression. F112 - Plant Peptide-Botanical Polyphenol Binding at the Limit: primary endpoint chemically verified peptide-polyphenol bound fraction (%). Fair comparator: free peptide, polyphenol alone, no-polyphenol equal-carrier control and fixed total-solute mixed vehicle. Disqualifying counterexample: irreversible aggregate precipitation, filtration surface loss, fluorescence self-quenching or polymer viscosity artifacts. F113 - Botanical Peptide Nanocarrier Protection at the Limit: primary endpoint parent peptide survival after external protease challenge (%). Fair comparator: free peptide, surface-spiked empty carrier, blank carrier with enzyme, and matched no-enzyme reference. Disqualifying counterexample: inhibited protease masquerading as protection, peptide surface adsorption, incomplete fractionation or analytical recovery loss. F114 - Plant Peptide Enzymatic Degradation Control at the Limit: primary endpoint peptide degradation half-life (h) under a qualified protease assay. Fair comparator: matched protease without carrier, heat-inactivated protease, intact free peptide and equal-matrix blank. Disqualifying counterexample: enzyme inactivation, substrate depletion, product detector saturation, adsorption loss or photochemical decay mistaken for proteolysis. F115 - Skin Compatibility Evidence for Botanical Peptide Blends at the Limit: primary endpoint qualified RhE tissue viability (%) and separately specified irritation surrogate. Fair comparator: vehicle-matched blank, peptide-free carrier, free peptide, polyphenol-free equal carrier and validated irritant reference. Disqualifying counterexample: colored peptide assay interference, tissue nonviability, contact occlusion, vehicle osmolality or cytokine nonspecificity. Methodological introduction F111: sequence-resolved chromatographic stability A single HPLC retention value can hide amino-acid sequence substitution, peak coelution or instrument suppression. The candidate experiment begins with parent-specific peptide LC-MS/MS fragments, assigned oxidation products, matched dark and isothermal comparisons, oxygen monitoring and complete extraction recovery. The critical falsifying world contains a stable-looking HPLC signal while the true peptide has already fragmented. Source and analytical identities must be separable before a stability claim is meaningful. F113: nanocarrier protection demands an active enzyme A peptide retained after protease exposure can appear protected because a shell excludes protease or because the carrier poisons the enzyme. The difference is decisive. External pr

summary: In the loop-erased ant process of Kious, Mailler and Schapira, ants walk in turn from a nest $N$ to a food source $F$ on a finite graph, and each ant reinforces the loop-erasure of its time-reversed trajectory. Kious, Mailler and Schapira conjectured that the weight of an edge grows linearly exactly when the edge lies on a geodesic from $N$ to $F$. Let $G_\ell$ consist of a triangle $N,u,v$ and two paths of $\ell$ edges, from $u$ to $F$ and from $v$ to $F$. On $G_\ell$ the normalised weights converge almost surely, and the limit on the edge $uv$ is $(1-1/\ell)\rho(1-\rho)$ for a non-degenerate random variable $\rho$ with values in $(0,1)$. For $\ell\ge2$ this edge lies on no geodesic, so the conjecture fails; for $\ell=1$, the losange, the edge dies. The same statements hold for the forward-loop-erased process of Armfield and Mailler, which has the same law.
title: A non-geodesic edge that survives in the loop-erased ant process

summary: Companion deposit for the conference paper "One Coefficient Is Not Enough: A Pre-specified Replication of the Impostor-Practice Effect on the CMU Keystroke Benchmark" (accepted at AICSET 2026). Killourhy and Maxion (RAID 2010) summarised impostor practice on the CMU benchmark as a single additive coefficient of +1.1 percentage points of equal-error rate in the no-update regime. This deposit re-runs their factorial design without updating — three detectors (scaled Manhattan, outlier count, Mahalanobis nearest neighbour), four training amounts, three feature sets, 51 subjects — and evaluates each of the 36 cells on 16 impostor windows spanning the eight sessions: 576 evaluations. It contains the analysis script, the result file from which every number in the paper is taken, three earlier independent reproductions that the script must match within 1e-12 before reading any cell, the pre-specified protocol (in French, validated on 13 October 2026 before measurement; dated but not lodged in a public registry), and the figure script. The computation is deterministic; a re-run reproduces the result file byte for byte. The CMU benchmark itself is NOT redistributed here. MANIFEST.tsv lists every file with its size and SHA-256; verify_manifest.py recomputes them. See README.md for the two documented differences from the internal working copies (identifiers in the protocol and the protocol file name recorded by the script; no numerical value differs). Version 1.1 adds the post-hoc sensitivity analyses reported in Section 4.6 and Table 3 of the camera-ready paper (src/km_grid_sensitivity.py and results/km_grid_sensitivity.json): a 200 000-resample bootstrap with five seeds, the unpruned-ROC EER, a random practice slope per subject, a paired-difference model, and a comparison with the predictions of Killourhy and Maxion (2010, Table 1). They were decided after peer review and amend no pre-specified reading. No code, result, protocol or figure file of version 1.0 is changed; README.md and MANIFEST.tsv are updated.
title: Impostor practice on the CMU keystroke benchmark: code, results and pre-specified protocol for a replication of Killourhy and Maxion (2010)

summary: This Zenodo archive provides files to train and evaluate machine-learning models for structural annotation of MS/MS spectra. Specifically, we provide Spectraverse, a harmonized and curated resource of publicly available MS/MS spectra. summary: GPU-native Julia framework for CT and photon-counting CT simulation, reconstruction, and quantitative spectral imaging. Provides distance-driven forward projection (with Siddon ray tracing as an alternative), polychromatic Beer-Lambert physics with vendor-realistic detector response (MC-derived LUTs for GE Gemstone scintillator and Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha CdTe), FDK, helical WFBP and hybrid iterative reconstruction, sinogram and image-domain beam-hardening correction, projection-domain dual-kVp and PCCT material decomposition (K-channel profile likelihood, Cong 2022), spectral denoising, and virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI + Grant 2014 Mono+) — all dispatching transparently across CPU, Metal, CUDA, and ROCm via AcceleratedKernels.jl.
title: BasisSimulator.jl: Open-source polychromatic CT simulation with a GPU-portable reconstruction stack

summary: Analysis code (code only; no data) for the manuscript "Where are deaths in the Republic of Korea certified with ill-defined causes, and which specific causes are recorded less often there?". Scripts build sex- and age-standardised expected deaths for ill-defined causes of death (ICD-10 R00-R99) in 229 districts, 2011-2024, run pre-specified substitution analyses against specific causes, fit Bayesian negative binomial spatio-temporal models with R-INLA, and generate every number, table and figure in the manuscript. All source statistics are public aggregate data from Statistics Korea and other national sources; processed data are available from the author on reasonable request.
title: Ill-defined causes of death and their inverse relation with specific causes across districts of the Republic of Korea, 2011-2024: analysis code

All source statistics are public aggregate data from Statistics Korea and other national sources; processed data are available from the author on reasonable request.
title: Ill-defined causes of death and their inverse relation with specific causes across districts of the Republic of Korea, 2011-2024: analysis code

summary: BOTANICAL PLANT PEPTIDE BLENDS AT THE LIMIT F111-F115 | Family 23 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: authenticated peptide HPLC retention, reversible polyphenol binding, carrier protease protection, degradation half-life and qualified reconstructed-tissue evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F111-F115; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of source-resolved peptide, carrier and nonclinical evidence F111 - Plant Peptide Extraction Stability at the Limit: primary endpoint sequence-resolved HPLC peptide retention (%). Fair comparator: authenticated free peptide, dark isothermal batch, deoxygenated vehicle and equal-solvent extraction control. Disqualifying counterexample: chromatographic coelution, peptide sequence substitution, oxygen/photo stress confounding and extraction-matrix suppression. F112 - Plant Peptide-Botanical Polyphenol Binding at the Limit: primary endpoint chemically verified peptide-polyphenol bound fraction (%). Fair comparator: free peptide, polyphenol alone, no-polyphenol equal-carrier control and fixed total-solute mixed vehicle. Disqualifying counterexample: irreversible aggregate precipitation, filtration surface loss, fluorescence self-quenching or polymer viscosity artifacts. F113 - Botanical Peptide Nanocarrier Protection at the Limit: primary endpoint parent peptide survival after external protease challenge (%). Fair comparator: free peptide, surface-spiked empty carrier, blank carrier with enzyme, and matched no-enzyme reference. Disqualifying counterexample: inhibited protease masquerading as protection, peptide surface adsorption, incomplete fractionation or analytical recovery loss. F114 - Plant Peptide Enzymatic Degradation Control at the Limit: primary endpoint peptide degradation half-life (h) under a qualified protease assay. Fair comparator: matched protease without carrier, heat-inactivated protease, intact free peptide and equal-matrix blank. Disqualifying counterexample: enzyme inactivation, substrate depletion, product detector saturation, adsorption loss or photochemical decay mistaken for proteolysis. F115 - Skin Compatibility Evidence for Botanical Peptide Blends at the Limit: primary endpoint qualified RhE tissue viability (%) and separately specified irritation surrogate. Fair comparator: vehicle-matched blank, peptide-free carrier, free peptide, polyphenol-free equal carrier and validated irritant reference. Disqualifying counterexample: colored peptide assay interference, tissue nonviability, contact occlusion, vehicle osmolality or cytokine nonspecificity. Methodological introduction F111: sequence-resolved chromatographic stability A single HPLC retention value can hide amino-acid sequence substitution, peak coelution or instrument suppression. The candidate experiment begins with parent-specific peptide LC-MS/MS fragments, assigned oxidation products, matched dark and isothermal comparisons, oxygen monitoring and complete extraction recovery. The critical falsifying world contains a stable-looking HPLC signal while the true peptide has already fragmented. Source and analytical identities must be separable before a stability claim is meaningful. F113: nanocarrier protection demands an active enzyme A peptide retained after protease exposure can appear protected because a shell excludes protease or because the carrier poisons the enzyme. The difference is decisive. External pr

summary: Technical Report S-A-R-v2.2-ORIGIN traces the historical genealogy and software engineering architecture of Curriculum-as-Code (CaC) across three distinct generations (2018–2026) and establishes the canonical S-A-R Standard v2.2 (Scalable / Auditable / Repeatable) reference architecture deployed across higher education and clinical kinesiology / nutrition cohorts. Generation 1 (2018–2020) originated in network infrastructure emulation (NRE Labs / Antidote Kubernetes container laboratories), proving that interactive technical instruction could be version-controlled in Git and compiled reproducibly. Generation 2 (2021–2024) adapted plain-text Single Sources of Truth (Markdown / LaTeX), early GitHub AI Co-Pilot workflows, Python federal data APIs, and Continuous Integration (CI/CD) pipelines to public planning and open textbooks—demonstrating version control and accessible HTML generation while remaining limited to flat document trees without pedagogical graph semantics or civil-rights compliance gates. Generation 3 (2025–2026, S-A-R Standard v2.2 — originated by Alan Lee Pruitt at Webcognita LLC and Arizona Western College) advances Curriculum-as-Code from flat Docs-as-Code into neuro-symbolic clinical pedagogy and upstream Compliance-as-Code. The architecture unites: (1) a 3,265-node DOM GraphRAG knowledge graph preserving heading hierarchy, learning outcomes, and primary federal Sources of Truth (HHS PAGA 2018 2nd Ed., 2025–2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans, ACSM 12th Ed., NASM OPT, and U.S. DOL ETA Advisory TEN No. 07-25 AI Literacy); (2) W3C PROV-O SHA-256 cryptographic provenance receipts and W3C SKOS bilingual (English / Norteño-Spanish) clinical ontologies; (3) automated pre-commit ADA Title II (28 CFR Part 35), WCAG 2.2 AA (9:1 Double-Contrast Guard), and WCAG 3.0 APCA accessibility linters verified at 0 open issues across 419+ production Canvas LMS pages; and (4) air-gapped Apple Silicon Edge AI inference preserving 100% FERPA and HIPAA data sovereignty under The Centaur Protocol and The Clinical Framing Protocol (Pattern / Rule / Solve).   Canonical Web Edition: https://alanpruitt.com/curriculum-as-code/ Institutional & Federal Partner Portal: https://www.webcognita.com/
title: From Infrastructure Automation to Clinical Pedagogy: The Origin and Evolution of Curriculum-as-Code (2018–2026)

summary: This record contains the Python analysis scripts, generated CSV data files, and environment specification used in the manuscript "Feasibility Bounds and Uncertainty Breakdown Near the Effectiveness Limit in Shell-and-Tube Exchangers" by Majid Esfandiari and Mustafa Omranshobi. Contents: - run_analysis.py: generates the agreement loci and area fractions (Fig. 2, Tables 1–3) - verify_levelA.py: verifies the effectiveness relation against the numerical ODE solution (Table 4) - uncertainty_compare.py: performs the Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis (Tables 6–9, Fig. 3) - ntu_crossflow_screening.py: compares cross-flow effectiveness relations for the Kang et al. measured case (Table 10) - fthx_model_margins.py: calculates the loose bounds from the reported effectiveness range - fig1.py: generates the schematic of the one-shell-pass/two-tube-pass exchanger (Fig. 1) - Generated CSV files corresponding to the tables and figures in the manuscript - requirements.txt: Python package versions - README.md: brief instructions for reproducing the results The Monte Carlo analysis uses 4 × 10^5 realizations per point with seed 7. This record is deposited to support reproducibility; the manuscript itself is not included in this record.

summary: This software and selected-data release accompanies the manuscript “ Symmetry defects and state-dependent order reduction in Fourier Laplace–rotation splitting ” by Fei Xue and Tianqi Zhang. Version 2.0.0 substantially extends the previous scalar MATLAB release (v1.1.0, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23151617) to provide a unified reproducibility package for scalar and spinor Bose–Einstein condensate dynamics. The package includes: MATLAB implementations of three-dimensional rotational BEC solvers, including explicit Laplace–rotation integrators, merged compact splitting, and full-step forward–method-adjoint (FB) constructions, together with scalar and spinor model components. Python verification tools for the seven-factor (EEI7) and five-operator (EEI5) symmetry-defect certificates, selected spinor subflows, and independent numerical reference calculations. Numerical benchmarks and selected data , including a small-grid matrix-exponential reference test, accuracy-versus-work comparisons, and arbitrary-axis rotation experiments examining the dependence of defect visibility on spatial resolution. Reproducibility documentation , including execution instructions, validation records, file provenance, version comparisons, and SHA-256 checksums. The associated manuscript establishes rigorous fixed-grid symmetry-defect results, analyzes their state-dependent visibility, and develops an adjoint-based implementation that restores the designed temporal order under the stated assumptions. The software provides numerical verification and reproducible examples supporting this analysis. Scope and limitations: The small-grid reference benchmark and selected verification tests have been rerun for this release. Historical large-grid MATLAB production experiments have not been rerun, and some historical terminal-state arrays are not redistributed. The documentation distinguishes independently verified results, archived computations, and derived data. The Python certificate tests are numerical cross-checks rather than substitutes for the mathematical proofs. This release supersedes the scalar-only software distribution while preserving the earlier version in the Zenodo version history.

summary: Replication package for the article "Example Scenarios, Random Sequences or Contract-Guided Exploration? Testing a Stateful Learning Agreement Service with Language Model Implementations, Seeded Faults and Blind Test Suites" (I. Tiievskyi). The study compares three black-box testing techniques on an executable contract of a learning agreement revision service inspired by the Erasmus Without Paper (EWP) Outgoing Mobility Learning Agreements workflow: example scenarios (EX), random request sequences (RND) and contract-guided breadth-first exploration (SYS). The package contains everything needed to rerun the experiments and recompute the reported numbers. Contents - contract/: the executable contract (ten obligations), a description of which parts of the EWP workflow it covers, the reference implementation REF with ten dependent faults, the fourteen example scenarios (EX) and unit tests. - study/impl_I1, study/impl_I2, study/i3: five implementations in total – REF plus I1 (Python) and I2 (Node.js) written from the contract and interface only, and I3 and I4 written by two further language models from the same brief; implementers' notes on ambiguities and file hashes. - study/faults, study/mutants_ext: 40 seeded mutants (F01–F10, G01–G10, GM01–GM10, PM01–PM10) with their catalogue, exact edits, revealing sequences and seeding briefs. - study/human_faults: ten faults (H01–H10) written by a backend developer without AI tools, together with the task sheet stating the inclusion criteria. - study/blind: ten example suites written by six language models from the contract text alone, the writers' brief, the pre-registered evaluation harness with its hashes, the corrected harness and the results before and after the correction. - study/harness, study/controls, study/robustness: the test bench (EX, RND, SYS, differential oracle), the black-box contract observer, oracle and budget controls, the census of disagreements between implementations, observation-level, pruning, hash-seed and fault-mechanism analyses, and regression tests of the scenario comparator. - Raw results (JSON) for every reported table; README.md maps each table of the article to the script and result file that produce it. Requirements and use Python 3.11 or later and Node.js 18 or later, standard libraries only, no network access. Each script is run from its own folder; a run of 20,000 requests takes about 5 seconds. README.md gives quick checks, the exact commands for the full blind-suite run and the census reproduction, and the random seeds used (RND seeds 1–5, 1–10 for the dependent faults, census seed 1, PYTHONHASHSEED 0 for the robustness analyses). Version 1.1 The census of disagreements now draws the request selected from history from a local generator initialised with the census seed, so the census is fully reproducible. All ten pairwise census runs were repeated; the sets of disagreements and the first detection of each point reported in Table 5 are unchanged. The version 1.0 census results are kept in study/census_v1.0. The main mutant and blind-suite runs are not affected by this change. Provenance The contract, the reference implementation, the example scenarios, the dependent faults, the harness and the analysis scripts were prepared by the author with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5). I1, I2 and F01–G10 were written by isolated Claude Opus 5.5 agents without access to the tests; I3, I4, GM01–GM10 and PM01–PM10 by GPT 6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon from the same briefs; the blind suites by Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2, GPT 6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon. The archived briefs cover the blind suites, I3/I4, the GM/PM mutants and the developer task; full agent and chat transcripts are not included. The developer agreed to the publication of the faults. Integrity SHA256SUMS lists the SHA-256 checksum of every file in the package (sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS in the package root).
title: Replication package: Example Scenarios, Random Sequences or Contract-Guided Exploration? Testing a Stateful Learning Agreement Service

summary: POLYPHENOL-LIPID COUPLING SCIENCE F096-F100 | Family 20 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: molecular interface binding, oil-peroxide kinetics, polyphenol redox depletion, genuine lipid nanocarrier co-loading, and nonclinical barrier/viability evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F096-F100; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of polyphenol-lipid-botanical causation F096 - Botanical Polyphenol-Lipid Interfacial Binding at the Limit: primary endpoint apparent binding constant K_app (L/mol). Fair comparator: free polyphenol alone, free oil/lipid alone, missing-component mixtures and matched blank liposomes. Disqualifying counterexample: surface adsorption, self-quenching, polyphenol autoxidation, incomplete recovery or bilayer disruption masquerading as molecular binding. F097 - Botanical Polyphenol-Plant Oil Antioxidant Coupling at the Limit: primary endpoint plant-oil peroxide formation rate (meq peroxide/kg oil per h). Fair comparator: polyphenol-free oil, oil-free polyphenol, matched vehicle, dark isothermal control and tocopherol reference. Disqualifying counterexample: autooxidation, probe quenching, transient induction-period selection or peroxide breakdown without suppressed secondary oxidation. F098 - Lipid Oxidation and Botanical Polyphenol Activity at the Limit: primary endpoint slope of polyphenol depletion versus lipid oxidation (prespecified native units). Fair comparator: unprotected oil, polyphenol without oil, oxidized-polyphenol spike and matched light-oxygen factorial controls. Disqualifying counterexample: reverse causality, time-confounded oxidation, ion suppression or antioxidant depletion without protection of the lipid phase. F099 - Botanical Polyphenol-Lipid Nano-Codelivery at the Limit: primary endpoint true co-loading fraction (%) of independently qualified polyphenol and lipid compartments. Fair comparator: free botanical in oil, empty carriers, equal-total-mass physically blended carriers and independent single-loaded formulations. Disqualifying counterexample: adsorption to particle surface, unseparated micelles, centrifugation loss or fluorescent overlap mistaken for shared nanocarrier loading. F100 - Barrier Evidence for Botanical Polyphenol-Lipid Formulations at the Limit: primary endpoint joint qualified barrier-surrogate effect and RhE viability (%), reported separately. Fair comparator: vehicle-matched control, polyphenol-only, lipid-only, blank carrier and positive reference irritant. Disqualifying counterexample: optical-probe self-quenching, surface occlusion, damaged RhE tissue, dye interference or unmatched vehicle causing false barrier evidence. Methodological introduction F096: apparent interfacial association is not proof of binding Different redox states and lipids require independent molecular identity. A change in fluorescence or oil-water partition can arise from self-quenching, adsorption or photochemical loss. An apparent binding constant must survive reversible washout, recovery checks and a separately measured lipid interface area. F098: oxidative depletion and lipid preservation are different A statistical slope between polyphenol depletion and lipid oxidation is a descriptive estimate, not a causal mechanism. Independently perturb oxygen and photon exposure, quantify oxidized parent molecules, and identify whether high-dose polyphenols can switch from inhibitory to pro-oxid

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Thirty-five entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten, a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), and a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation, a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight, and a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963), converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters, gives the absorbance template of a visual pigment of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for a peak wavelength and chromophore the caller states, and gives the distance between two colours in units of receptor noise by the model of Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), for a noise the caller states. Without a water type, it gives Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001) or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013), the remote sensing reflectance from a and bb (Gordon et al. 1988; Lee et al. 2002), and the Secchi depth from Kd and that reflectance (Lee et al. 2015), and inverts the reflectance to the absorption and backscattering coefficients by the quasi-analytical algorithm, in the version of IOCCG Report 5 (2006), checked against that report's published statistics, and as QAA_v6, checked against its author's spreadsheet. It carries four published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016) and Lee et al. (2015), for the caller to choose from
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: Markov chains for a Bayesian inverse problem with a 100-parameter Karhunen-Loeve log permeability field and an elliptic PDE, following P. G. Constantine, C. Kent and T. Bui-Thanh, "Accelerating Markov chain Monte Carlo with active subspaces", SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 38(5):A2779-A2805, 2016, doi:10.1137/15M1042127. pde_mcmc_chains.npz (load with numpy.load, no pickle) holds the synthetic data, the misfit gradients at 1000 prior samples and their active subspace, 20 random-walk Metropolis chains and 4 + 4 active-variable chains (reductions), and a grid of the misfit on the active variables. kl-short.npz is the Karhunen-Loeve basis the model uses. generate_data.py in the repository regenerates the chains from saved seeds. These files are deposited as the full-size archive of the data set uq_benchmarks/PDE_Inverse_Problem_MCMC in the as-data-sets repository ( https://github.com/paulcon/as-data-sets/tree/main/uq_benchmarks/PDE_Inverse_Problem_MCMC ), a collection of Jupyter notebooks that apply active subspaces (parameter-space dimension reduction) to science and engineering models. The notebook there analyzes these data; its DATA.md documents every file, column, unit and unknown. The repository keeps each file under 10 MB, so it ships the same arrays split into files under 10 MB. License: CC BY 4.0. Cite Constantine, Kent and Bui-Thanh (2016).
title: Markov chain Monte Carlo on the active variables of a PDE inverse problem: chains, subspace and grid

summary: BOTANICAL SHEET-MASK SCIENCE: FROM SERUM CHEMISTRY TO VERIFIED WET CONTACT F121-F125 | Family 25 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch | 33 x STARLI | Edition v1.0 / November 2026 Five integrated nonclinical research themes: storage marker integrity, lyocell sorption, three-dimensional wet contact, mass-based evaporation and qualified reconstructed-epidermis evidence. Scope and scientific authority This long-form technical notebook is a proposed investigation, not a laboratory or cosmetic product performance report. The primary source is the 817-page STARLI Botanical Master Blueprint v1.0, Family25 F121-F125; older Mothers F12 and F28 provide method and evidence constraints. The numerical charts are synthetic hypotheses. Chinese materia medica inspires provenance, processing and compound questions, not a biological proof. Claims about a commercial sheet mask, sensitive-skin suitability and humans would need independent ethically and legally appropriate evidence. Five different objects, five different vetoes F121 - Botanical Sheet-Mask Serum Active Stability at the Limit. Native measurement: stored mask-serum marker retention (%). Fair reference: equal-formula serum stored in an inert vessel, blank lyocell, matched nonwoven mask and light/dark paired packaging. Disqualifying rival: adsorption onto cellulose, packaging migration, altered extract recovery, optical co-elution or oxygen-driven degradation. F122 - Lyocell–Botanical Serum Adsorption at the Limit. Native measurement: identified botanical marker adsorbed on lyocell (mg/g). Fair reference: matched nonwoven material, no-sheet serum reservoir, same-area inert substrate and prewetted lyocell control. Disqualifying rival: surface liquid mistaken for bonded sorbate, unequal sheet density, incomplete desorption or retained marker counted as delivered. F123 - Botanical Mask Conformability and Liquid Distribution at the Limit. Native measurement: verified face-surface wet-contact area (cm2). Fair reference: shape-matched nonwoven mask, same-serum container exposure, equal-load flat phantom and reversed sheet orientation. Disqualifying rival: pressure shadows mistaken for contact, pixel threshold bias, droplet pooling in folds or high contact area with low local transfer. F124 - Botanical Mask Wear Time and Evaporation at the Limit. Native measurement: evaporation mass flux (g/m2/h). Fair reference: no-sheet serum film, humidity-matched nonwoven, impermeable occlusive reference and evaporation-free gravimetric blank. Disqualifying rival: short-term occlusion masquerades as barrier repair, variable wet area, edge leakage or ambient humidity drift. F125 - Botanical Nano-Sheet-Mask Sensitive-Skin Tolerability at the Limit. Native measurement: qualified reconstructed epidermis viability (%) and marker exposure (microg/cm2). Fair reference: same-contact-time matched serum alone, blank lyocell, nonwoven sheet with matched vehicle and qualified positive-irritant reference. Disqualifying rival: pigmented botanicals distort viability reagent, local occlusion hides evaporation, tissue necrosis mimics reduced flux or uncontrolled dose. Methodological sources and foundations Five independent scientific identities under one mask F121 tests marker retention through storage without confusing cellulose sorption with degradation. F122 resolves lyocell-bound and freely available serum markers. F123 measures the genuine 3D wet-contact area and spatial transfer rather than a photographic silhouette. F124 reconstructs evaporation by mass, time, true area and environmental gradients. F125 tests qualified RhE viability only with chemically verified exposure, matched vehicle and cell-free interference controls. None of the five outputs substitutes for another. F121: chemical stability versus package partition A marker lost from the liquid phase may reside inside lyocell, on packaging film, in a precipitate or as a true degradation product. The difference is decisive. I

summary: In the loop-erased ant process of Kious, Mailler and Schapira, ants walk in turn from a nest $N$ to a food source $F$ on a finite graph, and each ant reinforces the loop-erasure of its time-reversed trajectory. Kious, Mailler and Schapira conjectured that the weight of an edge grows linearly exactly when the edge lies on a geodesic from $N$ to $F$. Let $G_\ell$ consist of a triangle $N,u,v$ and two paths of $\ell$ edges, from $u$ to $F$ and from $v$ to $F$. On $G_\ell$ the normalised weights converge almost surely, and the limit on the edge $uv$ is $(1-1/\ell)\rho(1-\rho)$ for a non-degenerate random variable $\rho$ with values in $(0,1)$. For $\ell\ge2$ this edge lies on no geodesic, so the conjecture fails; for $\ell=1$, the losange, the edge dies. The same statements hold for the forward-loop-erased process of Armfield and Mailler, which has the same law.
title: A non-geodesic edge that survives in the loop-erased ant process

summary: BOTANICAL CERAMIDE AND BARRIER-LIPID SCIENCE F106-F110 | Family 22 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: botanical-active/ceramide precipitation, three-lipid mole-fraction order, lamellar repeat spacing, spatial delivery and viable-model water-loss evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F106-F110; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of authenticated botanical, lamellar and barrier evidence F106 - Botanical Active-Ceramide Compatibility at the Limit: primary endpoint botanical-active / ceramide precipitation fraction (%). Fair comparator: full-lipid reference, active-only, ceramide-only, matched vehicle and equal-oil nonlamellar controls. This volume preserves those sources as research-provoking intellectual history, not proof of efficacy. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F106-F110; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of authenticated botanical, lamellar and barrier evidence F106 - Botanical Active-Ceramide Compatibility at the Limit: primary endpoint botanical-active / ceramide precipitation fraction (%). Fair comparator: full-lipid reference, active-only, ceramide-only, matched vehicle and equal-oil nonlamellar controls. Disqualifying counterexample: color/turbidity interference, precipitated cholesterol, pH-triggered crystal formation, non-specific surface adsorption, pigment scattering. F107 - Ceramide-Cholesterol-Fatty Acid Ratios at the Limit: primary endpoint lamellar-order parameter (dimensionless) under defined three-lipid mole ratios. Fair comparator: matched single-lipid omissions, equimass nonlamellar dispersions and same-total-lipid reference. summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate by iteratively unmasking tokens with bidirectional attention, but rotary position embeddings (RoPE) still confine them to a fixed pretraining window. Existing training-free extrapolation, notably LongLLaDA, copies NTK-based RoPE scaling from autoregressive (AR) models and applies one static, length-only transform at every position and denoising step. That transplant ignores a signal unique to dLLMs: the evolving mask pattern of the partially decoded sequence. We propose Mask-Pattern Position Augmentation (MPPA). MPPA linearly interpolates indices into the pretrained window, then adds a per-position, per-step offset from cumulative mask density. The offset restores rotary phase resolution that interpolation collapses, and it shrinks as tokens are committed, so late steps see near-clean interpolated geometry. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct at twice its 4096-token window, MPPA reduces perplexity from 19.51 under standard decoding to 3.12 at 8192 tokens, below the in-window figure, with 100% passkey retrieval and unchanged needle-in-a-haystack accuracy. These preliminary $2\times$ results motivate mask-conditioned position engineering as a diffusion-native path to long-context generation.
title: Mask-Pattern Position Augmentation: Training-Free Long-Context Extrapolation for Diffusion LLMs

summary: We investigate a failed filament eruption and associated coronal heating in NOAA Active Region 12353 on 2015 May 23, focusing on the relationship between magnetic confinement and external reconnection. Coordinated observations from the Goode Solar Telescope and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, together with nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, allow us to trace the event from the merging of two low-lying filamentary structures to the failed eruption of the resulting elongated filament. Before the rapid rise, the modeled flux rope had entered a regime susceptible to kink instability, while low-atmospheric internal reconnection had already occurred; both may have contributed to the initial acceleration. The rising flux rope remained below the torus instability threshold and was confined by a strong, asymmetric overlying field that compressed it against the overlying loops. An elongated interface brightening, bidirectional plasmoid-like motions, newly brightened loop systems, and progressive weakening of the filament are consistent with external reconnection that changed the magnetic connectivity, removed magnetic flux from the rope, and disrupted its coherent structure. Differential emission measure analysis indicates that the external reconnection heated the active region loop system. A transient, localized structure with high-temperature emission was observed at the interaction interface, consistent with the expected location of a current sheet associated with external reconnection. These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation, enabling external reconnection to disrupt the flux rope and heat the active region loop system.
title: A Failed Filament Eruption and Associated Active Region Heating Driven by External Magnetic Reconnection

summary: Modelled LGA-week cholera surveillance series for Nigeria, 2022–2024 This dataset contains 120,744 records: 774 Nigerian local government areas (LGAs) across 37 states (36 states and the Federal Capital Territory) and six geopolitical zones, for 156 consecutive epidemiological weeks from 3 January 2022 to 29 December 2024. Each record gives the LGA identifier, name, state and zone, centroid coordinates, a weekly count of suspected cholera cases, and week and year indices. Population denominators come from the 2006 National Population Commission census and are available for 611 of the 774 LGAs (95,316 LGA-weeks). The file also holds simulated covariate columns (water, sanitation and hygiene access, flood risk, temperature, rainfall, mobility, population density and one further parameter) as supplied. Their provenance is undocumented. For selected weeks and states, the file includes state and national cases and deaths transcribed from Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) situation reports. Each transcribed value is traceable through its source and source-URL columns. Files File Content nigeria_cholera_lga_week_2022_2024_modelled.csv The dataset (UTF-8 with byte-order mark; 36 columns). Content identical to the file analysed in the manuscript, originally named nigeria_cholera_spatiotemporal_REAL_DATA_2022_2024.csv. data_dictionary.csv Description, type, unit and number of missing values for every column. code/ Python scripts for the associated analysis (Moran's I, Local Moran's I, Getis-Ord Gi*, and a Bayesian BYM2 spatiotemporal model fitted with a custom Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler). results/ Analysis outputs: exploratory_results.json, post_results.json, lga_results.csv, lga_analysis.csv, weekly.csv, table1.csv, state_year_recon.csv. figures/ The three manuscript figures (PNG). Reproducing the analysis Requires Python 3 with NumPy, SciPy, pandas and matplotlib. Put the CSV and the scripts in one folder (or set the environment variable WORKDIR to that folder), then run in this order: exploratory.py, run_chains.py (about four minutes per chain, four chains), post.py, figs12.py, fig3.py. Running exploratory.py on the packaged data reproduces results/exploratory_results.json and results/lga_analysis.csv exactly. weekly.csv, table1.csv and state_year_recon.csv were produced in an interactive step for the manuscript and have no separate script; they are supplied as outputs only. Random seeds: 20261103 (exploratory analysis) and 101, 202, 303, 404 (Bayesian chains). bym_st_v1.py (an earlier sampler version) is not included. 01_simulate_data.py  (corrected version) ======================================== Simulate weekly cholera cases for all 774 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Nigeria over a three-year (156-week) period. Output columns match the canonical file `nigeria_cholera_spatiotemporal.csv`:     lga_id, state, zone, latitude, longitude, week, year, week_of_year,     pop_density, population, wash_access, flood_risk, temperature_c,     rainfall_mm, mobility_index, beta, cholera_cases, incidence_per_100k Counts are generated conditionally as Poisson draws given a latent LGA-week rate (Equations 14-15). summary: Replication dataset and verification code for the manuscript "Split Custody and Fossilised Provenance: Cross-Regime Recordkeeping Governance Across Space-Mission Closeouts and Schema Migrations". The archive contains 36 unmodified files from the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS3 and PDS4 labels, catalog files, checksum manifests, user guides, errata and node policy pages) for the Apollo 15/17 Heat Flow Experiment, Clementine 1 Bistatic Radar, Magellan Venus GXDR and OSIRIS-REx SPICE archives; a manifest with official URLs and SHA-256 digests for the 10 policy, oversight and case documents analysed in the study (the documents themselves are not redistributed); a dependency-free Python 3 script, run_feasibility_audit.py; and its four output files. Running python3 run_feasibility_audit.py reproduces the output files byte for byte (SHA-256 digests are listed in README_Dataset.md). The script confirms that 11 of 11 PDS4 XML labels are well-formed, inventories 6,378 published MD5 manifest entries (430 in five PDS Geosciences Node manifests and 5,948 in the OSIRIS-REx checksum_v013.tab manifest), matches 22 of 22 local checksum comparisons across 21 sampled files, finds no cryptographic digital signatures in the 36 archive files, and writes the coded evidence matrix (E01 to E10) used in the manuscript. Third-party files in corpus/pds_artifacts/ are redistributed unmodified and remain subject to their original terms. The CC BY 4.0 licence applies to the script, outputs and documentation prepared for this dataset.

summary: Two partly ciphered letters (Gelders Archief, 0372 Huis Ammerzoden, inv. 52), 1614–1615, from Jean-Baptiste van Male, the Archdukes' agent in London, to his brother Abraham van Male, drost of Steenbergen. Edition of the deciphered passages, key, and historical context. Version 3 replaces version 2: the family link is confirmed from the Annuaire de la noblesse de Belgique (1865); the provenance is traced through the inventory (De la Kéthulle, Van Arkel); Abraham van Male died before March 1621; new readings in letter 2 ('chasque huict jours', 'mériter une belle chaine d'or', 'circonspect', 'het port van brieven'). Transcription and cryptanalysis were done with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).

summary: Agentic AI systems increasingly undertake extended tasks and act on people's behalf, making human-agent interaction central to their effectiveness. Successful interaction requires understanding human perspectives, coordinating complementary capabilities, and maintaining productive relationships within socio-technical environments. This paper examines how foundations developed by the Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (AAMAS) community inform these demands. We consider interactions ranging from individual human-agent partnerships to teams and larger groups, where participants differ in their roles, decision authority, capabilities, and objectives. We organize computational approaches around the connected challenges of understanding others and deciding how to interact with them. Theory of Mind, belief-desire-intention architectures, goal and plan recognition, inverse planning, and recursive reasoning provide mechanisms for representing and inferring partially observable mental states. Observer-aware planning, model reconciliation, and decision-theoretic communication connect these inferences to action, explanation, and information exchange. Together with shared autonomy, argumentation, and cooperative inverse reinforcement learning, these approaches offer foundations for agentic systems that account for evolving human knowledge, intentions, and expectations. We argue that progress requires treating human interaction as an ongoing decision problem shaped by uncertainty, interdependence, and potentially conflicting objectives.
title: Open Challenges and Opportunities in Human-Agent Systems

summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.
title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks

First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.

summary: Coordinating transmission networks, distribution networks, and microgrids enables distributed flexibility to support renewable energy integration and low-carbon operation. However, heterogeneous resources, cross-layer coupling, and varying operating requirements complicate the selection of models and coordination schemes that are both physically adequate and computationally tractable. This paper proposes TDMOpt, a LLM-driven multi-agent framework that replaces fixed modeling configurations with adaptive model composition. A layered component library provides executable network, resource, objective, constraint, and coordination models. Guided by retrieved physics and component knowledge, the agents infer specific modeling requirements and jointly select compatible components across layers according to operating conditions and computational budgets. The model compositions undergo independent AC power flow validation, since feasibility in a simplified formulation does not ensure compliance with physical network limits. A refinement mechanism interprets numerical feedback to identify modeling requirements for reconsideration and revise relevant component selections. Case studies on different scale systems illustrate the framework's ability to adapt model combinations and obtain validated dispatch solutions through targeted refinement under varying operating conditions.
title: TDMOpt: LLM-Driven Cross-layer Dispatch for Transmission-Distribution-Microgrid Systems

summary: Effective throughput, the product of raw throughput and transaction success rate, determines the useful capacity of Execute-Order-Validate blockchains such as Hyperledger Fabric. Most prior work either tunes configurations to raise raw throughput, requiring many costly redeployments, or controls conflicts to raise the success rate, repairing them only after execution with kernel modifications. The few joint approaches tune only a small set of parameters and still rely on kernel changes to resolve conflicts. To address these challenges, we present Auriga, a non-invasive framework that jointly optimizes both factors through sample-efficient LLM-guided configuration search and pre-execution conflict prevention. A harness-governed multi-agent architecture coordinates LLM agents for parameter exploration, saturation-aware evaluation, and experience consolidation, with the harness controlling tool and memory access and retaining termination authority. For transaction scheduling, an LLM extracts symbolic AST templates from smart contracts offline. At runtime, the scheduler predicts read-write sets without executing them and partitions transactions into conflict-free groups. Across three benchmarks and conflict rates up to 70%, Auriga improves effective throughput by up to 6.0 times over default Fabric and 2.0 times over the strongest baseline. The tuning agent also discovers undocumented parameter dependencies, and ablation studies show the independent contributions of both subsystems.
title: Auriga: Harness-Governed LLM Agents for Effective Throughput Optimization in Execute-Order-Validate Permissioned Blockchains

summary: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent. However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. This makes it difficult to balance localization accuracy and token cost. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Compared with individual baselines in each setting, CoLFA improves accuracy by up to 37.50% and reduces token consumption by up to 97.6%.
title: CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. This makes it difficult to balance localization accuracy and token cost. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Compared with individual baselines in each setting, CoLFA improves accuracy by up to 37.50% and reduces token consumption by up to 97.6%.
title: CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck. Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time. As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.
title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals

summary: Front-end coding agents are expected to produce applications that fulfill user goals, yet high task scores can coexist with failures in essential workflows. Evaluating these agents therefore requires an explicit distinction between partial implementation and application success. We introduce JoyFrontBench, a benchmark that makes this distinction through goal-oriented acceptance contracts. Each contract identifies core tasks and mandatory criteria before generation: a core task passes only when all mandatory criteria are satisfied and a shared completion threshold is met, while application success requires every core task to pass on the same operational artifact within a single run. Derived from practitioner requirements, JoyFrontBench comprises 100 front-end development problems, 764 tasks, and 2,596 atomic criteria, with reviewed annotations linking user goals to core tasks and evidence requirements. The evaluation framework combines evidence-grounded judgments with deterministic record auditing and fixed scoring rules, preserving graded task assessment alongside explicit core-task and application-level acceptance. We evaluate five coding models under two agent harnesses, OpenHands and OpenCode, on the 70-problem test set; the remaining 30 problems form a public set for validation and diagnostic analyses. Under OpenHands, the mean Average Task Score (ATS) across models is 87.69%, while the mean Application Success Rate (ASR) is 51.52%. Further analyses reveal changes in model rankings across harnesses and variation in application success across repeated runs. These findings highlight the limitations of aggregate task scores in characterizing application success and motivate explicit assessment of core-goal fulfillment alongside graded task performance.
title: JoyFrontBench: Evaluating Front-End Coding Agents through Goal-Oriented Acceptance Contracts

Physician-written references therefore contain both facts supported by prior clinical notes and reference-only content, potentially reflecting clinical synthesis, handoffs, or discharge planning. Reference-only evaluation can conflate failure to recover available information with failure to reproduce content absent from the model input. We introduce FairSumEval, an evidence-aware, fact-level framework that assesses whether each reference and generated fact is supported by the model's evidence and captured by the other summary. The resulting outcome map separates matches, omissions, and additions. Two complementary metrics, Soft IoU-S and Soft IoU-NS, measure reference-generation agreement for facts with and without identified evidence support. On 200 MIMIC-III admissions, 18.8% of physician reference facts have identified support in the prior evidence, compared with 65.4% and 63.5% of facts generated by a general-purpose and a medically specialized model. Overlap is substantially higher for supported content (0.255 and 0.236) than for content without identified support (0.030 and 0.026). The two scores are weakly correlated across admissions (rho = 0.22 and 0.17), and conventional metrics do not consistently capture both dimensions. FairSumEval distinguishes evidence-grounded summarization from agreement on content without identified support, revealing what models omit and add in each category.

summary: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. Evaluating three models across four data-context settings shows that the benchmarks separate data contexts and model tiers. Auditing candidate queries against causal provenance in the simulation log verifies gold programs without manual annotation, including on multi-event composite tasks that expose reasoning failures in state-of-the-art agents. We hope the community uses SynthCorp to generate more challenging and useful data estates and benchmarks that foster the development of enterprise data agents.

summary: We show that cyclic fatigue can occur in a system whose elements behave elastically up to an irreversible failure threshold, without plasticity, friction, or any time-dependent process. The model represents a weak interface between two elastic bodies loaded in shear. Under sufficiently large cyclic loading below the static failure threshold, a pre-existing flaw advances progressively, by a few lattice spacings per cycle. Two conditions are needed for this behavior: each bond fails more easily under one sense of the shear than the opposite, and the shear must be reversed during the cycle by an amount large enough to break bonds that have not yet failed. The model thus identifies the minimal conditions for an intrinsic, plasticity-free fatigue mechanism. Such conditions may be met at interfaces and weak planes subjected to strongly reversed shear, as in fretting, rolling contact, and reversed torsion, or in cyclic shear of cemented granular materials.
title: Fatigue crack growth without plasticity under cyclically reversed shear

DOI: https://doi.org/ 10.5281/zenodo.24029484 Received: 24 September 2026, Revised: 10 October 2026, Accepted: 31 October 2026, Online First:   13 November 2026 ABSTRACT Anorectal malformations (ARMs) are a spectrum of disease affecting rectum, anal canal and genito-urinary canal. ARM is also the leading cause of intestinal obstruction in the neonatal period [1, 2]. Paediatric age group along with various syndromes like VACTREL association in combination with laparoscopic approach for the correction of ARM pose unique challenges to anaesthesiologists, of which the presence of spinal dysraphism is particularly important as the analgesia in paediatric age group relies on neuraxial techniques like caudal block. Furthermore, providing adequate and sustained perioperative analgesia can be challenging due to the prolonged duration of surgery, involvement of both abdominal and perineal surgical fields, and limitations associated with conventional single-shot neuraxial techniques. We present a case of 3 children who underwent LAARP (Laparoscopic assisted anorectal pull through), during which instead of conventional caudal block, continuous epidural analgesia was administered as an adjunct to the general anaesthesia in a novel method by giving a bolus local anaesthetic dose (0.5 ml/kg) via the tuohy needle at T12-L1 intervertebral space prior to the epidural catheter insertion and thereafter, threading the catheter in caudad direction and fixing, to provide sustained analgesia all through the surgery and post-operative period. All the three children had lower pain scores in the post-operative period and had uneventful courses in the hospital.   Keywords: Paediatric anaesthesia, epidural catheters, Ano-rectal malformations, Laparoscopic assisted anorectal pull through surgery.     INTRODUCTION Anorectal malformations (ARMs) comprise a wide spectrum of disease affecting distal anal canal, rectum along with genital or urinary canal, occurring approximately 1 in 5000 live births. The disease can vary between minor, easily treatable to complex, requiring staged surgeries and poor prognosis in terms of functionality [1]. ARMs are also the leading cause of intestinal obstruction in the neonatal period in most of the lower-middle income countries in the world [2]. The incidence may be as high as 2.54 per 10,000 cases in middle income countries due to lower registered birth defects. As a famous Anecdote by Dr WJ Potts says “a properly functioning rectum is an unappreciated gift of the greatest price,” holds true in terms of ARM as well. For a neonate unable to pass the meconium, urgent surgery like lower ARM repair or colostomy is warrante
title: A Dual Mode Epidural Analgesia Technique as an Adjunct to General Anaesthesia for Laparoscopic Assisted Anorectal Pull Through Surgery in Children: A Case Series
