DOI: https://doi.org/ 10.5281/zenodo.24029484 Received: 24 September 2026, Revised: 10 October 2026, Accepted: 31 October 2026, Online First:   13 November 2026 ABSTRACT Anorectal malformations (ARMs) are a spectrum of disease affecting rectum, anal canal and genito-urinary canal. ARM is also the leading cause of intestinal obstruction in the neonatal period [1, 2]. Paediatric age group along with various syndromes like VACTREL association in combination with laparoscopic approach for the correction of ARM pose unique challenges to anaesthesiologists, of which the presence of spinal dysraphism is particularly important as the analgesia in paediatric age group relies on neuraxial techniques like caudal block. Furthermore, providing adequate and sustained perioperative analgesia can be challenging due to the prolonged duration of surgery, involvement of both abdominal and perineal surgical fields, and limitations associated with conventional single-shot neuraxial techniques. We present a case of 3 children who underwent LAARP (Laparoscopic assisted anorectal pull through), during which instead of conventional caudal block, continuous epidural analgesia was administered as an adjunct to the general anaesthesia in a novel method by giving a bolus local anaesthetic dose (0.5 ml/kg) via the tuohy needle at T12-L1 intervertebral space prior to the epidural catheter insertion and thereafter, threading the catheter in caudad direction and fixing, to provide sustained analgesia all through the surgery and post-operative period. All the three children had lower pain scores in the post-operative period and had uneventful courses in the hospital.   Keywords: Paediatric anaesthesia, epidural catheters, Ano-rectal malformations, Laparoscopic assisted anorectal pull through surgery.     INTRODUCTION Anorectal malformations (ARMs) comprise a wide spectrum of disease affecting distal anal canal, rectum along with genital or urinary canal, occurring approximately 1 in 5000 live births. The disease can vary between minor, easily treatable to complex, requiring staged surgeries and poor prognosis in terms of functionality [1]. ARMs are also the leading cause of intestinal obstruction in the neonatal period in most of the lower-middle income countries in the world [2]. The incidence may be as high as 2.54 per 10,000 cases in middle income countries due to lower registered birth defects. As a famous Anecdote by Dr WJ Potts says “a properly functioning rectum is an unappreciated gift of the greatest price,” holds true in terms of ARM as well. summary: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.
title: FOE-Dreamer: Deployment-Efficient Learning of Cyber Defense Policies in Operational Networks

summary: The visual world is cluttered: robust vision-language reasoning requires ignoring irrelevant information. Yet vision-language models (VLMs) can suffer substantial accuracy losses when answering questions about a target image with distractors present. Existing mitigations focus on selecting relevant images or limiting information exchange between images. Through a systematic analysis of three open 7-8B VLMs on five perception benchmarks adapted to include distractor images, we show that distractors reduce accuracy even when models correctly identify the relevant image, suggesting that selection alone is not enough. To understand the mechanism behind this interference, we combine attention analysis with targeted knockouts in Qwen2.5-VL and identify middle-layer distractor-to-text connections as a pathway through which irrelevant visual information affects reasoning. We introduce answer consistency regularization, which encourages consistent answer distributions with and without distractors. Without directly constraining attention, this objective reduces middle-layer attention from question tokens to distractor images, consistent with the pathway our analysis implicates. With five distractors, our approach improves circular accuracy by an average of 16 percentage points over the Qwen2.5-VL baseline across the five benchmarks while preserving single-image performance.
title: Back to the Question: Tracing Visual Distraction Through Text Tokens

summary: Strongly correlated topological states in Kondo lattices represent a frontier in condensed matter physics, where the coupling between boundary electrons and localized f states can reshape the low-energy electronic structure. Here, we combine termination-resolved angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), Ce 4$d \rightarrow 4f$ resonant photoemission, and surface electronic structure calculations to investigate the Kondo lattice compound CeCuAs$_2$. Two distinct surface electronic structures are assigned to the As1 and CeAs2 terminations through their characteristic Fermi-surface geometries and termination-specific calculations. On CeAs2, a Dirac surface state associated with the calculated nontrivial bulk topology coexists with a weakly dispersive Ce 4$f$ band near $E_F$. Resonant photoemission identifies the low-energy 4$f$ character and reveals crystal-field-related fine structure in the energy range traversed by the Dirac branch. On cooling, the 4$f$ and Dirac regions both gain spectral weight, whereas a reference conduction-band region changes much less. Together, these observations provide spectroscopic evidence for termination-selective $f$-Dirac hybridization and the development of 4$f$ character in a topological surface state. Our results identify surface termination as a microscopic means of controlling the interplay between Kondo correlations and topological boundary electrons.
title: Termination-selective Kondo hybridization of topological surface states in CeCuAs$_2$

On cooling, the 4$f$ and Dirac regions both gain spectral weight, whereas a reference conduction-band region changes much less. summary: Reward models (RMs) are increasingly deployed as service components in LLM alignment pipelines, where payment, audit, moderation, and governance workflows act on the scores they return. An inference proof alone does not show whether a score belongs to the intended request, model checkpoint, numerical configuration, and verifier: in a controlled comparison that isolates the accepted statement from prover scale, a generic inference proof wrapped for on-chain checking remains valid after six classes of such service-field substitution. We formulate verifiable reward-model-as-a-service (VRMaaS) as a service-output integrity problem and present a framework in which each returned reward becomes a proof-carrying artifact. Its off-chain acceptance rule binds request identity, committed weights, verifier and configuration identifiers, proof-task order, and the digest of the exported package, so auditors can check a reward without rerunning the private RM or exposing inputs, checkpoints, or hidden activations; an optional on-chain zero-knowledge wrapper gives contracts a partial attestation of selected consistency checks and supplied service fields. The framework decomposes Transformer RM serving into arithmetic and lookup-backed proof tasks, aggregates them into a composite proof, and links hidden operands to the committed weights. A GPU prototype on 1B, 3B, and 8B reward models over 128-1024 tokens preserves 93.5-99% pairwise agreement with the baseline RM and rejects every tested service-field substitution in complete artifacts. Using exact integer witnesses and request-level aggregation of weight-binding openings, it generates complete artifacts in 49.8-206.1 seconds across the evaluated settings; auditors verify retained artifacts in 1.94-5.11 seconds, and partial public attestation costs about 217K gas. These costs suit delayed audit, settlement, and governance workflows.

summary: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. Empirically, our method consistently outperforms standard parallel TTS approaches across benchmarks, while significantly improving token efficiency and reducing overall computation.
title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an integral part of wireless systems, yet much of today's wireless AI remains task-specific and reactive, with models typically trained to map current observations to predefined outputs or reconstruct observed data. While effective for individual tasks, such approaches provide limited support for learning what is predictable, reusable, and transferable in dynamic wireless environments. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) offers a different perspective by learning predictive representations in latent space that capture informative structure in the observations. In this article, we introduce Communication JEPA (CommJEPA) as a communication-oriented framework for predictive representation learning. The central idea is bidirectional. JEPA can equip wireless systems with predictive representations for capturing latent channel and environmental dynamics, integrating heterogeneous observations, adapting to changing conditions, and supporting future decisions. Conversely, the physical structure, partial observability, multiple time scales, action-dependent evolution, and resource constraints of wireless systems motivate new communication-aware JEPA designs. We develop this mutual perspective, organize the resulting design space, and discuss representative JEPA-based wireless instantiations for prediction and control. We further highlight open challenges toward scalable, interactive, and predictive wireless intelligence.
title: CommJEPA: When Predictive Representation Learning Meets Wireless Intelligence

summary: Unfamiliar walkers may follow the shortest route and miss nearby shade, indoor passages and multilevel connections. We define the resulting hidden solar cost as the direct-sun exposure avoidable through shade-informed routing without substantial detours. We developed a time-specific three-dimensional model of Hong Kong Island that combines indoor and outdoor walking networks with building geometry, vegetation mapped by light detection and ranging (LiDAR), and solar position. For 500 modelled journeys, we compared shortest and shade-informed routes at four daytime snapshots and five extra-distance limits. At noon, shade-informed routes reduced modelled direct-sun exposure by 13.5% relative to shortest routes under a 10% extra-distance limit. Route length increased by 2.85% on average. A 5% extra-distance limit delivered 77% of the reduction obtained at 10%. In a controlled comparison, outdoor shade information accounted for 86% of the reduction and indoor-protection information for 14%. Removing multilevel connections left only 191 of 500 journeys feasible within the original route-length limit. These route comparisons identify an avoidable solar cost when existing protection is missing from the information used to choose a route. Making protected routes visible and preserving their connections can reduce sun exposure without large detours.
title: The hidden solar cost of urban unfamiliarity

summary: Heat dissipation in laser optical materials depends not only on their thermal conductivity but also on how absorbed energy is redistributed among various phonon modes. In calcium fluoride (CaF2), rapid energy transfer from hot electrons to weakly propagating longitudinal optical (LO) phonons can create a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck effect that limits efficient heat removal. Here, we propose selective phonon excitation as an effective strategy to break this bottleneck. Combining electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we identify LO phonons as the primary modes that preferentially receive energy from hot carriers, leading to energy accumulation due to their inefficient transport and relaxation. Guided by three-phonon scattering phase-space analysis, selective excitation of transverse acoustic (TA) modes can accelerate LO relaxation and promote energy transfer toward heat-carrying acoustic modes. While sustained LO-phonon excitation reduces the thermal conductivity by approximately 12%, additional TA-mode excitation improves heat conduction by approximately 21% compared to the state limited by the LO-phonon bottleneck, surpassing the unexcited value. These findings demonstrate that controlling interbranch energy redistribution can counteract phonon-bottleneck-induced heat accumulation and reveal a working route for active thermal management in laser optical materials through selective control of phonon populations.
title: Improving Nonequilibrium Thermal Conduction in CaF2 by Breaking the Phonon Bottleneck Effect

summary: Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce \bench{}, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distribution generalization to unseen equation templates and shifted coefficient ranges. We further introduce RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, uses relative $L^2$ feedback to refine coefficients and numerical solvers, and applies a validation gate to policy and memory updates. We compare RSI-PDE with single-run baselines and native agent harnesses (Claude Code or Codex) across four frontier models. Across the three settings, RSI-PDE improves the pass rate averaged across the four models by 106.5--181.9\% relative to single-run baselines and by 3.0--19.6\% relative to native harnesses, while reducing total recorded model calls by 46.9\% across the 12 model--setting pairs. These results highlight the potential of validated recursive self-improvement in LLM agents to advance scientific computing.

summary: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulation tasks such as mental rotation, paper folding, and perspective taking, and is not explained by task difficulty, reasoning depth, or sequential update load. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway also encodes spatial information in a higher-rank, probe-decodable form, but is not the causal handle. To separate decodability from causal use, we analyze concentration, alignment, and semantic location. These diagnostics explain why behavior, probing, and intervention can diverge. Multimodal training thus reshapes the geometry of text-only reasoning, not just how visual input is processed.
title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training

summary: This dataset contains the code, data and experimental records supporting "Privacy-Aware Personalized Scheduling of Behind-the-Meter Energy Storage via an Edge-Resident Large Language Model." It covers natural-language request interpretation, condition validation and mapping, load-dependent robust scheduling, independent schedule verification, nominal recovery and execution-layer grid import enforcement. The scheduling data comprise 72 household-day profiles from six households and six request scenarios. Four methods receiving user conditions are evaluated under three forecast configurations, producing 5,184 daily trajectories and 124,416 hourly planning steps. Four corresponding planners with the user conditions removed add 864 trajectories and 20,736 steps; each trajectory is evaluated against six requests, yielding 5,184 no-personalization request evaluations. The current formal comparison therefore contains 6,048 trajectories, 145,152 planning steps and 10,368 request evaluations. Development runs, degradation-cost sensitivity experiments and separate reproducibility checks are also included. The main absolute-calibration comparison gives actual complete success rates of 55.32% for no-personalization nominal rolling scheduling and 94.21% for the proposed method, with mean daily operating costs of 5.2964 and 5.3631 USD2022, respectively. Costs combine electricity purchases under the constructed time-of-use tariff with throughput-based degradation costs. User clock times and tariff periods follow Europe/Berlin within fixed 24-hour UTC simulation windows. Language materials include prompts, request texts, saved responses, reference annotations and scoring code for the 80-request controlled benchmark, 240-request stress benchmark and 30-request extended benchmark, together with paired prompt-development records. Device records cover inference, request-to-schedule integration, resource monitoring and rolling scheduling on RK3588. The release provides source code, frozen inputs, raw results, machine-readable tables, independent data checks and a unified desktop reproduction entry point for Tables 1-10 and S1 and Figures 1-6 and S1. A result index links each output to its inputs and scripts. Dependency specifications, RK3588 operating instructions, component licenses and SHA-256 checksums accompany the archive. Research code is distributed under the MIT License. Research data, derived results and figures use CC BY 4.0; third-party materials retain their accompanying licenses. Household data source: Open Power System Data, Data Package Household Data, version 2020-04-15, https://data.open-power-system-data.org/household_data/2020-04-15/.

summary: Run records and figure data of the article "Exact nullspaces certify kinetic modules and other mass-action invariants in metabolic networks" by Philipp C. Schneider Chuzel (Science Advances, submitted). The archive holds every file that the figures, tables, Data S1 and S2 and the numbers of the article are computed from, and its README.md maps each file to the paper item it supports and to the script that reads it. Abstract of the article. Genome-scale metabolic models are routinely analyzed through their steady-state fluxes, but kinetics needs rate constants that are rarely known. Kinetic modules are independent of their exact values. Under mass-action kinetics, these are parts of a network whose concentrations keep fixed ratios in every positive steady state. Finding them means solving polynomial equations, which is out of reach at genome scale. Here, two existing methods are recast as exact nullspace computations, the natural tool for invariants. One proves kinetic modules but can miss some, and the other misses none but can report false ones. On 30 of 33 genome-scale networks the two agree, which certifies all kinetic modules and related invariants. Because exact nullspaces are cheap, this takes seconds to minutes per network. Contents of Kimonu_records.zip. networks/ the 33 genome-scale networks as every tool received them (blocked reactions removed), the same networks before removal, the exact coupling matrices the reference read, their deficiencies and e_coli_core for the symbolic baselines results/kimonu/ the Kimonu runs of 2026-11-11 on the final code. These are the timed runs on exclusive nodes (iterated route with detached and attached uptakes, reference-equivalent mode, tangent route, small networks), both routes in both uptake modes, coverage counts, ACR and ACRR lists, the gap networks, the uniformly drawn flux with its Schwartz-Zippel bound, the rounding check, the floating-point comparison and the symbolic baselines results/cocoa_jl/ COCOA.jl v1.1.0 with efficient=false and efficient=true, three seeds each (frozen records), and how every run on a network without a result ended results/reference/ the reference implementation of Langary et al. (2025), exhaustive and sampled (frozen records), and its 24-h trial runs on all 33 networks results/hardware/ nodes, CPUs, memory, threads and software versions of every benchmark run figures/ the published figures (SVG), Data S1 and S2 (CSV) and the source data the figures are drawn from Kimonu.py-078414e.zip a snapshot of the source code and the scripts at commit 078414e SHA256SUMS lists every file with its checksum. The scripts in scripts/ of the repository read the unpacked archive as their records folder (environment variable KIMONU_RECORDS) and rebuild the figures, tables and numbers. The Kimonu results were computed with commit 451a748 of https://github.com/VonAlphaBisZulu/Kimonu.py , and later commits up to the snapshot restructure the package without changing its results (scripts/kinetic_variants/refactor_equivalence.py). Data, records and figures are licensed under CC BY 4.0, and the code in the snapshot under the Apache License 2.0.

summary: Video-editing agents must update dependent timeline state while keeping the project available for manual revision. We study how to divide responsibility between a language model and the editing environment. We present Cassette-Editor, an agent harness in which manual gestures and agent patches share an action language, executor, rulebook, and history. Within the editor's supported domain and authorized scope, the agent language can express the content changes available to manual editing. The model chooses edits; the editor derives dependent changes, checks project invariants, returns localized diagnostics, and maps source evidence to the current timeline. With GPT-6 Luna as released, the full harness satisfied the scored request checks in 92/93 unattended trials across 31 authored requests on two interview documentaries, against 48/93 with basic tools, an internal baseline with restricted actions and reduced execution support. Follow-up experiments provide evidence that dependency maintenance and rule enforcement with its fixes improve completion under targeted conditions. Read-mapping and repair experiments found lower agent effort with edit-aware reads and diagnostic receipts. A complete-system comparison on 50 TVSum videos found greater agreement with human annotations than a general agent using the same model (F1 23.8 vs. 20.1). Perceptual quality and sustained human-agent editing remain unevaluated.
title: Cassette-Editor: An Agent Harness for Editing Video the Way You Do

summary: Durably removing ~10 Gt CO₂ yr⁻¹ by 2050 is widely treated as necessary for meeting Paris temperature goals. I found three problems with the 10-Gt benchmark when I tracked carbon-dioxide-removal (CDR) estimates across 51 sources and analyzed the underlying scenarios from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). First, the citation pathway traces almost exclusively to IPCC reports, but the 10-Gt magnitude did not come from a direct reading of IPCC outputs. The number first appeared in a 2017 news piece as an informal estimate, was declared the 'needed' amount in a 2019 National Academy report, and propagated from there; low-CDR scenarios in both IPCC and independent sources were largely ignored. Second, 10 Gt CO₂ yr⁻¹ is larger than the IPCC ensemble medians, which are themselves CDR-reliant, treating emissions reductions and future removals as interchangeable. In the 6th Assessment Report (AR6) I found CDR magnitude correlated with near-term mitigation pace, and as target temperatures rose, the additional carbon-budget space was, on median, filled by continued emissions rather than by reduced CDR. Third, as CDR estimates moved into NGO and industry sectors, the discourse shifted: language describing CDR changed from conditional (e.g., 'scenarios show') to prescriptive (e.g., 'CDR is necessary'), risk discussion diminished, and CDR type narrowed to durable approaches only, excluding the nature-based methods the IPCC scenarios included. The 10-Gt benchmark is therefore larger than warranted by the underlying scenarios, disconnected from the mitigation choices that produced it, and stripped of the context decision-makers need. With the next IPCC assessment report (AR7) underway, there is an opportunity to build a better CDR discourse. One that connects CDR magnitude to mitigation choices, includes lower-CDR pathways, matches CDR durability to its varied roles, and characterizes feasibility, costs, and risks.
title: How carbon dioxide removal lost its way: tracing the origin and transformation of the 10-Gt durable CDR target

summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. We present EvoX, a Rust-based, multi-model agent runtime guided by The Second Policy, which views the harness as an Operational Policy complementing the foundation model's Semantic Policy. EvoX combines model-facing guidance with deterministic runtime control through three complementary mechanisms: Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. To evaluate harnesses without suppressing their native behaviors, we introduce Contrast, a controlled and auditable framework integrating explicit fairness constraints, provider-bound request verification, and evidence-based adjudication. Across five benchmarks, six foundation models, and six agent harnesses, EvoX achieves the highest numerical success rate of 56.2% over 691 common task--model pairs, exceeding the average of the other five harnesses by approximately 3.0 percentage points. Its larger advantages on GLM-5.3 (+10.7 points) and Kimi K3 (+7.9 points) highlight the model-dependent effectiveness of harness design and the potential for cross-provider adaptability. Achieved without memory, evolution, or extensions, these results establish EvoX as a competitive multi-model agent runtime and underscore the importance of harness-level operational control in realizing foundation-model capabilities.
title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy

summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.
title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime

summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

summary: This paper develops a distributed inverse-optimal fixed-time integral reinforcement learning framework for unknown nonlinear leader-follower multi-agent systems. The proposed method first reconstructs the unknown agent dynamics from finite integral data. Based on the identified dynamics, a distributed inverse-optimal formulation is constructed by prescribing a desired fixed-time value function and recovering a compatible running cost. A critic-only integral reinforcement learning architecture is then developed using current integral data and finitely informative experience-replay data, thereby avoiding the persistent-excitation requirement. Practical fixed-time convergence of the critic-weight errors is established in the presence of identification and function-approximation residuals. Finally, a network-level composite Lyapunov analysis proves practical fixed-time leader-following consensus of the true unknown nonlinear multi-agent system. Numerical simulations are provided to validate the developed theory.
title: Inverse-Optimal Fixed-Time Integral Reinforcement Learning for Unknown Nonlinear Leader-Follower Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Graph-based observability analysis runs in seconds where Lie-derivative tests take hours, but it answers only one question: is the system observable or not. It cannot say how well a given set of measurements supports state reconstruction. This paper extends the graph-based approach with symbolic observability coefficients computed from a symbolic Jacobian of the state-space equations, in which every dependency is classified as constant, nonlinear polynomial, or rational. We show that the coefficient tracks the analytical observability determinant of the Lie-derivative approach: it is zero when the determinant vanishes, lies strictly between zero and one when the determinant depends on the state, and equals one when the determinant is a nonzero constant. We apply the method to a seven-state synchronous machine and to the 21-state Western System Coordinating Council nine-bus system under several synchrophasor measurement configurations. On the nine-bus system, the coefficient grows from 0.0952 with one PMU to 0.1905 with two and 0.2857 with three, and the whole analysis runs in under five seconds. Configurations with the same number of PMUs receive the same coefficient, yet an unscented Kalman filter estimates the states with different accuracy for each. The symbolic coefficient therefore grades measurement sets beyond identifying root strongly connected components, while telling PMU locations apart still requires the numerical parameters of the system.
title: Beyond Yes or No: Grading Observability of Power System Dynamic States with Symbolic Coefficients

summary: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.

summary: Talagrand's convolution conjecture, recently proven by J. Lu, S. Guo, and E. Fang, concerns the smoothing properties of the heat semigroup on $\{-1,1\}^N$. We follow their perturbed coupled reverse-heat approach to generalize the theorem to tensor powers of irreducible continuous-time Markov semigroups on finite state spaces. Specifically, let $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ be the semigroup of an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $G_0$ with stationary distribution $π$. Then, for every $τ>0$, there exists a finite constant $C_{τ,S,π}<\infty$ such that, for every $N\geq1$, every nonnegative function $f:G_0^N\to[0,\infty)$, and every $η>1$, \begin{align*} π^{\otimes N}\left(S_τ^{\otimes N}f>η\int_{G_0^N}f\,dπ^{\otimes N}\right)\leq\frac{C_{τ,S,π}}{η\sqrt{\logη}}, \end{align*} where the constant is independent of $N$, $f$, and $η$. Most of the machinery developed by Lu, Guo, and Fang transfers cleanly, but since probability distributions on $|G_0|$ elements are not determined by their mean for $|G_0|>2$, we must use explicit terminal bridge laws to find a dimension-independent bound for the terminal-discrepancy estimate. We have formalized our result in Lean 4. The formalization is publicly available.
title: Talagrand's Convolution Bound for Tensor Powers of Finite-State Markov Semigroups

summary: RF fingerprinting benchmarks report how well a classifier separates transmitters, not whether that separability reflects the individual unit or its hardware family. We compare a benchmark's real hardware grouping with size-matched random groupings of the same devices, using calibrated, unclipped variational lower bounds under label-blind, device-level cross-fitting on devices never seen in training. On WiSig (OFDM Wi-Fi), the generation grouping exceeded all 999 matched random groupings (permutation p = 0.001, the resolution floor), although no grouping attained a positive certified bound, and the direction survives removing channel equalization. A preregistered replication on a LoRa corpus (chirp spread spectrum, three hardware models), with a front-end frozen on synthetic data, again exceeded all 999 (p = 0.001), and two sensitivity analyses judged by a reversal rule fixed in advance did not reverse the direction. This is a directional replication only: the excess magnitude reflects a miscalibrated null, the chain-rule decomposition leaves a residual of +0.296 bits, and capture order is undocumented. In a same-model corpus of 122 ESP32 radios, a temperature-calibrated held-out bound of +3.338 bits (label entropy 6.931 bits) indicates substantial device-specific identity, not separable from per-device capture-session effects; relying on the calibrated bound was decided after the uncalibrated bound changed sign. On synthetic transmitters a high-capacity convolutional decoder reaches 98.5% of a known 6-bit ceiling, and the audit protocol leaves chain-rule residuals of +0.072 bits (synthetic, fixed physical features) and +0.060 bits (WiSig, audit features). Two further corpora were excluded by preregistered ingest gates. Across WiSig and LoRa, hardware-family groupings consistently produced stronger identity-associated signal than size-matched random groupings.
title: What Does an RF Fingerprint Identify? A Cross-Corpus Evaluation of Hardware-Family-Associated and Unit-Level Signal

On WiSig (OFDM Wi-Fi), the generation grouping exceeded all 999 matched random groupings (permutation p = 0.001, the resolution floor), although no grouping attained a positive certified bound, and the direction survives removing channel equalization. A preregistered replication on a LoRa corpus (chirp spread spectrum, three hardware models), with a front-end frozen on synthetic data, again exceeded all 999 (p = 0.001), and two sensitivity analyses judged by a reversal rule fixed in advance did not reverse the direction. This is a directional replication only: the excess magnitude reflects a miscalibrated null, the chain-rule decomposition leaves a residual of +0.296 bits, and capture order is undocumented. In a same-model corpus of 122 ESP32 radios, a temperature-calibrated held-out bound of +3.338 bits (label entropy 6.931 bits) indicates substantial device-specific identity, not separable from per-device capture-session effects; relying on the calibrated bound was decided after the uncalibrated bound changed sign. On synthetic transmitters a high-capacity convolutional decoder reaches 98.5% of a known 6-bit ceiling, and the audit protocol leaves chain-rule residuals of +0.072 bits (synthetic, fixed physical features) and +0.060 bits (WiSig, audit features). Two further corpora were excluded by preregistered ingest gates. Across WiSig and LoRa, hardware-family groupings consistently produced stronger identity-associated signal than size-matched random groupings.
title: What Does an RF Fingerprint Identify? A Cross-Corpus Evaluation of Hardware-Family-Associated and Unit-Level Signal

summary: Cataloguing a Roman Imperial coin involves reading its legends and identifying its imagery in order to match it to an entry in the standard reference catalogue. Previous work has automated individual parts of this process, such as identifying the issuer or recognizing reverse motifs, by formulating each part as a classification task over a predefined set of labels. We instead formulate coin description as image-to-text generation and adapt an open-weight vision-language model (VLM), Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, to four tasks: transcribing the obverse and reverse legends, and describing the obverse and reverse imagery. To obtain training data, we convert approximately 30,000 auction records into structured image-text pairs. We separate the two sides of each coin, extract and normalize legends and descriptions, and standardize obverse descriptions against a bust-type taxonomy. We then train a separate low-rank adapter for each task on a single 20GB GPU, and evaluate each task with metrics that we define to capture the key components of numismatic descriptions. The adapted models outperform both the unadapted base model and GPT-4.1 on all four tasks, reducing the normalized edit distance of legend transcriptions by over 40% relative to GPT-4.1. The improvement is smaller, but still present, on legends absent from the training data.
title: From Classification to Generation: Vision-Language Models for Roman Imperial Coin Description

summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://triplibre.hhtdiary.org/docs/
title: TripLibre: An Open-Source, Privacy-First Travel Diary for Mobility Research

summary: SPECIMEN 1.0.0 SPECIMEN's first stable release (tracker #7) provides workflows for automated, strain-specific genome-scale metabolic model reconstruction and curation: HQTB: Build a model from a high-quality template and an annotated genome. CMPB: Extend and curate a CarveMe model using refineGEMs and ModelPolisher. 🔧 Fixes Corrected CLI parameter handling for analysis and smoothing. Fixed validation commands and selection of individual validation tests. Restored MetaNetX setup, including missing-table detection and download chunk-size handling. Fixed batch HQTB execution across genome subdirectories and temporary configuration handling. 📖 Documentation and usability Revised workflow descriptions, configuration guidance, installation instructions, and CLI documentation. Updated workflow diagrams, logos, and README badges. Refreshed the workflow tutorial and removed outdated notebooks. Fixed documentation build dependencies. 🚧 Project maintenance Added contribution guidelines, issue templates, a pull request template, and a code of conduct. Added a Docker Hub publishing workflow with a CLI smoke test. Added automated dependency security updates. 🟢 Scope The workflows have been tested on prokaryotic genomes. BiGG remains the best-supported namespace; feedback on other namespaces is welcome. The new PGAB workflow is under development. Full changelog: v0.0.dev3 → v1.0.0

summary: Access. Restricted: the metadata is public and the files are visible to the depositor and to the Zenodo accounts thomas@digitalethercomputing.com and wasi@digitalethercomputing.com only. This record holds data and trained checkpoints only. It contains no source code and no third-party model weights. Data and checkpoints for the manuscript on inverse-folding distillation for foldable RNA (Bhat, Ul-Kabir, Islam, Caulfield; Digital Ether Computing LLC). A grammar proposes secondary-structure scaffolds, inverse folding writes sequences onto them, a ViennaRNA refold keeps the sequences that fold into a stable, well-defined structure, and a small masked-diffusion language model (AptaLM, 21 M parameters) is trained on the survivors. The files below are every dataset and every trained checkpoint behind the manuscript's tables and figures. Sequences are 10–80 nt over A, C, G, U. Subdivisions (files) aptalm_synthetic_cohort.tar.zst – the synthetic cohort. corpora/screened_pool.jsonl is the screened synthetic pool (about 3.8 million sequences, each with its target dot-bracket, ViennaRNA energy terms, structure descriptors, generating stream, and screen label; screened_pool_streams.json counts the streams). The training corpora built from it: IF (338,049 sequences, natural length profile), PoolBins (338,049, the pool's own length profile), IF-34k and IF-100k (size subsets of IF ), IF-Cond (the IF sequences paired with their ViennaRNA minimum-free-energy structures, as conditioning input), and RF (338,049 sequences from grammar structures filled with random nucleotides, then passed through the same refold screen; the no-inverse-folding control). IF-matched and RF-matched are the synthetic arms of a composition-matched trio (164,559 sequences each, equal counts in 189 length-by-GC cells). Also the structure reference refs/train_passer_ss.jsonl (15,000 pool sequences folded with ViennaRNA) and 5,000-sequence samples of IF and RF . aptalm_natural_cohort.tar.zst – the natural cohort, derived only from RNAcentral. natural_rep90.jsonl is the non-redundant natural reference (1,735,854 sequences, 10–80 nt, one representative per 90% identity cluster; each row carries its RNAcentral URS accession), natural_all.jsonl a capped per-RNA-type sample, and the corpora Nat (338,049, the same length profile as IF ), NatScreen (338,049, natural sequences passed through the pool's fold screen), and Nat-matched (the natural arm of the matched trio), with the structure reference refs/natural_rep90_ss.jsonl (15,000 sequences folded with ViennaRNA) and a 5,000-sequence sample of Nat . aptalm_aptamer_references.tar.zst – refs/aptamer_core_analysis.jsonl : 637 published aptamers used only as an evaluation reference, never for training. 583 rows are from the UTexas Aptamer Database (September 2023 snapshot; primer-stripped to the random region; 515 of them 10–80 nt) and 54 rows are native aptamer models from RNAapt3D. aptalm_checkpoints.tar.zst – 19 trained checkpoints, weights/ablations/*.pt , each the epoch with the lowest validation loss. LLaDA-style masked diffusion (AptaLM): AptaLM (full pool), AptaLM-IF , AptaLM-IF-seed1 , AptaLM-Nat , AptaLM-Nat-seed1 , AptaLM-RF , AptaLM-RF-seed1 , AptaLM-NatScreen , AptaLM-PoolBins , AptaLM-34k , AptaLM-100k , AptaLM-IF-matched , AptaLM-Nat-matched , AptaLM-RF-matched (each named after its training corpus); AptaLM-FT10 and AptaLM-FT30 ( AptaLM-Nat fine-tuned on IF for 10 and 30 epochs); AptaLM-Cond (structure-conditioned, trained on IF-Cond ). Autoregressive Llama-style control (LlamaRNA, 20.5 M parameters): AptaLM-AR ( IF ) and AptaLM-AR-Nat ( Nat ). SHA256SUMS.txt – checksums of the four archives. summary: Replication package for the article "Example Scenarios, Random Sequences or Contract-Guided Exploration? Testing a Stateful Learning Agreement Service with Language Model Implementations, Seeded Faults and Blind Test Suites" (I. Tiievskyi). The study compares three black-box testing techniques on an executable contract of a learning agreement revision service inspired by the Erasmus Without Paper (EWP) Outgoing Mobility Learning Agreements workflow: example scenarios (EX), random request sequences (RND) and contract-guided breadth-first exploration (SYS). The package contains everything needed to rerun the experiments and recompute the reported numbers. Contents - contract/: the executable contract (ten obligations), a description of which parts of the EWP workflow it covers, the reference implementation REF with ten dependent faults, the fourteen example scenarios (EX) and unit tests. - study/impl_I1, study/impl_I2, study/i3: five implementations in total – REF plus I1 (Python) and I2 (Node.js) written from the contract and interface only, and I3 and I4 written by two further language models from the same brief; implementers' notes on ambiguities and file hashes. - study/faults, study/mutants_ext: 40 seeded mutants (F01–F10, G01–G10, GM01–GM10, PM01–PM10) with their catalogue, exact edits, revealing sequences and seeding briefs. - study/human_faults: ten faults (H01–H10) written by a backend developer without AI tools, together with the task sheet stating the inclusion criteria. - study/blind: ten example suites written by six language models from the contract text alone, the writers' brief, the pre-registered evaluation harness with its hashes, the corrected harness and the results before and after the correction. - study/harness, study/controls, study/robustness: the test bench (EX, RND, SYS, differential oracle), the black-box contract observer, oracle and budget controls, the census of disagreements between implementations, observation-level, pruning, hash-seed and fault-mechanism analyses, and regression tests of the scenario comparator. - Raw results (JSON) for every reported table; README.md maps each table of the article to the script and result file that produce it. Requirements and use Python 3.11 or later and Node.js 18 or later, standard libraries only, no network access. Each script is run from its own folder; a run of 20,000 requests takes about 5 seconds. README.md gives quick checks, the exact commands for the full blind-suite run and the census reproduction, and the random seeds used (RND seeds 1–5, 1–10 for the dependent faults, census seed 1, PYTHONHASHSEED 0 for the robustness analyses). Version 1.1 The census of disagreements now draws the request selected from history from a local generator initialised with the census seed, so the census is fully reproducible. All ten pairwise census runs were repeated; the sets of disagreements and the first detection of each point reported in Table 5 are unchanged. The version 1.0 census results are kept in study/census_v1.0. The main mutant and blind-suite runs are not affected by this change. Provenance The contract, the reference implementation, the example scenarios, the dependent faults, the harness and the analysis scripts were prepared by the author with AI assistance (Claude Opus 5.5). I1, I2 and F01–G10 were written by isolated Claude Opus 5.5 agents without access to the tests; I3, I4, GM01–GM10 and PM01–PM10 by GPT 6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon from the same briefs; the blind suites by Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2, GPT 6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon. The archived briefs cover the blind suites, I3/I4, the GM/PM mutants and the developer task; full agent and chat transcripts are not included. The developer agreed to the publication of the faults. Integrity SHA256SUMS lists the SHA-256 checksum of every file in the package (sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS in the package root).

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Thirty-five entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten, a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), and a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation, a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight, and a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963), converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters, gives the absorbance template of a visual pigment of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for a peak wavelength and chromophore the caller states, and gives the distance between two colours in units of receptor noise by the model of Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), for a noise the caller states. Without a water type, it gives Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001) or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013), the remote sensing reflectance from a and bb (Gordon et al. 1988; Lee et al. 2002), and the Secchi depth from Kd and that reflectance (Lee et al. 2015), and inverts the reflectance to the absorption and backscattering coefficients by the quasi-analytical algorithm, in the version of IOCCG Report 5 (2006), checked against that report's published statistics, and as QAA_v6, checked against its author's spreadsheet. It carries four published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016) and Lee et al. (2015), for the caller to choose from

summary: BOTANICAL SHEET-MASK SCIENCE: FROM SERUM CHEMISTRY TO VERIFIED WET CONTACT F121-F125 | Family 25 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch | 33 x STARLI | Edition v1.0 / November 2026 Five integrated nonclinical research themes: storage marker integrity, lyocell sorption, three-dimensional wet contact, mass-based evaporation and qualified reconstructed-epidermis evidence. Scope and scientific authority This long-form technical notebook is a proposed investigation, not a laboratory or cosmetic product performance report. The primary source is the 817-page STARLI Botanical Master Blueprint v1.0, Family25 F121-F125; older Mothers F12 and F28 provide method and evidence constraints. The numerical charts are synthetic hypotheses. Chinese materia medica inspires provenance, processing and compound questions, not a biological proof. Claims about a commercial sheet mask, sensitive-skin suitability and humans would need independent ethically and legally appropriate evidence. Five different objects, five different vetoes F121 - Botanical Sheet-Mask Serum Active Stability at the Limit. Native measurement: stored mask-serum marker retention (%). Fair reference: equal-formula serum stored in an inert vessel, blank lyocell, matched nonwoven mask and light/dark paired packaging. Disqualifying rival: adsorption onto cellulose, packaging migration, altered extract recovery, optical co-elution or oxygen-driven degradation. F122 - Lyocell–Botanical Serum Adsorption at the Limit. Native measurement: identified botanical marker adsorbed on lyocell (mg/g). Fair reference: matched nonwoven material, no-sheet serum reservoir, same-area inert substrate and prewetted lyocell control. Disqualifying rival: surface liquid mistaken for bonded sorbate, unequal sheet density, incomplete desorption or retained marker counted as delivered. F123 - Botanical Mask Conformability and Liquid Distribution at the Limit. Native measurement: verified face-surface wet-contact area (cm2). Fair reference: shape-matched nonwoven mask, same-serum container exposure, equal-load flat phantom and reversed sheet orientation. Disqualifying rival: pressure shadows mistaken for contact, pixel threshold bias, droplet pooling in folds or high contact area with low local transfer. F124 - Botanical Mask Wear Time and Evaporation at the Limit. Native measurement: evaporation mass flux (g/m2/h). Fair reference: no-sheet serum film, humidity-matched nonwoven, impermeable occlusive reference and evaporation-free gravimetric blank. Disqualifying rival: short-term occlusion masquerades as barrier repair, variable wet area, edge leakage or ambient humidity drift. F125 - Botanical Nano-Sheet-Mask Sensitive-Skin Tolerability at the Limit. Native measurement: qualified reconstructed epidermis viability (%) and marker exposure (microg/cm2). Fair reference: same-contact-time matched serum alone, blank lyocell, nonwoven sheet with matched vehicle and qualified positive-irritant reference. Disqualifying rival: pigmented botanicals distort viability reagent, local occlusion hides evaporation, tissue necrosis mimics reduced flux or uncontrolled dose. Methodological sources and foundations Five independent scientific identities under one mask F121 tests marker retention through storage without confusing cellulose sorption with degradation. F122 resolves lyocell-bound and freely available serum markers. F123 measures the genuine 3D wet-contact area and spatial transfer rather than a photographic silhouette. F124 reconstructs evaporation by mass, time, true area and environmental gradients. F125 tests qualified RhE viability only with chemically verified exposure, matched vehicle and cell-free interference controls. None of the five outputs substitutes for another. F121: chemical stability versus package partition A marker lost from the liquid phase may reside inside lyocell, on packaging film, in a precipitate or as a true degradation product. The difference is decisive. I

Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F106-F110; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of authenticated botanical, lamellar and barrier evidence F106 - Botanical Active-Ceramide Compatibility at the Limit: primary endpoint botanical-active / ceramide precipitation fraction (%). Fair comparator: full-lipid reference, active-only, ceramide-only, matched vehicle and equal-oil nonlamellar controls. Disqualifying counterexample: color/turbidity interference, precipitated cholesterol, pH-triggered crystal formation, non-specific surface adsorption, pigment scattering. F107 - Ceramide-Cholesterol-Fatty Acid Ratios at the Limit: primary endpoint lamellar-order parameter (dimensionless) under defined three-lipid mole ratios. Fair comparator: matched single-lipid omissions, equimass nonlamellar dispersions and same-total-lipid reference. F108 - Botanical Lipid Lamellar Structure Formation at the Limit: primary endpoint lamellar-domain repeat spacing (nm) with reported scattering resolution. Fair comparator: equal-total-lipid disordered reference, reordered lipid mixture and water-activity-matched blank. Disqualifying counterexample: instrument q-calibration drift, sample thickness, cholesterol crystals, preferred orientation or hydration swelling misassigned to layered structure. F109 - Botanical Barrier Lipid Nanodelivery at the Limit: primary endpoint coefficient of variation of component distribution in a nonclinical lipid model (%). Fair comparator: equal-lipid nonlamellar vehicle, matched blank nanocarrier, free-active mixture and depth-attenuation reference. Disqualifying counterexample: fluorescent dye decoupling, light attenuation, optical scatter, surface contamination mistaken for depth deposition. Fair comparator: equal-lipid vehicle, occlusive inert reference, missing-ceramide arm, full-lipid reference and sham-treated qualified RhE. summary: Modelled LGA-week cholera surveillance series for Nigeria, 2022–2024 This dataset contains 120,744 records: 774 Nigerian local government areas (LGAs) across 37 states (36 states and the Federal Capital Territory) and six geopolitical zones, for 156 consecutive epidemiological weeks from 3 January 2022 to 29 December 2024. Each record gives the LGA identifier, name, state and zone, centroid coordinates, a weekly count of suspected cholera cases, and week and year indices. Population denominators come from the 2006 National Population Commission census and are available for 611 of the 774 LGAs (95,316 LGA-weeks). The file also holds simulated covariate columns (water, sanitation and hygiene access, flood risk, temperature, rainfall, mobility, population density and one further parameter) as supplied. Their provenance is undocumented. For selected weeks and states, the file includes state and national cases and deaths transcribed from Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) situation reports. Each transcribed value is traceable through its source and source-URL columns. Files File Content nigeria_cholera_lga_week_2022_2024_modelled.csv The dataset (UTF-8 with byte-order mark; 36 columns). Content identical to the file analysed in the manuscript, originally named nigeria_cholera_spatiotemporal_REAL_DATA_2022_2024.csv. data_dictionary.csv Description, type, unit and number of missing values for every column. code/ Python scripts for the associated analysis (Moran's I, Local Moran's I, Getis-Ord Gi*, and a Bayesian BYM2 spatiotemporal model fitted with a custom Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler). results/ Analysis outputs: exploratory_results.json, post_results.json, lga_results.csv, lga_analysis.csv, weekly.csv, table1.csv, state_year_recon.csv. figures/ The three manuscript figures (PNG). Reproducing the analysis Requires Python 3 with NumPy, SciPy, pandas and matplotlib. Put the CSV and the scripts in one folder (or set the environment variable WORKDIR to that folder), then run in this order: exploratory.py, run_chains.py (about four minutes per chain, four chains), post.py, figs12.py, fig3.py. Running exploratory.py on the packaged data reproduces results/exploratory_results.json and results/lga_analysis.csv exactly. weekly.csv, table1.csv and state_year_recon.csv were produced in an interactive step for the manuscript and have no separate script; they are supplied as outputs only. Random seeds: 20261103 (exploratory analysis) and 101, 202, 303, 404 (Bayesian chains). bym_st_v1.py (an earlier sampler version) is not included. 01_simulate_data.py  (corrected version) ======================================== Simulate weekly cholera cases for all 774 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Nigeria over a three-year (156-week) period. Output columns match the canonical file `nigeria_cholera_spatiotemporal.csv`:     lga_id, state, zone, latitude, longitude, week, year, week_of_year,     pop_density, population, wash_access, flood_risk, temperature_c,     rainfall_mm, mobility_index, beta, cholera_cases, incidence_per_100k Counts are generated conditionally as Poisson draws given a latent LGA-week rate (Equations 14-15). summary: Replication dataset and verification code for the manuscript "Split Custody and Fossilised Provenance: Cross-Regime Recordkeeping Governance Across Space-Mission Closeouts and Schema Migrations". The archive contains 36 unmodified files from the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS3 and PDS4 labels, catalog files, checksum manifests, user guides, errata and node policy pages) for the Apollo 15/17 Heat Flow Experiment, Clementine 1 Bistatic Radar, Magellan Venus GXDR and OSIRIS-REx SPICE archives; a manifest with official URLs and SHA-256 digests for the 10 policy, oversight and case documents analysed in the study (the documents themselves are not redistributed); a dependency-free Python 3 script, run_feasibility_audit.py; and its four output files. Running python3 run_feasibility_audit.py reproduces the output files byte for byte (SHA-256 digests are listed in README_Dataset.md). The script confirms that 11 of 11 PDS4 XML labels are well-formed, inventories 6,378 published MD5 manifest entries (430 in five PDS Geosciences Node manifests and 5,948 in the OSIRIS-REx checksum_v013.tab manifest), matches 22 of 22 local checksum comparisons across 21 sampled files, finds no cryptographic digital signatures in the 36 archive files, and writes the coded evidence matrix (E01 to E10) used in the manuscript. Third-party files in corpus/pds_artifacts/ are redistributed unmodified and remain subject to their original terms. summary: Two partly ciphered letters (Gelders Archief, 0372 Huis Ammerzoden, inv. 52), 1614–1615, from Jean-Baptiste van Male, the Archdukes' agent in London, to his brother Abraham van Male, drost of Steenbergen. Edition of the deciphered passages, key, and historical context. Version 3 replaces version 2: the family link is confirmed from the Annuaire de la noblesse de Belgique (1865); the provenance is traced through the inventory (De la Kéthulle, Van Arkel); Abraham van Male died before March 1621; new readings in letter 2 ('chasque huict jours', 'mériter une belle chaine d'or', 'circonspect', 'het port van brieven'). Transcription and cryptanalysis were done with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).
title: 'De Londres le 28e de Xbre': two partly ciphered letters from Jean-Baptiste van Male, the Archdukes' agent in London, to his brother Abraham, drost of Steenbergen (1614–1615)

summary: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. Evaluating three models across four data-context settings shows that the benchmarks separate data contexts and model tiers. Auditing candidate queries against causal provenance in the simulation log verifies gold programs without manual annotation, including on multi-event composite tasks that expose reasoning failures in state-of-the-art agents. We hope the community uses SynthCorp to generate more challenging and useful data estates and benchmarks that foster the development of enterprise data agents.
title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents

summary: This dataset contains the code, data and experimental records supporting "Privacy-Aware Personalized Scheduling of Behind-the-Meter Energy Storage via an Edge-Resident Large Language Model." It covers natural-language request interpretation, condition validation and mapping, load-dependent robust scheduling, independent schedule verification, nominal recovery and execution-layer grid import enforcement. The scheduling data comprise 72 household-day profiles from six households and six request scenarios. Four methods receiving user conditions are evaluated under three forecast configurations, producing 5,184 daily trajectories and 124,416 hourly planning steps. Four corresponding planners with the user conditions removed add 864 trajectories and 20,736 steps; each trajectory is evaluated against six requests, yielding 5,184 no-personalization request evaluations. The current formal comparison therefore contains 6,048 trajectories, 145,152 planning steps and 10,368 request evaluations. Development runs, degradation-cost sensitivity experiments and separate reproducibility checks are also included. The main absolute-calibration comparison gives actual complete success rates of 55.32% for no-personalization nominal rolling scheduling and 94.21% for the proposed method, with mean daily operating costs of 5.2964 and 5.3631 USD2022, respectively. Costs combine electricity purchases under the constructed time-of-use tariff with throughput-based degradation costs. User clock times and tariff periods follow Europe/Berlin within fixed 24-hour UTC simulation windows. Language materials include prompts, request texts, saved responses, reference annotations and scoring code for the 80-request controlled benchmark, 240-request stress benchmark and 30-request extended benchmark, together with paired prompt-development records. Device records cover inference, request-to-schedule integration, resource monitoring and rolling scheduling on RK3588. The release provides source code, frozen inputs, raw results, machine-readable tables, independent data checks and a unified desktop reproduction entry point for Tables 1-10 and S1 and Figures 1-6 and S1. A result index links each output to its inputs and scripts. Dependency specifications, RK3588 operating instructions, component licenses and SHA-256 checksums accompany the archive. Research code is distributed under the MIT License. Research data, derived results and figures use CC BY 4.0; third-party materials retain their accompanying licenses. Household data source: Open Power System Data, Data Package Household Data, version 2020-04-15, https://data.open-power-system-data.org/household_data/2020-04-15/.
title: Data and Code for Privacy-Aware Personalized Scheduling of Behind-the-Meter Energy Storage via an Edge-Resident Large Language Model

summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full and reliable lane-level traffic observations are available to all agents. In practice, urban road networks exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity (e.g., lane configurations and phase designs), while sensor failures and incomplete detector coverage often result in missing incoming lane measurements. Such issues can severely impair coordination and destabilize learning. To address these challenges, we propose HALight, a communication-enhanced heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for traffic signal control under lane-level missing observations. HALight supports intersection-specific observation and action modeling to accommodate heterogeneous intersections, and incorporates a lightweight one-hop neighborhood communication module to enrich spatial context when lane-level observations are partially unavailable. Moreover, HALight adopts a sequential policy update scheme to improve coordination among heterogeneous agents. Experimental results on two real-world road networks demonstrate that HALight outperforms representative homogeneous and heterogeneous baselines in terms of traffic efficiency and convergence behavior. The code and datasets used in this work are available at https://github.com/Huchenkaii/HALight.
title: HALight: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control under Lane-Level Missing Observations

summary: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: the main agent must issue useful subtasks, while subagents must return reliable evidence. Existing training either optimizes only the main agent or broadcasts the same team advantage to all agents, which can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful ones. We introduce LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning), a joint main-agent-subagent training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment. A training-time rubric evaluates the research utility of each subagent report and gates its inherited team advantage, while final-answer correctness remains the only team reward; no token, step, or speedup reward is used. Across five benchmarks and two model families, LEAD-RL improves answer quality. On BrowseComp, it improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5% over joint training with shared team credit. During validation, accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost. These results show that contribution-aware credit assignment improves the quality-efficiency trade-off of multi-agent deep research.
title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
