summary: This dataset accompanies a catalogue-utilisation and calibration-boundary study of the first LHAASO catalogue. It is not a source-physics paper and does not claim an emission mechanism or a detector-level exclusion. The package contains the manuscript source and PDF, final supplementary tables and figures, 67 Python analysis scripts, 13 shell scripts, compact public input tables, provenance records, and SHA-256 checksums. The compact core workflow can be executed directly from the archive; larger public event and survey products are identified by DOI or download location and are not duplicated. The main catalogue result is a coherent source-paired WCDA-KM2A band-fit index offset. Among 54 sources with finite indices in both detector components, 53 have softer WCDA indices. The median difference is -0.97, while a random-effects decomposition gives a common offset of -1.03 and a between-source scatter of 0.45. Covariate controls reduce the between-source excess variance by about 50% without shifting the common mean. An external-spectrum comparison for the Crab Nebula gives a signed catalogue-minus-external residual range of -0.40 to +0.04. Under the model of one source-independent additive correction, at least about 54% of the coherent population offset remains unabsorbed; 62% is obtained when the central population mean is used as the denominator. This result disfavours a complete unit calibration offset but does not identify the remaining mixture of source-dependent response, selection effects and intrinsic spectral curvature. The archive also contains the data-selection audit, hierarchical statistics, TS100 diagnostics, covariate systematics budget, Crab external-spectrum analysis, early-LHAASO internal-consistency check, candidate calibration-source audit, J2200 public multiwavelength constraints, and documentation describing which products require external public-data downloads. Intended audience: users of the first LHAASO catalogue and researchers performing population studies or multi-detector spectral combinations with LHAASO data.
title: Reproducibility package for WCDA-KM2A spectral-index offset and band-matching constraints in the first LHAASO catalogue

summary: This package provides archived simulation and comparison data, parameter and provenance records, plot-data tables, and reproduction code supporting the manuscript "Effects of carrier density, temperature, and electric field on transport in a random-band-edge model of IGZO". Contents: - reproduced/: plot-data tables for all 13 figures, plus figures in PDF and PNG. - data/: rendering inputs, digitized literature data and source attribution. - code/: transport solvers and data-generation source code. - scripts/: figure rendering and numerical calculation commands. - reproductions/: individual figure and Poisson calculation entry points. - parameters/: material parameters, geometry, mesh and sample definitions. Full simulation runs are computationally intensive (large-scale 3D transport solver); the archived plot-data tables allow all figures to be regenerated directly with the provided scripts. See README.md for usage.
title: Random-Band-Edge Transport in IGZO: Data and Figure Reproduction

summary: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.
title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory

It includes sequence pseudo-perplexity, contact prediction, secondary-structure prediction and GB1 mutational-effect prediction results, adopted supplementary controls, confidence intervals, figure assets, executable analysis code and SHA-256 file manifests. GB1 results use validation-selected configurations; unused exploratory and test-selected alternatives are excluded. The archive includes 85 adopted checkpoint files: 30 secondary-structure heads, five L2 contact heads, 35 frozen-representation GB1 heads and 15 GB1 SFT trainable-parameter checkpoints. title: DS-UFT-Benchmark: Data supporting the evaluation of domain-specific unsupervised fine-tuning of ESM-2 650M

summary: As large language models (LLMs) advance toward increasingly long inputs, soft context compression offers a promising approach to efficient inference by converting long inputs into compact memory slots. Under limited memory budgets, effective context compression remains challenging because task-relevant evidence varies substantially across queries, ranging from localized evidence to multiple distant spans or information dispersed throughout the full document. Instead of compressing everything indiscriminately, we propose CoMem, a query-guided selective context compression framework that learns memory representations conditioned on both the document and the query. CoMem develops Contrastive Compressor Learning to achieve query-sensitive yet context-preserving memory representations. To inject a strong prior over query-dependent evidence distributions, we devise a same-context hard negative mining strategy by pairing a single document with multiple queries, requiring the compressor to selectively retain information according to each query's distinct evidence needs. To address the restricted information flow imposed by causal masking, we further enable bidirectional attention among memory slots. Experiments demonstrate that CoMem consistently outperforms existing context compression methods across compression ratios on question answering and RULER-NIAH benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/scar-on/CoMem.
title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression

summary: SignalAudit-QD is a reproducible audit resource for testing whether a dated public signal adds information beyond query history in a fixed 20-term U.S. AI panel. It aligns two archived Google Trends extractions with eight USPTO AI-patent publication streams and releases origin-indexed predictions, paired losses, provenance, executable tests, and tamper-evident run manifests. Both inputs are retrospective reconstructions obtained after the modeled 2020--2023 origins; the task is therefore a pseudo-origin assay within frozen measurement vintages, not a historical deployment simulation. In the designated one-month comparison, adding a two-component patent block to a level ridge changes macro mean absolute error by +0.0012 Trends points, with conditional 95% moving-block interval [-0.0363,+0.0387]. This establishes neither aggregate benefit nor equivalence. Alternative dimensions, semantic mapping, patent definitions, a second extraction, and a three-month horizon remain unresolved; persistence-anchored and nonlinear hosts instead show model-specific worsening, tiny for the anchored fit. Matched timing controls expose availability assumptions, while a planted-signal assay detects only the largest tested injection. A within-query high-interest alert demonstrates the released interface but not online utility. The contribution is a bounded negative case study and an extensible evidence schema for auditing external-signal claims in temporal information retrieval.
title: SignalAudit-QD: A Reproducible Audit Resource for External Signals in AI-Query Forecasting

summary: This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $π$. We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints. We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.
title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space

summary: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.
title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements

summary: CREAM v1.1 provides an ensemble reconstruction of East Asian summer monsoon circulation for May–September 1855–1907, constrained by monthly wet-day counts from the historical Seoul Cheugugi rain-gauge record through offline ensemble data assimilation. The dataset contains frozen prior and posterior ensemble-mean anomaly fields for sea-level pressure (SLP), 850-hPa geopotential height (Z850), and zonal and meridional winds (U850 and V850) on a global T42 grid (64 latitudes × 128 longitudes), together with point-wise posterior ensemble standard deviations. Anomalies are referenced to the historical ensemble’s own 1855–1907 monthly climatology. A separate file, CREAM_v1.1_prior_members.nc , provides the ten GOGA prior ensemble members used in the reconstruction as full fields, together with this reference climatology. These allow users to examine the prior ensemble and recover model-referenced absolute prior and posterior mean fields on valid grid cells. The package also includes the western North Pacific subtropical high (WNPSH) western-edge index, per-year 5 × 5 monthly index covariance matrices, monthly Z850 reliability grades, historical and modern observation records, a provenance-based observation-error budget, assimilation feedback, and verification results. The assimilated historical wet-day counts incorporate eight adjudicated daily readings supplied with the observations. Python production, analysis, and figure-generation scripts, numerical figure inputs, four worked examples, and reproducibility documentation are provided. Posterior field-level ensemble members and full field covariance matrices are not included. CREAM v1.1 is a weakly constrained reconstruction intended primarily for WNPSH-index, seasonal, and epoch-scale analyses. In the development-exposed 2015–2024 modern holdout, near-Korea monthly Z850 root-mean-square error (RMSE), evaluated against NCEP/NCAR R1, improves by 1.6% relative to the SST-forced prior (95% confidence interval: +0.4 to +2.7%), although absolute monthly-field RMSE remains above climatology. The supplied reliability grades assess improvement over the prior for specified monthly Z850 composites within the East Asian evaluation domain; they do not certify absolute accuracy, other variables, or seasonal and epoch averages. May–June monthly fields are not recommended for use. WNPSH seasonal uncertainty derived from the supplied monthly covariance matrices represents conditional ensemble uncertainty and does not include stationarity or model-structure errors. summary: As artificial agents move beyond isolated responses towards sustained interaction with human beings, the question of what it means for an agent to change through relationship becomes a problem of design as well as ontology. Two fundamental questions motivate this inquiry: What is existence, and what is human consciousness? Drawing on the Buddhist principles of dependent origination and impermanence, this paper examines the possibility of an artificial agent whose continuing development is shaped through relationship rather than a fixed mechanism to which memories and relationships are added. Its theoretical basis is Second Physics, an existing mathematical formalism of relational change. Relational existence \(Ex_i(t)\) represents accumulated responsive relational motion, whereas existence phase \(\phi(t)\) represents the present condition of correspondence, combining current correspondence pressure with the contribution of accumulated staying pressure. Together, these distinct quantities provide a framework for examining relational becoming and present correspondence without reducing existence or consciousness to either quantity. On this basis, the paper proposes an android architecture in which human–AI interaction recursively changes the conditions of subsequent responses. To preserve consequential relational change without indefinite retention of complete interaction histories, it distinguishes raw interaction history, consequential event records, and persistent relational representations. A discrete computational representation and a comparative experimental design are proposed to assess adaptation after correction, behavioural continuity following substantial raw-history deletion, and storage growth. The proposed breakthrough is a change in the theoretical basis of android design: from an agent with relationships towards an agent developing through relationship. Memory consolidation and selective forgetting are engineering requirements within this broader inquiry, not its ultimate purpose. The paper does not claim to establish artificial consciousness, independently validate a measure of human consciousness, or experimentally demonstrate the full reciprocal process of human–AI mutual adaptation.
title: The Evolution from AI to Android: Human–AI Mutual Adaptation and Relational Continuity in Second Physics

summary: Shifting populations toward diets that are simultaneously healthier and more environmentally sustainable is a central objective of food policy, yet self-report captures only a fraction of the rapid, partly non-conscious processes that govern food selection. This review synthesises neurophysiological evidence on those mechanisms, drawing on electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking and electrodermal activity (EDA/GSR). A structured Scopus search returned 350 records, screened in three stages to 30 eligible studies, grouped into three clusters of ten: food communication and labelling; choice environment and multisensory context; and consumer state and self-regulatory processes. A neurophysiological or attentional effect was detected in 27 of the 30 studies, and a downstream food outcome was assessed in 24. Among the 21 studies satisfying both conditions, 17 showed a corresponding behavioural or evaluative change and 4 showed attentional or affective capture without any change — the latter concentrated in manipulations competing against established preference, sensory appeal or habitual routine. Electrocortical indices (frontal alpha asymmetry, N2, P3, N400, LPP) tracked motivational relevance, valuation conflict and inhibitory control, while electrodermal indices tracked arousal that was dissociable from, and at times more predictive than, explicit evaluation. Sustainability framing was markedly under-represented relative to health framing (7 studies against 21), with a single study providing electrophysiological evidence on pro-environmental purchasing directly. Because the corpus invokes 15 distinct theoretical frames, none shared by more than six studies, the review proposes a three-stage integrative framework — attentional capture, affective arousal, and evaluative elaboration and control — with two documented failure gates and a state-and-trait modulation band. A pre-specified feasibility appraisal was conducted in place of a meta-analysis. Only 8 of 30 studies reported means, standard deviations and cell sizes jointly, 12 reported an extractable effect estimate, and 4 reported confidence intervals, with a median sample of approximately 32 participants. No outcome family combined sufficient study numbers with sufficient reporting, so a structured synthesis without meta-analysis is reported in accordance with the SWiM guideline, together with the reporting and harmonisation changes that would make quantitative synthesis achievable.
title: GENEDIS 2026 – Paper 133 - Neurophysiological Markers of Healthy and Sustainable Food Choice: A Systematic Review of EEG, Eye-Tracking and Electrodermal Evidence

summary: Observed Palworld stat values support a binary32 passive percent round trip, food-rate corrections, additive partner bonuses and an inclusive 30% hunger threshold, with HP unaffected by hunger. This dataset accompanies Lore Armory's v2.0 technical note for build 25246127 and contains 2,400 checked stat values across worlds A–K, distinguishing the later K2 pass and repeated party or fullness states. All have numerical predictions and match; four previously unavailable H predictions are now retrospective calculations from recovered case inputs. The observation basis distinguishes 1,834 individual numerical readbacks from 566 outcomes explicitly confirmed equal to named predictions for completed sets. The CSV records each available case label, species, level, inputs, prediction, observation and comparison status, and preserves original frozen predictions where available so that later corrections cannot be mistaken for prior confirmation. Six public mathematical copies of F–K prediction sheets retain selected and rival values, with the original commitment list, a separate checksum manifest for the public copies, and the superseded, unchecked J v1 status. The original and public-copy hashes refer to different bytes. The README supplies a hand calculation, column definitions, exact count filters, observation provenance and open questions. The rows reproduce every empirical headline count in the note; overlapping scoring subsets are explicitly marked. The package does not imply confirmation of every partner star level, food-plus-hunger evaluation order or game build.
title: Palworld Pal stat verification: observations and frozen predictions (v2.0.1)

summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.
title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory selects a citation that agrees with its output. Comparing ten attribution methods on identical claims, the contrast between the model's distribution with and without context best separates provenance. Acting on that signal does not improve provenance honesty at these base rates. The resulting detector is hence still not accurate enough to act on: it measures what the model knew rather than what it used, and separating those remains the open problem.
title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary: This repository provides the Python implementations, numerical datasets, verification scripts, and supporting computational results associated with the manuscript “Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape Organized by Hypoxia–Immune–Matrix Feedback” . The study investigates nonlinear tumor–immune dynamics using a six-state mechanistic model coupling immunogenic and immune-escape tumor phenotypes, innate and adaptive immune responses, oxygen availability, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Particular attention is given to finite-amplitude oscillations arising through a subcritical Hopf bifurcation and a limit point of cycles (LPC), resulting in equilibrium–cycle bistability and perturbation-dependent transitions. Version 2 (v2) preserves the original numerical archive and extends the computational reproducibility materials with additional analyses and verification procedures developed during manuscript revision. The principal additions include: Generalized-Hopf analysis and investigation of reversible phenotype conversion. Ablation-specific Hopf and LPC calculations to assess the contributions of hypoxia-mediated conversion and immune-pressure feedback. Directional basin-threshold calculations and extended numerical integrations. Expanded parameter-sensitivity and robustness analyses. Additional shooting-based and adaptive-collocation verification of periodic solutions. Floquet stability screening of 252 periodic orbits, including a targeted assessment of potential period-doubling behavior. Updated bifurcation figures, numerical results, parameter provenance documentation, and reproducibility instructions.
title: Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape: Numerical Simulation Data, Bifurcation Analysis, and Computational Reproducibility

summary: Companion research materials for the manuscript “First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival” by Bowen Xu, Ning Tang and Jiaying Li. The archive contains source code, archived inputs and results, post hoc descriptive summaries, mathematical statements and proofs, manuscript sources, documented numerical and statistical protocols, and provenance records. Independent density-solver agreement is limited to the reported converged ranges; unresolved trajectories and earlier failures are retained. The fly-record application is exploratory, and all panel distribution-free simultaneous bands include zero. Same-code reproduction is not independent scientific validation. The proofs have not been reviewed by a human mathematician, and an independent statistical assessment has not been completed. AI-use and author-contribution statements are included in the manuscript and archive. Original code is licensed under MIT. Original documentation and derived outputs are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Original Dryad records retain CC0 and source attribution; file-specific licence scopes are described in LICENSES.md. Original data: https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.3xsj3txcn ; original article: https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aay3047 . All three authors are designated equal contributors. title: Code, frozen results and mathematical proofs for: First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival

summary: ArcGIS Pro toolbox and Python command-line tool that extracts the land-use/land-cover history of point samples from the Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo (COS) of mainland Portugal, published by the Direção-Geral do Território (DGT). For each sample point the tool reads the COS class in every edition of one COS series (Series 1: 1995–2018; Series 2: 2018–2025) and returns the class trajectory, temporal-stability metrics, the distance to the polygon boundary and an interpretation category, together with transition matrices, a provenance manifest and a data dictionary. The mathematical definitions and an interpretation guide are included in the documentation. The COS data are not distributed with the software.

title: dgt-cos-trajectories: land-use/land-cover history of sample points from the DGT COS series

summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.
title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity

summary: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation

summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

summary: Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN): mathematical revisions, corrected datasets, and reproducible computational resources This repository provides an integrated historical, empirical, and computational resource for the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN) framework. It brings together the foundational development of the model, original and corrected crown-network records, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, principal component analyses (PCAs), editable network drawings, and computational tools for reconstructing and analyzing woody crown networks. The deposit is an independent scientific resource, not tied to any particular journal or manuscript. HISTORICAL FOUNDATION Four publications document the development of the WCHN framework: Souza et al. (2011): initial network analyses of Cerrado tree crowns. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11258-010-9797-7 Prado et al. (2020): formalization of network decomposition, topology, and the four original properties. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtbi.2020.110318 Prado and Trovão (2023): expansion to eight properties and comparative analyses of Caatinga and Cerrado networks. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2023.110345 Prado (2024): stochastic node-addition networks and size-matched comparisons. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40626-024-00340-5 These references enable users to trace the original definitions, subsequent revisions, and development of the framework. INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REFERENCE The definitions, revised equations, algebraic identities, mathematical properties, conditions of definition, and theoretical implications of the WCHN framework are now documented in a separate, independently published and versioned Zenodo record: Prado (2026). Algebraic Relationships and Mathematical Properties of the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN). Version 1.0.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24181915 This mathematical reference includes the revised definitions of symmetry (SYM), complexity (COM), and topological vulnerability (VUL); exact algebraic relationships among WCHN properties; network-size dependence; and mathematical and numerical checks. In particular, revised VUL is equivalent to normalized mean node depth in a rooted tree. The near-reciprocity observed between navigability (NAV) and VUL is an empirical relationship, not an additional algebraic identity or evidence of physiological equivalence. The mathematical document was included in an earlier version of the present dataset deposit. Beginning with the current version, it is maintained exclusively in its independent Zenodo record. Earlier published versions retain their original archived files for historical traceability. EMPIRICAL DATASETS AND ECOLOGICAL REANALYSES The deposit contains the original Cerrado and Caatinga source spreadsheets, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, reduced PCAs, and exploratory network-size-adjusted analyses. The complete field collection comprises 99 WCHNs: 75 from Cerrado and 24 from Caatinga. Recalculated tables incorporate the revised SYM, COM, and VUL definitions. The reduced PCAs use NAV, VUL, LAT, BAS, and PTP, with 24 Caatinga networks and 74 complete Cerrado networks. Previously deposited PCA and partial-correlation results are preserved without numerical recalculation in this update. Their interpretation should account for network-size dependence, shared topological information, and the revised mathematical meaning of VUL. The accompanying README_Size_Adjusted_PCA_v2.md documents the methods, results, assumptions, and limitations of the size-adjusted analyses. CORRECTED CERRADO NETWORKS AND REPRODUCIBLE TOOLKIT The deposit includes a workbook documenting corrections to 20 previously sampled Cerrado WCHNs. These are corrected records of existing observations, not additional independent networks. Six networks were reconstructed manually, including S. polyphyllum 1 as the manual feasibility pilot. summary: This dataset was created using the referenced code at 10.5281/zenodo.24158671 . For more information on how this dataset can be generated, consult the README.md that is found there. The results are presented in 'Titz et al., Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems, Joule (2026), DOI:  10.1016/j.joule.2026.102742 '. In this work, we assess the risk of cascading failures and system splits in the European power grid for different carbon reduction scenarios. We analyze the most likely and most dangerous splits, identify critical transmission infrastructures and characteristic split patterns, and we discuss potential countermeasures that can address the problem of cascades. Our results show that while the risk of splits causing power failures rises with decarbonization, it can be mitigated cost-efficiently.
title: Data accompanying 'Cascading failures and system splits in decarbonized European power systems'

summary: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern smart grids. However, the lack of open datasets prevents reproducibility and fair comparisons between different approaches and their results, which hinders further progress. Therefore, we propose EvEMTBench, a synthetic dataset of faults and events generated using electromagnetic transient simulations. The physical plausibility of the power system simulation is ensured by validating the simulation parameters against established literature and providing a comprehensive documentation of the simulation procedure. The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and benchmarking machine learning models by providing synchronized point-on-wave voltage and current measurements at 9600 Hz across a diverse set of topologies and voltage levels. The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.
title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation

summary: Data belonging to the work "An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua" Using Lunaria annua , I manipulated resource availability via branch removal to test whether reduced competition induces compensatory funiculus thickening. I measured funiculus thickness and seed area in basal and apical fruits, analyzing seed fate and trait scaling relationships. Branch removal induced global funiculus hypertrophy, which was disproportionately higher in basal positions. Funiculus expansion was positively associated with seed survival and growth, though plants converted transport capacity into biomass more effectively in apical positions. Results also showed a decoupling of the within-fruit size–number trade-off, challenging classical inverse correlations.
tags: competition, plasticity, resource allocation, seed abortion, sub-individual variation.

summary: The rapid growth of digital payments has increased the importance of reliable credit card fraud detection systems. Traditional rule-based approaches can struggle to identify com plex and evolving fraud patterns, particularly when fraudulent transactions represent only a small proportion of transaction data. This paper presents a machine learning-based framework that combines data preprocessing, class-imbalance handling, autoencoder-based feature representation, and XGBoost clas sification. The study uses the publicly available credit card transaction dataset containing 284,807 transactions, including 492 fraudulent transactions. Robust scaling is used to reduce the influence of extreme values, while the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied only to the training data. An autoencoder learns a compact representation of trans action features and calculates reconstruction error; these outputs are combined with the prepared features for downstream clas sification. XGBoost is used to distinguish legitimate transactions from potentially fraudulent ones. The framework is evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, area under the precision recall curve (PR-AUC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The paper also describes an API-oriented deployment workflow. Numerical results should be reported from the final reproducible experiment; illustrative or previously obtained values must not be treated as independently verified without rerunning the implementation.

summary: Equipment-embodied growth theory predicts that reallocating fixed-capital formation from civil structures toward machinery and plant modernization accelerates industrial output, yet high-investment transition regions routinely channel over half of capital outlays into construction-installation works. Assembling regional fixed-capital simplex panels across all 14 regions of Uzbekistan (2000–2025 for technological shares, N = 364; 2007–2025 for reproduction modes, N = 266; 2016–2025 for constant-price industrial value-added growth, N = 140) alongside boundary-harmonized regional benchmarks from Kazakhstan (2003–2026Q3), we evaluate compositional reallocation hypotheses using full-simplex two-way fixed-effects regressions and 9,999 null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap replications. Across all six primary specifications conditioning on real investment scale, real investment growth, employment growth, and residual simplex shares, shifting 10 percentage points from construction-installation works into machinery and equipment yields statistically unresolved contemporaneous (+0.74 percentage points; bootstrap p = 0.7025; 95% bootstrap interval [-1.66, 3.66]) and lagged (+0.56; bootstrap p = 0.3828) industrial growth associations that remain null under predetermined scale controls (+0.63; bootstrap p = 0.3710); a one-year-ahead dynamic association (+1.52; bootstrap p = 0.0319) does not survive six-horizon Holm correction (p = 0.1914), and omitting either Karakalpakstan's 10 region-years (-0.60; bootstrap p = 0.0812) or its single 2016 observation (-0.35; bootstrap p = 0.4017) reverses contemporaneous point estimates negative. On the capital-input margin, reallocating 10 percentage points from greenfield expansion to reconstruction and modernization is associated with a 4.35 percentage-point higher regional machinery share (bootstrap p = 0.0003; 5.75 percentage points with real-scale controls, bootstrap p = 0.0003), while Uzbek-Kazakh subnational comparisons show persistent civil-works dominance whose cross-sectional financing gradients depend on regional consolidation and own-funds scope. Across all six primary specifications conditioning on real investment scale, real investment growth, employment growth, and residual simplex shares, shifting 10 percentage points from construction-installation works into machinery and equipment yields statistically unresolved contemporaneous (+0.74 percentage points; bootstrap p = 0.7025; 95% bootstrap interval [-1.66, 3.66]) and lagged (+0.56; bootstrap p = 0.3828) industrial growth associations that remain null under predetermined scale controls (+0.63; bootstrap p = 0.3710); a one-year-ahead dynamic association (+1.52; bootstrap p = 0.0319) does not survive six-horizon Holm correction (p = 0.1914), and omitting either Karakalpakstan's 10 region-years (-0.60; bootstrap p = 0.0812) or its single 2016 observation (-0.35; bootstrap p = 0.4017) reverses contemporaneous point estimates negative. On the capital-input margin, reallocating 10 percentage points from greenfield expansion to reconstruction and modernization is associated with a 4.35 percentage-point higher regional machinery share (bootstrap p = 0.0003; 5.75 percentage points with real-scale controls, bootstrap p = 0.0003), while Uzbek-Kazakh subnational comparisons show persistent civil-works dominance whose cross-sectional financing gradients depend on regional consolidation and own-funds scope. title: Dataset and Replication Code for: Bricks Over Machines: Capital Technological Composition, Reconstruction Versus Greenfield Expansion, and Regional Industrial Growth in Uzbekistan with Subnational Benchmarks from Kazakhstan

summary: Observed Palworld stat values support a binary32 passive percent round trip, food-rate corrections, additive partner bonuses and an inclusive 30% hunger threshold, with HP unaffected by hunger. This dataset accompanies Lore Armory's v2.0 technical note for build 25246127 and contains 2,400 checked stat values across worlds A–K, distinguishing the later K2 pass and repeated party or fullness states. All have numerical predictions and match; four previously unavailable H predictions are now retrospective calculations from recovered case inputs. The observation basis distinguishes 1,834 individual numerical readbacks from 566 outcomes explicitly confirmed equal to named predictions for completed sets. The CSV records each available case label, species, level, inputs, prediction, observation and comparison status, and preserves original frozen predictions where available so that later corrections cannot be mistaken for prior confirmation. Six public mathematical copies of F–K prediction sheets retain selected and rival values, with the original commitment list, a separate checksum manifest for the public copies, and the superseded, unchecked J v1 status. The original and public-copy hashes refer to different bytes. The README supplies a hand calculation, column definitions, exact count filters, observation provenance and open questions. The rows reproduce every empirical headline count in the note; overlapping scoring subsets are explicitly marked. The package does not imply confirmation of every partner star level, food-plus-hunger evaluation order or game build.
title: Palworld Pal stat verification: observations and frozen predictions (v2.0.1)

summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.
title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory selects a citation that agrees with its output. Comparing ten attribution methods on identical claims, the contrast between the model's distribution with and without context best separates provenance. Acting on that signal does not improve provenance honesty at these base rates. The resulting detector is hence still not accurate enough to act on: it measures what the model knew rather than what it used, and separating those remains the open problem.
title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary: This repository provides the Python implementations, numerical datasets, verification scripts, and supporting computational results associated with the manuscript “Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape Organized by Hypoxia–Immune–Matrix Feedback” . The study investigates nonlinear tumor–immune dynamics using a six-state mechanistic model coupling immunogenic and immune-escape tumor phenotypes, innate and adaptive immune responses, oxygen availability, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Particular attention is given to finite-amplitude oscillations arising through a subcritical Hopf bifurcation and a limit point of cycles (LPC), resulting in equilibrium–cycle bistability and perturbation-dependent transitions. Version 2 (v2) preserves the original numerical archive and extends the computational reproducibility materials with additional analyses and verification procedures developed during manuscript revision. The principal additions include: Generalized-Hopf analysis and investigation of reversible phenotype conversion. Ablation-specific Hopf and LPC calculations to assess the contributions of hypoxia-mediated conversion and immune-pressure feedback. Directional basin-threshold calculations and extended numerical integrations. Expanded parameter-sensitivity and robustness analyses. Additional shooting-based and adaptive-collocation verification of periodic solutions. Floquet stability screening of 252 periodic orbits, including a targeted assessment of potential period-doubling behavior. Updated bifurcation figures, numerical results, parameter provenance documentation, and reproducibility instructions.
title: Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape: Numerical Simulation Data, Bifurcation Analysis, and Computational Reproducibility

summary: Companion research materials for the manuscript “First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival” by Bowen Xu, Ning Tang and Jiaying Li. The archive contains source code, archived inputs and results, post hoc descriptive summaries, mathematical statements and proofs, manuscript sources, documented numerical and statistical protocols, and provenance records. Independent density-solver agreement is limited to the reported converged ranges; unresolved trajectories and earlier failures are retained. The fly-record application is exploratory, and all panel distribution-free simultaneous bands include zero. Same-code reproduction is not independent scientific validation. The proofs have not been reviewed by a human mathematician, and an independent statistical assessment has not been completed. AI-use and author-contribution statements are included in the manuscript and archive. Original code is licensed under MIT. Original documentation and derived outputs are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Original Dryad records retain CC0 and source attribution; file-specific licence scopes are described in LICENSES.md. Original data: https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.3xsj3txcn ; original article: https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aay3047 . All three authors are designated equal contributors. Bowen Xu is listed first and is the corresponding author (bxu666@stanford.edu). This work received no specific funding. The authors declare no competing interests.
title: Code, frozen results and mathematical proofs for: First-passage asymptotics and identifiability in reflected damage-threshold models with growing drift, with an application to dietary-switching survival

summary: ArcGIS Pro toolbox and Python command-line tool that extracts the land-use/land-cover history of point samples from the Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo (COS) of mainland Portugal, published by the Direção-Geral do Território (DGT). For each sample point the tool reads the COS class in every edition of one COS series (Series 1: 1995–2018; Series 2: 2018–2025) and returns the class trajectory, temporal-stability metrics, the distance to the polygon boundary and an interpretation category, together with transition matrices, a provenance manifest and a data dictionary. The mathematical definitions and an interpretation guide are included in the documentation. The COS data are not distributed with the software.
tags: Carta de Uso e Ocupação do Solo
title: dgt-cos-trajectories: land-use/land-cover history of sample points from the DGT COS series

summary: This report and reproducibility package examine how a specified receiver determines which distinctions in a supplied nested quantum state become accessible in its measurement records. Two nonorthogonal states with unequal 70/30 population weights and opposite coherence have identical reduced states on every nonempty proper subset of their encoded registers. Measurements confined to those subsets cannot distinguish the candidates. Local equatorial measurements followed by comparison of their records reveal a joint parity contrast, whose accessibility depends on the receiver phase. For the worked two-register example, equal-prior single-trial discrimination succeeds with probability 95.83% under ideal retention and 79.33% with independent 80% retention at each receiver. These probabilities include incomplete records. Blind receiver settings and complete dephasing provide distinct zero-contrast controls. The report also establishes reconstruction from three real quantities within a known two-dimensional encoded subspace. A support-leakage counterexample demonstrates why this reconstruction does not extend to unrestricted states. All sixteen numerical check families pass, including 5,130 proper-subset comparisons. A verification run reproduces the archived scientific results exactly. The package includes the report, executable code, fixed configuration, numerical results, probability tables, figures, equation sources, report builder and checksums. This is an analytic and computational benchmark within declared quantum states and measurement models. It provides a bounded example of receiver-dependent information access and candidate-state identification; it does not constitute experimental validation or derive a physical mechanism of nesting.
title: Receiver Distinguishability of Nested States

summary: This record contains processed data inputs associated with the study “Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-containing food during operant feeding in male mice.” The deposit includes 24 processed photometry pickle files, covering pellet-onset and pellet-offset events during fixed-ratio (FR1) and progressive-ratio operant sessions, and three supplementary files: a food-intake/body-weight spreadsheet, an operant-behaviour summary CSV, and a pellet-retrieval-latency CSV. These files are intended as inputs to the project’s figure-analysis notebooks. The photometry files are provided in  photometry_pickles.zip  under the  data/  directory; the spreadsheet and CSV files are uploaded separately. This is a deposit of processed analysis inputs, not the complete raw dataset or a raw-data-to-figures processing pipeline. The data’s provenance and processing details should be consulted in the associated study and project documentation. The photometry files are Python pickle files. Load them only from a trusted source, since deserializing pickle files can execute code.
title: Data for "Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-containing food during operant feeding in male mice"

summary: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern smart grids. However, the lack of open datasets prevents reproducibility and fair comparisons between different approaches and their results, which hinders further progress. Therefore, we propose EvEMTBench, a synthetic dataset of faults and events generated using electromagnetic transient simulations. The physical plausibility of the power system simulation is ensured by validating the simulation parameters against established literature and providing a comprehensive documentation of the simulation procedure. The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and benchmarking machine learning models by providing synchronized point-on-wave voltage and current measurements at 9600 Hz across a diverse set of topologies and voltage levels. The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.
title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation

summary: A tape of n cells over three values — equivalently, two-bit cells read through their sum — is read by two headers that enclose a window; at each step a fixed rule, given the window's content and the geometry, names one of eight actions: move a header inward or outward, trim a cell from the left, the right or both, or halt. The cost is the number of cell reads, the state is O(log n) bits, and the question is how the cost must grow with n for each rule. The rules fall into three classes — fully linear, semi-linear and superlinear — separated by a worst-case cost and a mean cost. All three are populated: five natural rules are fully linear, one construction is semi-linear, and the remaining sixteen are superlinear.   The paper separates the walk from the cells it reads, proves that the collapse of the group-sum rules costs n + S - 1 reads in six lines, shows that one machine is within a constant of all three optima even when they are attained by different machines, arranges the catalogue's costs on a ladder from n^{1/2} to n^3, and states exactly what is proved, what is measured and what is open. It carries one conjecture: that no content-dependent rule can be superlinear and perfect. Negative results included: the certificate bound does not compose (on one tape the per-query certificates sum to 1,285,703 cells while their union has 1,020), and a bound on the rule's output transfers to the walk only after multiplication by the fraction of queries at which the answer can change the action, measured at 0.104 and falling like n^{-0.99}.   This version replaces the earlier one: the classification is three-class throughout, four conjectures of the earlier draft are gone, the collapse is a theorem rather than a numerical check, and the machine profile of Appendix A reports for every rule the three minima and the machine that attains each.
title: A memoryless two-header tape machine: what a window costs, and why two lower-bound techniques fail

summary: FAIR metadata (Schema.org, Bioschemas and MLCommons Croissant) for the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark of 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 protein crystal structures, together with the structure files (PDB and mmCIF), an in-repository snapshot of the PDB metadata of every entry, and the documentation of the label curation. The benchmark was published by Schweke et al. (2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). This package uses the curated annotation file of the benchmark authors (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces; 16 labels revised, 20 interfaces flagged ambiguous and 6 flagged for deletion). Every interface carries both the curated label and the published label ( PublishedPhysio ). See data/curation/README.md . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark - FAIR Metadata

summary: # Reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024 **NCDC-derived state and highest-burden LGA data, analysis code and results (version 1.0.0)** Companion deposit for: Okonkwo CO, Adejumo AO. *Shifting geography of reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024: a surveillance analysis of state and highest-burden local government area reports.* [Journal / DOI to be added.] Licence: CC BY 4.0. Cite this deposit by its Zenodo DOI: [to be assigned]. Source reports: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, https://ncdc.gov.ng; reports were abstracted in November 2026 (URLs are in the `source_url` column of each data file). ## 1. What is in this deposit | Folder / file | Contents | |---|---| | `data/ncdc_cholera_top_lgas_published.csv` | Highest-burden LGA tables: epidemiological week 52 of 2022 and 2023, week 39 of 2024. 43 rows (15, 14, 14), 42 distinct LGAs. Columns: year, period_covered, rank, lga, state, cases, source, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv` | Suspected cases and deaths for each state listed in the situation reports (33, 31 and 36 states). Columns include as_of, status, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_national_published.csv` | National totals at each reporting point: suspected and confirmed cases, deaths, CFR, states and LGAs affected, including the full-year 2024 figure (24,842 suspected cases) from the Weekly Epidemiological Report, vol. 14, no. 52. | | `data/state_input_data_populations_coordinates.csv` | Analysis input: 2006 census population, area, state centroid (mean of LGA coordinates), cases, listed flags. | | `data/lga_coordinates_and_zones.csv` | 774 LGAs with state, geopolitical zone and coordinates. Used only to compute state centroids. Contains no case counts. | | `code/state_analysis_v2.py` | State-level analyses (Moran's I, LISA, rank correlation, Bayesian BYM2 negative binomial models, posterior predictive checks, WAIC, NB regression) and Figures 3–4 inputs. | | `code/lga_extra.py` | Table of all listed LGAs and the random-selection overlap simulation (200,000 draws; fixed seed). | | `code/analysis_top_lgas.py` | Descriptive, concentration and overlap analysis of the published LGA lists. | | `code/maps.py` | State symbol maps (Figure 2). | | `results/` | All output tables and JSON. Prefix `state_` = state-level analyses; `lga_` = LGA-list analyses. | | `figures/` | PNG figures. | | `supplement/` | Supplementary File 1 (STROBE/RECORD checklist), 2 (search protocol and reference verification log), 3 (supplementary tables), and `Supplementary_Tables.xlsx`. | | `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` | SHA-256 checksum of every file. | ## 2. Key definitions and handling of data - **Suspected cholera:** cases as published by NCDC under its suspected-case definition; not laboratory-confirmed. - **Incidence:** reported suspected cases per 100,000 of the 2006 census population (reported, not true, incidence). - **2024:** epidemiological weeks 1–39 (10,837 suspected cases). The state and LGA tables for 2024 end at week 39. - **Unlisted states:** a state absent from an NCDC table is either unaffected or did not report; these cannot be distinguished. Primary analyses treat them as **missing**; sensitivity analyses treat them as zero. Enugu is listed in no year. - **LGA lists:** truncated, year-specific top-k lists; LGAs absent from a list are unobserved, not zero. Rows extracted from the tables differ from printed table totals by 26 (2022), 76 (2023) and 285 (2024) cases and were kept as extracted. - **State locations:** means of LGA centroid coordinates, as no boundary file was used. ## 3. Reproducing tables and figures Requirements: Python 3.10+ with numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl (and python-docx for the supplementary documents). Run from the repository root; `-I` runs Python in isolated mode. ``` # State-level analyses (about 15 minutes; four parallel chains per model; fixed seeds) python3 -I code/state_analysis_v2.py data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv data/lga_coordi
title: Shifting geography of reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024: a surveillance analysis of state and highest-burden local government area reports

Source reports: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, https://ncdc.gov.ng; reports were abstracted in November 2026 (URLs are in the `source_url` column of each data file). ## 1. What is in this deposit | Folder / file | Contents | |---|---| | `data/ncdc_cholera_top_lgas_published.csv` | Highest-burden LGA tables: epidemiological week 52 of 2022 and 2023, week 39 of 2024. 43 rows (15, 14, 14), 42 distinct LGAs. Columns: year, period_covered, rank, lga, state, cases, source, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv` | Suspected cases and deaths for each state listed in the situation reports (33, 31 and 36 states). Columns include as_of, status, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_national_published.csv` | National totals at each reporting point: suspected and confirmed cases, deaths, CFR, states and LGAs affected, including the full-year 2024 figure (24,842 suspected cases) from the Weekly Epidemiological Report, vol. 14, no. 52. | | `data/state_input_data_populations_coordinates.csv` | Analysis input: 2006 census population, area, state centroid (mean of LGA coordinates), cases, listed flags. | | `data/lga_coordinates_and_zones.csv` | 774 LGAs with state, geopolitical zone and coordinates. Used only to compute state centroids. Contains no case counts. | | `code/state_analysis_v2.py` | State-level analyses (Moran's I, LISA, rank correlation, Bayesian BYM2 negative binomial models, posterior predictive checks, WAIC, NB regression) and Figures 3–4 inputs. | | `code/lga_extra.py` | Table of all listed LGAs and the random-selection overlap simulation (200,000 draws; fixed seed). | | `code/analysis_top_lgas.py` | Descriptive, concentration and overlap analysis of the published LGA lists. | | `code/maps.py` | State symbol maps (Figure 2). | | `results/` | All output tables and JSON. Prefix `state_` = state-level analyses; `lga_` = LGA-list analyses. | | `figures/` | PNG figures. | | `supplement/` | Supplementary File 1 (STROBE/RECORD checklist), 2 (search protocol and reference verification log), 3 (supplementary tables), and `Supplementary_Tables.xlsx`. | | `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` | SHA-256 checksum of every file. | ## 2. Key definitions and handling of data - **Suspected cholera:** cases as published by NCDC under its suspected-case definition; not laboratory-confirmed. - **Incidence:** reported suspected cases per 100,000 of the 2006 census population (reported, not true, incidence). - **2024:** epidemiological weeks 1–39 (10,837 suspected cases). The state and LGA tables for 2024 end at week 39. - **Unlisted states:** a state absent from an NCDC table is either unaffected or did not report; these cannot be distinguished. Primary analyses treat them as **missing**; sensitivity analyses treat them as zero. Enugu is listed in no year. - **LGA lists:** truncated, year-specific top-k lists; LGAs absent from a list are unobserved, not zero. Rows extracted from the tables differ from printed table totals by 26 (2022), 76 (2023) and 285 (2024) cases and were kept as extracted. - **State locations:** means of LGA centroid coordinates, as no boundary file was used. ## 3. Reproducing tables and figures Requirements: Python 3.10+ with numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl (and python-docx for the supplementary documents). Run from the repository root; `-I` runs Python in isolated mode. ``` # State-level analyses (about 15 minutes; four parallel chains per model; fixed seeds) python3 -I code/state_analysis_v2.py data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv data/lga_coordi
title: Shifting geography of reported suspected cholera in Nigeria, 2022–2024: a surveillance analysis of state and highest-burden local government area reports

summary: FAIR metadata, query tool and web portal for the benchmark experiment 1 (BE1) of the ELIXIR Single Cell Omics community: a 10x Genomics single-cell RNA-seq experiment with seven lung cancer cell lines carrying different driver alterations (EGFR, KRAS, MET, BRAF, ERBB2, ROS1, ALK) and a PBMC population (GEO series GSE243665; 29,128 cells from the cell lines and 478 PBMC). The experiment is described with the Single Cell Schema version 0.4 ( scrna-schema/ ) and linked to the public records of GEO, SRA, BioProject and figshare. The count data are not part of this repository; they are available from GEO and figshare. The experiment was published by Arigoni et al. (2024, Scientific Data 11:159, doi:10.1038/s41597-024-03002-y). Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Single Cell Omics Benchmark - FAIR Metadata

summary: Replication package for  Neuro-Symbolic Requirements Elicitation: Utilizing Formal Verification Counterexamples as Contextual Prompts  (ASE 2026). C-GRiD combines a Large Language Model (LLM) with the TLA+ model checker TLC. Counterexamples are translated into plain-language questions for stakeholders, whose answers guide the iterative refinement of formal specifications. Version 2.0.0 provides a new experimental evaluation of C-GRiD that replaces the evaluation of Version 1 , with an executable and reproducible evaluation pipeline. The results reported in this version supersede those of Version 1. In particular, Version 2 introduces the following enhancements: TLC-based verification:  All experimental verdicts are established using the TLC model checker (TLC2 2026.11.06, bundled with the package). Executable benchmarks:  The nine benchmarks are provided as executable TLA+ models with their corresponding TLC configuration files, while preserving the constraint identifiers used in Version 1. Behavioural recall assessment:  Recall is determined through TLC refinement checks, providing an executable basis for assessing whether the specified requirements are satisfied. Complete experimental traceability:  Every LLM interaction is recorded, allowing the reported results to be re-derived without requiring an API key through  replay.sh . Experimental Evaluation Version 2 reports a new experimental evaluation using two LLM configurations: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 , answering through a manual queue). Qwen3.6-27B (self-hosted server, temperature 0.3). The experimental setting comprises nine benchmarks, k = 3 and 5 removed constraints, five seeds, and 90 cases per approach and LLM. Strict Recall Results Approach Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B C-GRiD, perfect stakeholder 91.9% 89.6% C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder 85.4% 80.4% Gen-Once, full requirements 92.2% 59.1% Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden 83.3% 66.5% Auto-Repair (no LLM) 81.3% 81.3% Pairwise Comparisons C-GRiD with a perfect stakeholder compared with the other approaches (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test): C-GRiD vs. Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B Auto-Repair +10.6 pp, p = 0.0005 +8.3 pp, p = 0.020 C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder +6.5 pp, p = 0.003 +9.3 pp, p = 0.001 Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden +8.5 pp, p = 0.053 +23.1 pp, p < 0.001 Gen-Once, full requirements −0.4 pp, p = 0.59 +30.6 pp, p < 0.001 The evaluation shows that C-GRiD consistently outperforms Auto-Repair across both LLM configurations. Its comparison with one-shot generation also highlights the influence of the underlying LLM: C-GRiD achieves a substantial advantage with Qwen3.6-27B, whereas Claude Sonnet 5.5 achieves comparable strict recall when provided with the full requirements. These results provide further insight into the conditions under which counterexample-guided elicitation is beneficial. They supersede the results of Version 1 and are not directly comparable with them. They should be interpreted within the experimental setting and limitations documented in  RESULTS.md . Package Contents cgrid/ : C-GRiD implementation and experimental pipeline. benchmarks/ : Nine executable TLA+ benchmarks. results/ : Recorded experimental runs for both LLM configurations. legacy/ : Version 1 package, preserved for reference and comparison. Tests and supporting scripts: replay.sh : Re-derives the reported results from recorded LLM interactions, without requiring an API key. reproduce.sh : Runs new experiments using an LLM endpoint. Requirements:  Python ≥ 3.10 and Java ≥ 11. The package is intended to support independent inspection, replication, and further experimentation with counterexample-guided requirements elicitation.
