summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne

summary: Complete computational pipeline and outputs for the manuscript “Information limits of acoustic constraint on CO₂-mixture equations of state in the metering-critical window” (R. C. Aiken; prepared for Measurement Science and Technology). An earlier version of the manuscript was titled “Acoustically optimal state points for constraining CCS mixture models in the metering-critical region of CO₂ + N₂, O₂, and Ar”. Contents: candidate-grid Jacobians and input-derivative grids for CO₂ + N₂, O₂ and Ar (295–310 K, 7.4–11 MPa, 1–5 mol%); measurement designs with per-point precision requirements; projected covariances; replicate fit results; extracted literature comparison values; and the verified CO₂–Ar model implementation. The environment specification gives exact package versions and random seeds (CoolProp 8.0.0). New in version 1.2.0: Nested design sequences regenerated with a deterministic pair-search initialization. The 48-point designs are unchanged; the v1.1.0 sequences are retained as greedy_seq_v1_*.csv. Revision analyses (scripts/revision_*.py, outputs in out/revision/): dependence on composition uncertainty, comparison with conventional designs, batch structure, D/I/G criterion comparison, prediction uncertainty under parameter anchoring, density and bubble-pressure propagation, linearized out-of-family detection, and nonlinear coverage. README_REVISION.txt describes the additions and their run order.

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory selects a citation that agrees with its output. Comparing ten attribution methods on identical claims, the contrast between the model's distribution with and without context best separates provenance. Acting on that signal does not improve provenance honesty at these base rates. The resulting detector is hence still not accurate enough to act on: it measures what the model knew rather than what it used, and separating those remains the open problem.
title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary: This repository provides the Python implementations, numerical datasets, verification scripts, and supporting computational results associated with the manuscript “Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape Organized by Hypoxia–Immune–Matrix Feedback” . The study investigates nonlinear tumor–immune dynamics using a six-state mechanistic model coupling immunogenic and immune-escape tumor phenotypes, innate and adaptive immune responses, oxygen availability, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Particular attention is given to finite-amplitude oscillations arising through a subcritical Hopf bifurcation and a limit point of cycles (LPC), resulting in equilibrium–cycle bistability and perturbation-dependent transitions. Version 2 (v2) preserves the original numerical archive and extends the computational reproducibility materials with additional analyses and verification procedures developed during manuscript revision. The principal additions include: Generalized-Hopf analysis and investigation of reversible phenotype conversion. Ablation-specific Hopf and LPC calculations to assess the contributions of hypoxia-mediated conversion and immune-pressure feedback. Directional basin-threshold calculations and extended numerical integrations. Expanded parameter-sensitivity and robustness analyses. Additional shooting-based and adaptive-collocation verification of periodic solutions. Floquet stability screening of 252 periodic orbits, including a targeted assessment of potential period-doubling behavior. Updated bifurcation figures, numerical results, parameter provenance documentation, and reproducibility instructions.
title: Finite-Amplitude Tipping in Tumor Escape: Numerical Simulation Data, Bifurcation Analysis, and Computational Reproducibility

summary: What information about environmental memory must a quantum controller retain to guarantee a specified computational output? This preprint formulates that question in terms of task-sufficient process representations, intervention-valid predictions, stochastic clock laws, and explicit resource accounting. The central requirement is to preserve the outcomes and costs of the permitted decisions, with a stated accuracy contract and a finite-sample certificate. The paper connects two complementary lines of analysis. An operational construction studies Gaussian dephasing and controlled qubit tasks. A separate stochastic-clock analysis studies direct and inverse time changes, fractional relaxation, and the information that temporal coarse graining must transport. These constructions address related modelling questions but are not identified as a single microscopic noise model. The main elements are: Identical uncontrolled channels, different controlled responses. A continuum of Gaussian phase processes has the same uncontrolled coherence at every time and zero Breuer-Laine-Piilo backflow, yet different spin-echo responses. The construction shows why an uncontrolled channel family alone can fail to determine an intervention-dependent control decision. Task-sufficient equivalence and resource contracts. The manuscript defines a contract functional collecting accepted-output moments, acceptance probabilities, and physical costs over a declared policy family. Its finite linear task quotient identifies distinctions relevant to those predictions. Approximate sufficiency is accompanied by stability bounds that expose the sensitivity of conditional guarantees to low acceptance probabilities and small feasibility margins. Simultaneous finite-policy certification. Conservative confidence bounds certify conditional task bias and expected cost per accepted outcome after selection among a fixed, finite set of candidate policies. The assumptions include independent reset attempts, bounded observations and costs, and a trusted ideal reference. Failure to certify a candidate is explicitly distinguished from proof that no feasible physical policy exists. An explicit coarse-graining framework for stochastic clocks. The proposed decorated phase space records the process, permitted policy family, observable set, and clock law. The clock component transports stable laws under their natural scaling and relates domains of attraction to regular variation of waiting-time tails. Within the stated two-parameter clock-and-coupling family, the relaxation-rate direction scales with eigenvalue c^alpha. These clock results are placed in the established probabilistic renormalization literature; they do not establish hyperbolicity or convergence for the full decorated operator. A reset-sensitive fractional-relaxation calculation. Direct subordination of a quantum dynamical semigroup is distinguished from inverse-stable time change. For the latter, the paper compares uninterrupted evolution with independent renewal of the hidden clock and relevant environment. At half order and dimensionless rate one, the exact erfcx representation gives the short-time defect Delta(h) ~ 0.660989212585294 sqrt(h). The difference concerns the declared reset protocols, rather than a general assertion that every physical gate resets its environment. The reported classical benchmark uses ten candidate policies with explicit pulse depolarisation and separate X- and Z-expectation contracts. At the quasistatic endpoint, midpoint echo increases average identity-gate fidelity from 0.789293 to 0.990050. The fidelity crossover near r = 0.0467883 is distinct from the stricter X-task feasibility threshold r >= 0.9688074. For the selected Z-task input, dephasing is harmless and unnecessary echo pulses reduce the expectation. Conventional calibrated echo matches the best tested control performance; calibration, sampling, rejected attempts, and amortisation remain part of the resource account. Two q
title: Task-Sufficient Memory under Stochastic Clocks: Coarse-graining operators, fixed points, and finite-policy certification

No measure or class definition changed. v1.8.0 adds log entry R8, committed before its analyses ran, after earlier results were known: sensitivity of the grade analysis to misclassification of untraced text, equivalence tests, order of the echo and shared-source rules, agreement with retyped code, a label-noise ceiling for the human codes, a comparison with the LLM classifiers released with RelianceScope, post-test models with pre-activity covariates, numerical-Hessian standard errors for the censored models, and token-level five-class labels produced by the attribution of the 275 FLoRA proposals (CC BY 4.0). summary: This report and reproducibility package examine how a specified receiver determines which distinctions in a supplied nested quantum state become accessible in its measurement records. Two nonorthogonal states with unequal 70/30 population weights and opposite coherence have identical reduced states on every nonempty proper subset of their encoded registers. Measurements confined to those subsets cannot distinguish the candidates. Local equatorial measurements followed by comparison of their records reveal a joint parity contrast, whose accessibility depends on the receiver phase. For the worked two-register example, equal-prior single-trial discrimination succeeds with probability 95.83% under ideal retention and 79.33% with independent 80% retention at each receiver. These probabilities include incomplete records. Blind receiver settings and complete dephasing provide distinct zero-contrast controls. The report also establishes reconstruction from three real quantities within a known two-dimensional encoded subspace. A support-leakage counterexample demonstrates why this reconstruction does not extend to unrestricted states. All sixteen numerical check families pass, including 5,130 proper-subset comparisons. A verification run reproduces the archived scientific results exactly. The package includes the report, executable code, fixed configuration, numerical results, probability tables, figures, equation sources, report builder and checksums. This is an analytic and computational benchmark within declared quantum states and measurement models. It provides a bounded example of receiver-dependent information access and candidate-state identification; it does not constitute experimental validation or derive a physical mechanism of nesting.
title: Receiver Distinguishability of Nested States

summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

summary: Data belonging to the work "An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua" Using Lunaria annua , I manipulated resource availability via branch removal to test whether reduced competition induces compensatory funiculus thickening. I measured funiculus thickness and seed area in basal and apical fruits, analyzing seed fate and trait scaling relationships. Branch removal induced global funiculus hypertrophy, which was disproportionately higher in basal positions. Funiculus expansion was positively associated with seed survival and growth, though plants converted transport capacity into biomass more effectively in apical positions. Results also showed a decoupling of the within-fruit size–number trade-off, challenging classical inverse correlations.
tags: competition, plasticity, resource allocation, seed abortion, sub-individual variation.
title: An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua

Columns: year, period_covered, rank, lga, state, cases, source, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_state_by_year.csv` | Suspected cases and deaths for each state listed in the situation reports (33, 31 and 36 states). Columns include as_of, status, source_url. | | `data/ncdc_cholera_national_published.csv` | National totals at each reporting point: suspected and confirmed cases, deaths, CFR, states and LGAs affected, including the full-year 2024 figure (24,842 suspected cases) from the Weekly Epidemiological Report, vol. 14, no. 52. | | `data/state_input_data_populations_coordinates.csv` | Analysis input: 2006 census population, area, state centroid (mean of LGA coordinates), cases, listed flags. | | `data/lga_coordinates_and_zones.csv` | 774 LGAs with state, geopolitical zone and coordinates. Used only to compute state centroids. Contains no case counts. | | `code/state_analysis_v2.py` | State-level analyses (Moran's I, LISA, rank correlation, Bayesian BYM2 negative binomial models, posterior predictive checks, WAIC, NB regression) and Figures 3–4 inputs. | | `code/lga_extra.py` | Table of all listed LGAs and the random-selection overlap simulation (200,000 draws; fixed seed). | | `code/analysis_top_lgas.py` | Descriptive, concentration and overlap analysis of the published LGA lists. | | `code/maps.py` | State symbol maps (Figure 2). | | `results/` | All output tables and JSON. Prefix `state_` = state-level analyses; `lga_` = LGA-list analyses. | | `figures/` | PNG figures. | | `supplement/` | Supplementary File 1 (STROBE/RECORD checklist), 2 (search protocol and reference verification log), 3 (supplementary tables), and `Supplementary_Tables.xlsx`. | | `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` | SHA-256 checksum of every file. | ## 2. Key definitions and handling of data - **Suspected cholera:** cases as published by NCDC under its suspected-case definition; not laboratory-confirmed. - **Incidence:** reported suspected cases per 100,000 of the 2006 census population (reported, not true, incidence). - **2024:** epidemiological weeks 1–39 (10,837 suspected cases). The state and LGA tables for 2024 end at week 39. - **Unlisted states:** a state absent from an NCDC table is either unaffected or did not report; these cannot be distinguished. Primary analyses treat them as **missing**; sensitivity analyses treat them as zero. Enugu is listed in no year. - **LGA lists:** truncated, year-specific top-k lists; LGAs absent from a list are unobserved, not zero. Rows extracted from the tables differ from printed table totals by 26 (2022), 76 (2023) and 285 (2024) cases and were kept as extracted. - **State locations:** means of LGA centroid coordinates, as no boundary file was used. ## 3. summary: Replication package for  Neuro-Symbolic Requirements Elicitation: Utilizing Formal Verification Counterexamples as Contextual Prompts  (ASE 2026). C-GRiD combines a Large Language Model (LLM) with the TLA+ model checker TLC. Counterexamples are translated into plain-language questions for stakeholders, whose answers guide the iterative refinement of formal specifications. Version 2.0.0 provides a new experimental evaluation of C-GRiD that replaces the evaluation of Version 1 , with an executable and reproducible evaluation pipeline. The results reported in this version supersede those of Version 1. In particular, Version 2 introduces the following enhancements: TLC-based verification:  All experimental verdicts are established using the TLC model checker (TLC2 2026.11.06, bundled with the package). Executable benchmarks:  The nine benchmarks are provided as executable TLA+ models with their corresponding TLC configuration files, while preserving the constraint identifiers used in Version 1. Behavioural recall assessment:  Recall is determined through TLC refinement checks, providing an executable basis for assessing whether the specified requirements are satisfied. Complete experimental traceability:  Every LLM interaction is recorded, allowing the reported results to be re-derived without requiring an API key through  replay.sh . Experimental Evaluation Version 2 reports a new experimental evaluation using two LLM configurations: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 , answering through a manual queue). Qwen3.6-27B (self-hosted server, temperature 0.3). The experimental setting comprises nine benchmarks, k = 3 and 5 removed constraints, five seeds, and 90 cases per approach and LLM. Strict Recall Results Approach Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B C-GRiD, perfect stakeholder 91.9% 89.6% C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder 85.4% 80.4% Gen-Once, full requirements 92.2% 59.1% Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden 83.3% 66.5% Auto-Repair (no LLM) 81.3% 81.3% Pairwise Comparisons C-GRiD with a perfect stakeholder compared with the other approaches (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test): C-GRiD vs. Claude Sonnet 5.5 Qwen3.6-27B Auto-Repair +10.6 pp, p = 0.0005 +8.3 pp, p = 0.020 C-GRiD, noisy stakeholder +6.5 pp, p = 0.003 +9.3 pp, p = 0.001 Gen-Once, missing requirements hidden +8.5 pp, p = 0.053 +23.1 pp, p < 0.001 Gen-Once, full requirements −0.4 pp, p = 0.59 +30.6 pp, p < 0.001 The evaluation shows that C-GRiD consistently outperforms Auto-Repair across both LLM configurations. Its comparison with one-shot generation also highlights the influence of the underlying LLM: C-GRiD achieves a substantial advantage with Qwen3.6-27B, whereas Claude Sonnet 5.5 achieves comparable strict recall when provided with the full requirements. These results provide further insight into the conditions under which counterexample-guided elicitation is beneficial. They supersede the results of Version 1 and are not directly comparable with them. They should be interpreted within the experimental setting and limitations documented in  RESULTS.md . Package Contents cgrid/ : C-GRiD implementation and experimental pipeline. benchmarks/ : Nine executable TLA+ benchmarks. results/ : Recorded experimental runs for both LLM configurations. legacy/ : Version 1 package, preserved for reference and comparison. Tests and supporting scripts: replay.sh : Re-derives the reported results from recorded LLM interactions, without requiring an API key. reproduce.sh : Runs new experiments using an LLM endpoint. Requirements:  Python ≥ 3.10 and Java ≥ 11. The package is intended to support independent inspection, replication, and further experimentation with counterexample-guided requirements elicitation.
title: Counterexample-Guided Requirements Discovery

summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

THE OTHER SIDE OF THE 4D MATERIALS RESEARCH An inverse design begins with a wish: a material should bend to a specific shape after a particular sequence of heat, light, solvent or magnetic stimuli. The wish is not evidence. A specimen has a history, a printer has a feature limit, and a camera can mistake a smooth silhouette for recovered function. In this notebook the research chain is followed from physical permission to constitutive model, to competing computational designs, to damaged and rejected specimens, and finally to a negative case that another laboratory can recreate. Five independent flagships supply different scientific questions. F056 concerns a constrained inverse map from target response to material recipe. F057 studies the discrete matching of material configuration with time-dependent target shapes. F058 forces mathematical topology into a printable connected solid. F059 asks whether prediction intervals survive new lots and measurement chains. F060 refuses to consider a design validated until printed output, failures, material loss and costs have been measured. Coupling them yields a useful research system only when their evidence contracts remain distinct. The source genealogy matters. The author-provided four-dimensional microrobotics research book gives a physical vocabulary for responsive structures, fatigue and fabrication. The independent BCI-stroke study gives a separate rationale for minimizing assistance and distinguishing device function from recovery after a device is removed. The forty-family blueprint identifies the F056-F060 lineage and emphasizes the hazard of an optimum that cannot be manufactured. No source proves that a quantum-designed microbot has restored human motor function. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is the public name of the present research method. The first stage asks what material and laboratory can legitimately do. The second asks which mathematical program is meaningful. The third proposes a strong ordinary rival. The fourth tries hard, bounded counterexamples. The fifth freezes the evidence that can survive independent reconstruction. This is a set of epistemic viewpoints, not a claim about physical parallel universes. A strong scientific notebook should be able to disagree with the monograph. Where the monograph records an observable and a pre-registered test, the notebook should ask why the observable was chosen, what the test would miss, and which apparently trivial rival might explain its result. Repetition can be a conceptual return to a difficult distinction rather than duplicated filler. But no return should be mistaken for new measurement. The most important distinction is between speed of design and quality of evidence. More candidate samples, more attractive plots or more pages cannot establish physical printability. Nor can a verified specimen establish quantum computational advantage if the full pipeline costs and carefully tuned classical methods were never compared. A scientific stop is legitimate when the boundary and next decisive experiment are clear. Research Doors should remain the most alive part of this system. The question left at the end of each chapter is not an invitation to endorse the current model. It is an instruction to try to defeat it with a better observation. If the next laboratory discovers that a classical algorithm, a clamp motion or a material batch artifact explains the beautiful result, the research family has still preserved useful knowledge. The relevant physical endpoints are held-out curvature error [1/m], tip displacement [um] and batch yield [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a rich surrogate or uncounted classical preprocessing explains the optimization gain. A blinded test should blindly swap material lots and stimulus order after designs are frozen. A blinded test should conceal target shapes and reverse their temporal stimulus order. Independent instruments include three-axis shape field [um], synchronized stimulus onset [s], printed voxel map and decoded composition identity; the ordinary comparator set comprises strong integer programming, genetic search, Bayesian optimization and conventional discrete trajectory matching under identical material alphabets. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. The relevant physical endpoints are fabricated topology fidelity [1], stiffness [Pa] and actual curvature [1/m]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that simulation favors disconnected or sub-resolution ligaments that cannot print. A blinded test should blindly print held-out topologies with fixed voxel resolution and support rules. Independent instruments include volumetric z-stack [um], print line width [um], calibrated microforce [uN], FE mesh ledger and connected-component count; the ordinary comparator set comprises calibrated SIMP, compliant-mechanism topology optimization, integer programming and mesh-matched density methods. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that surrogate uncertainty is underdispersed or repeated specimens are treated as independent. A blinded test should blindly challenge unseen lots at changed humidity, exposure and measurement chains. Independent instruments include held-out batch curvature [1/m], interval coverage [1], calibration-camera uncertainty [um] and independent lot identifiers; the ordinary comparator set comprises validated Monte Carlo, hierarchical uncertainty propagation, conformal calibration and independent classical surrogate models. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence. F060 | Manufacturability and Experimental Validation of Quantum-Designed 4D Materials at the Limit This flagship examines closing the optimization-fabrication-test loop with hard defect and exposure vetoes. The relevant physical endpoints are print yield [1], metrology deviation [um], force drift [N] and full system cost. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a virtual optimum disappears when sacrificial structures, curing and failed prints are counted. A blinded test should preregister fabrication quotas and independently measure every successful and failed specimen. Independent instruments include full attempted print roster, geometry residual [um], released particle mass [ug], force after cycling [uN] and cost ledger; the ordinary comparator set comprises a tuned classical design-of-experiments pipeline, matched-printer fabrication quota, process-cost accounting and blind metrology. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a sequence across optimization, coding, topology, uncertainty and fabrication without importing one another's evidence.

summary: تقدم هذه الورقة البحثية التأسيسية إطاراً معرفياً-وجودياً جديداً لمعالجة أزمة "الفائض المعلوماتي" (Information Overload)، ليس بوصفها مجرد تحدٍ تقني أو نفسي، بل بوصفها أزمة بنيوية في "السياق" (Context) و"قواعد التحويل" (Transformation Rules). من خلال صهر وتطوير أربعة أطروحات متكاملة (نظرية السياقات، معلومات الانحراف السياقي CDI، نظرية المصنوعات، ونظرية الاجترار الثقافي)، تقترح الورقة "رياضيات جديدة للوعي الدلالي". أبرز مساهمات الورقة: إعادة تعريف الوعي: نعرّف الوعي صورياً بوصفه نظاماً بديهياً توليدياً (Axiomatic Generative System) تقاس كميته بالرتبة البرهانية (Proof-Theoretic Ordinal)، ونبرهن رياضياً أن الفائض المعلوماتي في غياب سياق تأويلي يؤدي إلى "العمى السياقي" (Contextual Blindness). ميكانيكا الانحراف: تقديم مقاييس رياضية دقيقة (CDI و SDI) للتمييز بين "المفاجأة الإحصائية" (نظرية شانون) و"الانحراف المعياري عن السياق"، ولقياس "الزيف الدلالي" في الرسائل الاتصالية (مثل هلوسات الذكاء الاصطناعي). ديناميكا المصنوعات: البرهنة على "مبرهنة الصعود الميتا-سياقي" (Meta-contextual Ascent)، التي تثبت كيف تُعيد المصنوعات الرقمية (مثل النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة) تشكيل وعي المستخدم، ليس سلوكياً فحسب، بل على مستوى البديهيات والمعتقدات. السيادة المعرفية: تعميم الإطار من الفرد إلى الحضارة عبر "نظرية الاجترار الثقافي"، وإثبات أن غزارة المحتوى (K) مع ثبات قواعد التحويل (T) تُنتج "فجوة سيادية" تنمو أسّياً وتؤدي إلى التبعية المعرفية. تُختتم الورقة بتقديم برنامج بحثي متكامل ومؤشرات قابلة للقياس لبناء "مناعة معرفية" تحمي الوعي البشري من التعديل التخريبي في عصر السياقات اللانهائية. هذه الورقة تمثل نقطة التقاء رائدة بين نظرية البرهان الرياضي، وفلسفة العقل، وعلم المعلومات، ودراسات الذكاء الاصطناعي.

summary: تقدم هذه الورقة البحثية التأسيسية إطاراً معرفياً-وجودياً جديداً لمعالجة أزمة "الفائض المعلوماتي" (Information Overload)، ليس بوصفها مجرد تحدٍ تقني أو نفسي، بل بوصفها أزمة بنيوية في "السياق" (Context) و"قواعد التحويل" (Transformation Rules). من خلال صهر وتطوير أربعة أطروحات متكاملة (نظرية السياقات، معلومات الانحراف السياقي CDI، نظرية المصنوعات، ونظرية الاجترار الثقافي)، تقترح الورقة "رياضيات جديدة للوعي الدلالي". أبرز مساهمات الورقة: إعادة تعريف الوعي: نعرّف الوعي صورياً بوصفه نظاماً بديهياً توليدياً (Axiomatic Generative System) تقاس كميته بالرتبة البرهانية (Proof-Theoretic Ordinal)، ونبرهن رياضياً أن الفائض المعلوماتي في غياب سياق تأويلي يؤدي إلى "العمى السياقي" (Contextual Blindness). ميكانيكا الانحراف: تقديم مقاييس رياضية دقيقة (CDI و SDI) للتمييز بين "المفاجأة الإحصائية" (نظرية شانون) و"الانحراف المعياري عن السياق"، ولقياس "الزيف الدلالي" في الرسائل الاتصالية (مثل هلوسات الذكاء الاصطناعي). ديناميكا المصنوعات: البرهنة على "مبرهنة الصعود الميتا-سياقي" (Meta-contextual Ascent)، التي تثبت كيف تُعيد المصنوعات الرقمية (مثل النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة) تشكيل وعي المستخدم، ليس سلوكياً فحسب، بل على مستوى البديهيات والمعتقدات. السيادة المعرفية: تعميم الإطار من الفرد إلى الحضارة عبر "نظرية الاجترار الثقافي"، وإثبات أن غزارة المحتوى (K) مع ثبات قواعد التحويل (T) تُنتج "فجوة سيادية" تنمو أسّياً وتؤدي إلى التبعية المعرفية. تُختتم الورقة بتقديم برنامج بحثي متكامل ومؤشرات قابلة للقياس لبناء "مناعة معرفية" تحمي الوعي البشري من التعديل التخريبي في عصر السياقات اللانهائية. هذه الورقة تمثل نقطة التقاء رائدة بين نظرية البرهان الرياضي، وفلسفة العقل، وعلم المعلومات، ودراسات الذكاء الاصطناعي.

QUANTUM OPTIMIZATION FOR REHABILITATION CONTROL AT THE LIMIT FAMILY 11 | F051-F055 | SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK A connected argument through 82 chapters: Mechanism / Measurement / Refutation Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI | White Rainbow Era | 2026 SCIENTIFIC STATUS: Prospective, nonclinical, falsifiable research architecture. No patient trial, tested quantum supremacy, demonstrated stroke recovery, or qualified medical device is claimed. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CONTROL MONOGRAPH The technical notebook is not a glossary pasted below the research monograph. It is a second argumentative surface. The monograph states exactly what can be tested, with candidate equations, independent measurements and research gates. The notebook asks why the experiment deserves construction, which competing explanation should be taken most seriously and how an unsuccessful first generation could become a stronger foundation for someone else. This difference is a methodological commitment rather than a claim of novel experimental results. Family eleven begins from an uncomfortable contrast between optimization and authority. A method may compute a more attractive control input, but no numerical attractiveness can authorize an illegal actuator command. The physical and ethical permission envelope must be defined outside the optimizer, and a safe fallback must remain available when the proposed method is late, uncertain, energy-depleted or dependent on inaccessible backend infrastructure. The most important output of a difficult trial may be an unambiguous refusal. The five flagship mechanisms form a causal chain without becoming duplicates. F051 asks what it means to optimize permitted control gains fairly. F052 places the optimizer inside the receding-horizon control clock. F053 asks whether progressively less assistance can maintain a fixed mechanical task, while refusing to equate phantom success with human recovery. F054 requires energy and latency to be counted across acquisition, computation, communication and actuation. F055 tests whether every scientific conclusion remains subordinate to command legality, independent vetoes and serious classical rivals. This lineage comes from two distinct source studies and the author-supplied STARLI forty-family research DNA blueprint. The four-dimensional microrobotics source supplies material history, force generation, responsive structures and safety concerns. The BCI-stroke atlas supplies intention observability, minimally necessary assistance, withdrawal and the crucial distinction between assisted motion and restored independent function. These source relationships are not evidence that a fused 4D, quantum, BCI and clinical treatment platform exists. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is a public name for a disciplined research workflow. Physical origin asks what the bench is permitted to do. Mathematical evolution asks which candidate model and parameters represent it. Counterfactual branching makes the ordinary baseline and hidden confounder genuine competitors. Extreme extrapolation applies bounded adversarial inputs, where the correct output may be stop. Evidence convergence leaves both a reconstructable result and an open Research Gate. These stages are viewpoints on one research contract, not literal physical parallel worlds. A 4D actuator can return to its familiar geometry and still lose force. A quantum optimizer can return a lower cost and still arrive after the legal deadline. A minimally assisted movement can succeed while a person would remain dependent on the device. A smooth average can hide a rare illegal command. Those four asymmetries explain why this research must separate shape, computation, mechanical assistance, function and safety, and why none of these outcomes can be imported into the others without a new experiment. The wisdom of stopping is the opposite of indifference. It means ending a research round when the testable contract is complete, the strongest rival has been confronted, the permission gates have been audited and the next laboratory can reconstruct the adverse case. When further parameter search no longer distinguishes the mechanism from the rival, additional polished prose or training calls do not create new evidence. The unresolved difference becomes an explicit research door for future investigators. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F051 | Quantum-Assisted Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Control Optimization at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is control gain search under hard actuator and state constraints. Its measurable endpoint is angle tracking error and total tuning-to-command cost. The leading alternative says benefit is produced by extra search, hidden preprocessing or the classical controller. The preregistered blind competition would blind-swap candidate gain vectors on identical nonhuman control traces. A fully observed test requires encoder angle [rad], actuator command, output torque [N m], motor work [J], gain-search calls and full wall time [ms] and resource-equivalent comparison with tuned robust PID/LQR, constrained SQP, CMA-ES and mixed-integer gain search with identical runs and CPU/GPU ledger. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F052 | Quantum-Assisted Model Predictive Control for Rehabilitation Robots at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is finite-horizon constrained optimization with receding-horizon deadlines. Its measurable endpoint is closed-loop error, solver completion percentile and deadline violation. The leading alternative says a solver-only benchmark ignores compilation, upload, readout and communication. The preregistered blind competition would conceal horizon changes and impose actuator-relevant controller deadlines. A fully observed test requires state estimator [rad,rad/s], solver input/output timestamp [ms], horizon [steps], safety margin and fallback event and resource-equivalent comparison with well-tuned conventional MPC, SQP, mixed-integer solvers, warm starts and robust tube MPC on identical task clocks. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F053 | Quantum Optimization for Minimum Necessary Assistance at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is assistance-minimizing policy with a fixed task-feasibility envelope. Its measurable endpoint is minimum delivered force and unassisted phantom-task feasibility. The leading alternative says a more forceful actuator makes the task look easier without reducing dependence. The preregistered blind competition would blindly taper physical assistance and test device-off task feasibility. A fully observed test requires independent load cell [N], motion target error [rad], assisted/unassisted phantom condition and residual passive force and resource-equivalent comparison with a fixed-gain assistive policy, optimal classical assistance scheduler and a fully disengaged zero-assistance phantom control. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F054 | Energy-Latency Tradeoffs in Quantum Rehabilitation Control at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is energy-constrained compute-actuation scheduling and deadline-aware fallback. Its measurable endpoint is joules per safe episode, wall latency and feasible trajectory fraction. The leading alternative says external service electricity or device idle consumption disappears from cost. The preregistered blind competition would inject finite battery, network stalls and safe-stop events in randomized order. A fully observed test requires electrical energy [J], power [W], battery state [J], acquisition and network timestamp [ms], safe-stop trace and resource-equivalent comparison with energy-aware classical MPC, local deterministic fallback and measured on-device scheduling with the same task energy budget. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F055 | Safety-Constrained Quantum Rehabilitation Control Against Classical Baselines at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is noncompensatory command legality with paired quantum-classical evaluation. Its measurable endpoint is illegal commands, veto timing, safety margin and matched-cost task error. The leading alternative says rare forbidden states are omitted while average performance improves. The preregistered blind competition would inject hidden infeasible states and verify fail-silent refusal before actuation. A fully observed test requires command legality indicator, independent hardware veto timestamp [ms], state margin, source version and paired baseline results and resource-equivalent comparison with independently certified physical interlock, robust classical MPC, rule-based veto and cost-matched quantum candidates. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question.

summary: Replication package for the paper "Percentile in Percentile: Evaluating Scholars Across Career Stages" (Ipeirotis & Tian, Quantitative Science Studies). Contents: the SQL that builds every table in the paper ( sql/ , numbered in run order); CSV exports of the 28 result tables those queries write, aggregates only ( results/ ); the data behind every figure and the plotting scripts ( figures/ ); the Lean 4 formal verification package ( lean/ ) and numerical checks ( checks/ ) of the score's properties; the curated Wikidata honors and the scripts of the later-recognition test ( honors/ ); the manuscript source ( manuscript_qss/ ); COMPUTATION.md , which explains how the SQL evaluates the integral that defines PiP; and FINDINGS.md , which records every number with the query that produced it. The per-author and per-article tables (about 312 GB, and 215 GB for the analysis without self-citations) are not in this archive. They are in the BigQuery datasets scholar-version2.paper_rp and scholar-version2.paper_rp_noself , which anyone signed in to Google Cloud can query; queries are billed to the reader's own project. Sources: Semantic Scholar Academic Graph, release 2026-10-27 (ODC-BY); Wikidata (CC0), queried 5 November 2026. summary: Many high-stakes AI failures trace to the training data rather than the model, yet teams still treat pre-training data validation as a checklist and rarely wire its signals to a go/no-go decision or to a governance framework. We study the detectability boundary of that validation: what a pre-training data-readiness gate catches, what it misses, and why a flagged source is often not blocked. We reuse a validation gate from a prior single-domain system and generalize it across three high-stakes domains (healthcare, finance, and government) on the real MIMIC-IV, SEC EDGAR, and CMS Open Payments datasets, injecting controlled defects across simulated sources. A composite readiness score detects 0.76 of degraded sources (95% CI [0.74, 0.76]) but withholds only 0.42; the 0.34 gap (95% CI [0.32, 0.35]) traces to a single averaging step, and we show it is fixable but privacy-sensitive. The grid is small by design (six sources per domain, two degraded, five seeds), so the intervals describe this controlled setting, not field variability. We map the privacy-utility curve of validating on differentially private summaries, prove a blind spot for symmetric label noise on balanced targets, and add a confident-learning label detector that runs on DP-noised summaries and keeps its recall down to epsilon = 0.1. We compare against Great Expectations and Deequ, measure how poorly thresholds port across domains, and map the gate to the NIST AI RMF MEASURE function. We report the negatives, among them a near-chance inter-rater reliability on fine-grained incident coding. What is new is the integration of production incidents, a private benchmarked gate, and a governance mapping, not any one of those parts.

summary: siwecal-soft v0.1.0 First release of siwecal-soft , the software of the SiW-ECAL TB2026 test-beam campaign at CERN: data conversion, simulation, reconstruction and analysis in one Key4hep/Gaudi project. Origin This repository merges two earlier repositories into a single code base with a fresh history: siwecal_k4sim @ 075dedd : simulation of the prototype. DD4hep geometry (including the H2-like upstream beam line), ddsim launchers, digitisation and the simulation campaigns. siwecal-tb2026 @ 90b2e55 : test-beam data. Raw/LCIO decoding, event building with the muon calibration, particle-ID shower variables, ACTS tracking, event viewer and analysis. An important part of the DAQ data decoding (SLB frame and raw decoders) and of the pedestal/MIP calibration is based on SiWECAL-TB-analysis , the SiW-ECAL test-beam analysis software. Both repositories are frozen at those commits (tag final-before-monorepo ); new development happens here. Every file of the two repositories is accounted for in tools/migration/ (copied, rewritten or excluded), and the merge was validated against the frozen builds (identical tracking output: 137/137 data and 144/144 simulation EDM4hep branches). What changed with the merge One CMake project (C++20, Key4hep 2026-04-08), one install, one environment script ( init_siwecalsoft.sh ). Shared code and mappings live once in common/ ; calibration tables are read from EOS only. Unified ACTS tracking for data and simulation. Processing steps formerly done in Python now run as Gaudi algorithms: ecal tree writer, occupancy-sag and trigger turn-on calibrators, and the post-PID event selection and valtree ( EcalEventSelection , EcalValTreeWriter ). Each was validated against the Python version. New: run-by-run simulation ( simulation/campaign/make_run_sim_dag.py ). One simulated sample per data run, with the gun tuned to that run's measured beam spot ( siwecal_beamspot ) and the run's statistics; used for final_v10. Control tests ( tests/control/ ) run with ./build.sh (ctest + pytest). Authors Jesus Pedro Marquez Hernandez (IJCLab), Olmo Arquero Peinazo (CIEMAT), Yukun Shi (LLR). See CITATION.cff for how to cite this software.

summary: 🧬 Streptococcus iniae SIKU01 — Genome, Comparative Genomics and Reverse Vaccinology Release: Manuscript v43 · 26 October 2026 Response to reviewers (peer-review round 1): RESPONSE_TO_REVIEWERS_v43 · 26 October 2026 📖 Overview This repository provides the genome assembly, comparative genomic datasets, analysis code, vaccine-candidate prioritization results, and supporting reproducibility resources for Streptococcus iniae strain SIKU01. Five S. iniae isolates (SIKU01–SIKU05) were obtained from diseased farmed Asian seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) in Thailand and sequenced using Illumina paired-end technology. The SIKU01 dataset was selected for complete genome assembly and annotation. The study integrates genome annotation, comparative genomics across 90 S. iniae isolates, pangenome and conservation analyses, antigen characterization, reverse vaccinology, and Quality-by-Design (QbD) approaches to prioritize candidates according to immunological and biomanufacturing criteria. 🔗 Public sequence records Resource Accession / link NCBI BioProject PRJNA933632 SIKU01 BioSample SAMN33244440 SIKU01 GenBank chromosome CP121692.1 GenBank assembly GCA_046581345.1 RefSeq assembly GCF_046581345.1 SIKU01 raw reads SRR23406918 Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.22128864 Zenodo all-versions citation 10.5281/zenodo.15264953 🧫 Raw sequencing datasets Five Illumina paired-end sequencing datasets were deposited under BioProject PRJNA933632. Isolate NCBI SRA accession SIKU01 SRR23406918 SIKU02 SRR23406921 SIKU03 SRR23406920 SIKU04 SRR23406919 SIKU05 SRR23406922 The public complete genome assembly and annotation correspond to SIKU01. The remaining four sequencing datasets are retained as raw sequencing records. 📦 Files included in this dataset 📝 Manuscript File Description 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.pdf Manuscript, PDF format 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.docx Editable Word manuscript 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43_corrected.md Markdown manuscript source, including six embedded figures 📊 Data workbooks Each workbook includes a CONTENTS sheet describing its tables and supporting metadata. File Contents Data_file_1.xlsx Biological and comparative-genomic datasets; 47 data worksheets, with source tables, dimensions and hashes Data_file_2.xlsx Prioritization rules, parameters, route definitions, sensitivity settings and test specifications; 8 data worksheets Data_file_3.xlsx Candidate-level outcomes, route-specific scores, leave-one-out and leave-one-component-out analyses, and final candidate summaries; 10 data worksheets 🧩 Analysis and reproducibility archives Archive Contents SIKU01_1_capsules.zip 19 analysis capsules containing code, intermediate tables, documentation and supporting inputs SIKU01_2_pipeline_ranking.zip Prioritization pipeline, frozen inputs, preflight, ranking, post-flight checks, tests and execution-stage documentation SIKU01_3_inputs_raw_and_frozen.zip Panaroo outputs, input genomes, hashes, core-gene MAFFT alignments and harmonized gene tables SIKU01_4_registry_layers_code_docs.zip Environment, scripts, verification utilities, analysis-to-code mappings, result registries, shared libraries, figure-generation code and manuscript files SIKU01_5_data_files_1_2_3_folders.zip Individual source tables underlying the three Excel workbooks SIKU01_6_figures_journal_450dpi.zip Six journal figures in PDF and PNG formats, with resolution information and a figure manifest The analysis capsules cover genome annotation, pangenomics, conservation, population lineages, recombination, plasmids, antimicrobial resistance, host similarity, protein surface architecture, physicochemical descriptors, epitope evidence, literature evidence and structural mapping. 🖼️ Figures The figure archive contains six journal figures in PNG and PDF formats, at 450 dpi or greater at 183 mm width. Its manifest distinguishes native-resolution images from enlarged outputs. 📽️ Scientific Presentation (PowerPoint) File Description SIKU01_7_Scientific_Presentation.pptx Editabl

Five S. iniae isolates (SIKU01–SIKU05) were obtained from diseased farmed Asian seabass ( Lates calcarifer ) in Thailand and sequenced using Illumina paired-end technology. The SIKU01 dataset was selected for complete genome assembly and annotation. The study integrates genome annotation, comparative genomics across 90 S. iniae isolates, pangenome and conservation analyses, antigen characterization, reverse vaccinology, and Quality-by-Design (QbD) approaches to prioritize candidates according to immunological and biomanufacturing criteria. 🔗 Public sequence records Resource Accession / link NCBI BioProject PRJNA933632 SIKU01 BioSample SAMN33244440 SIKU01 GenBank chromosome CP121692.1 GenBank assembly GCA_046581345.1 RefSeq assembly GCF_046581345.1 SIKU01 raw reads SRR23406918 Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.22128864 Zenodo all-versions citation 10.5281/zenodo.15264953 🧫 Raw sequencing datasets Five Illumina paired-end sequencing datasets were deposited under BioProject PRJNA933632. Isolate NCBI SRA accession SIKU01 SRR23406918 SIKU02 SRR23406921 SIKU03 SRR23406920 SIKU04 SRR23406919 SIKU05 SRR23406922 The public complete genome assembly and annotation correspond to SIKU01. The remaining four sequencing datasets are retained as raw sequencing records. 📦 Files included in this dataset 📝 Manuscript File Description 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.pdf Manuscript, PDF format 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43.docx Editable Word manuscript 01_Manuscript_RV_SI_v43_corrected.md Markdown manuscript source, including six embedded figures 📊 Data workbooks Each workbook includes a CONTENTS sheet describing its tables and supporting metadata. File Contents Data_file_1.xlsx Biological and comparative-genomic datasets; 47 data worksheets, with source tables, dimensions and hashes Data_file_2.xlsx Prioritization rules, parameters, route definitions, sensitivity settings and test specifications; 8 data worksheets Data_file_3.xlsx Candidate-level outcomes, route-specific scores, leave-one-out and leave-one-component-out analyses, and final candidate summaries; 10 data worksheets 🧩 Analysis and reproducibility archives Archive Contents SIKU01_1_capsules.zip 19 analysis capsules containing code, intermediate tables, documentation and supporting inputs SIKU01_2_pipeline_ranking.zip Prioritization pipeline, frozen inputs, preflight, ranking, post-flight checks, tests and execution-stage documentation SIKU01_3_inputs_raw_and_frozen.zip Panaroo outputs, input genomes, hashes, core-gene MAFFT alignments and harmonized gene tables SIKU01_4_registry_layers_code_docs.zip Environment, scripts, verification utilities, analysis-to-code mappings, result registries, shared libraries, figure-generation code and manuscript files SIKU01_5_data_files_1_2_3_folders.zip Individual source tables underlying the three Excel workbooks SIKU01_6_figures_journal_450dpi.zip Six journal figures in PDF and PNG formats, with resolution information and a figure manifest The analysis capsules cover genome annotation, pangenomics, conservation, population lineages, recombination, plasmids, antimicrobial resistance, host similarity, protein surface architecture, physicochemical descriptors, epitope evidence, literature evidence and structural mapping. 🖼️ Figures The figure archive contains six journal figures in PNG and PDF formats, at 450 dpi or greater at 183 mm width. Its manifest distinguishes native-resolution images from enlarged outputs. 📽️ Scientific Presentation (PowerPoint) File Description SIKU01_7_Scientific_Presentation.pptx Editabl

summary: Split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) compression data for 22 AISI 316 stainless steel specimens: raw bar signals, processed 1-wave / 3-wave stress-strain series, and the specimen and test records (RDF/Turtle, QUDT units, W3C PROV. From these tests: Johnson-Cook and Zerilli-Armstrong calibrations by least-squares fit and by a physics-informed neural network (PINN) - 78 single-seed runs and 8 seed ensembles, with parameter cards, uncertainties, identifiability diagnostics, training logs, predicted stress surfaces and checkpoints - and 308 LS-DYNA simulations of the tests driven by the calibrated models. See README.md for the layout and data_dictionary.csv for every term and column.
title: SS316L dynamic compression: SHPB tests, LS-DYNA simulations and physics-informed constitutive calibrations

summary: Observed Palworld stat values support the Palworld IV formula and its modifiers: a binary32 passive percent round trip, food-rate corrections, hunger, party bonuses that replace specific Attack Up and Defense Up passives, emblem bonuses, partner star ladders, linear helper contributions and maximum-only same-species source stacking. This dataset accompanies Lore Armory's v3.1 technical note. The full CSV contains 2,594 checked values, including 272 older contextual rows outside the note's 2,322-value denominator; 194 of the note's values are screenshot-backed readings from worlds L and L3. Frozen numerical predictions, competing alternatives and later eligibility corrections are kept distinct, and public mathematical copies of the frozen prediction sheets carry their own checksums, separate from the original commitments (the superseded J v1 sheet stays marked as such). Screenshot references and hashes accompany the readback ledger. The README supplies column definitions, exact count filters, observation provenance and open questions. The archive iv-data-v3.1.tar.gz holds the full data directory with its folder structure. The package does not claim confirmation of enhancement statuses, combat-only conditional effects or tower-boss HP scaling.

summary: This record contains supplementary research materials supporting the manuscript entitled "Evaluating Out-of-Fold Weighted Soft Voting for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefits and Limitations of Classifier Fusion" (Manuscript ID: MJCSC-D-26-00018R3), submitted to the Mesopotamian Journal of Computer Science. The study evaluates training-derived optimized weighted soft voting for multiclass network intrusion detection using Decision Tree (DT-Gini), Random Forest variants (RF-Gini and RF-Entropy), and XGBoost. The primary evaluation uses a prepared CICIDS2017 development subset comprising 78,437 observations and 15 traffic classes. An additional dataset-specific evaluation uses a prepared CICIoT2023 subset comprising 99,327 observations, 34 traffic classes, and 39 numerical predictors. The experimental framework includes data preprocessing, mutual information-based feature selection, training-only minority-class oversampling, stratified outer cross-validation, and inner out-of-fold optimization of classifier fusion weights. The supplementary materials are intended to support verification of the reported experimental configurations and results. The original complete source-scanning log and sampling-run metadata for CICIoT2023 are unavailable; therefore, exact independent reconstruction of the original sampling run has not been established. These materials accompany the third-round revised manuscript submitted to the journal.
tags: Network Intrusion Detection; CICIDS2017; CICIoT2023; XGBoost; Weighted Soft Voting; Machine Learning; Reproducibility

The study evaluates training-derived optimized weighted soft voting for multiclass network intrusion detection using Decision Tree (DT-Gini), Random Forest variants (RF-Gini and RF-Entropy), and XGBoost. The primary evaluation uses a prepared CICIDS2017 development subset comprising 78,437 observations and 15 traffic classes. An additional dataset-specific evaluation uses a prepared CICIoT2023 subset comprising 99,327 observations, 34 traffic classes, and 39 numerical predictors. The experimental framework includes data preprocessing, mutual information-based feature selection, training-only minority-class oversampling, stratified outer cross-validation, and inner out-of-fold optimization of classifier fusion weights. The supplementary materials are intended to support verification of the reported experimental configurations and results. The original complete source-scanning log and sampling-run metadata for CICIoT2023 are unavailable; therefore, exact independent reconstruction of the original sampling run has not been established. These materials accompany the third-round revised manuscript submitted to the journal.
